review_text:
The newest restaurant you need to try is from the team behind Milk & Cream Cereal Bar, which is just a few blocks away in Chinatown, where the owners are also from and drawing inspiration for this great new spot.

They are making some amazing takes on classic Chinese dishes in a fun spot with great hip hop music playing non-stop.

Definitely start with Potstickers ($11) and a very unique Endive Salad ($15) with dragonfruit and pistachios. The XO Fried Rice ($18) is also a must, as is the Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles ($16) and Braised Short Ribs ($32). For dessert, make sure you try the Almond Cookie Soft Serve.

They are currently in soft open mode with dinner only Thursday - Sunday, but I'm looking forward to returning to try everything.

So cute inside! Staff was really nice. I like that the menu is small. I tried the potstickers (amazing) salty, savory, spicy, overall great. Had the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles which were pretty good. Mushrooms were tasty. And had the spicy eggplant side which was delicious. Cant wait to come back and try more!!! Theyre doing a soft launch. So only open thursday through sunday for dinner

Came here to try this place for dinner after learning about their soft opening through a friend and wasn't disappointed!

Came at 6:50PM on a Friday and got seated. The inside is a huge nostalgia for late 90s/early 2000s Hong Kong comedy cinema. This place was described to me as a modern take on Chinese favorites and it rang true.

We looked at the menu and decided (after some deliberation) the endive salad, salt and paper chicken, Berkshire potstickers and the soy braised ribs.

Salad came out first, and visually it looked very fresh and refreshing. The fruits (dragonfruit, oranges and others) were very fresh and sweet. This made a good contrast with the veggies and some nuts on it that just freshened your up on a hot day.

The pot stickers were a nice touch. They were quite tasty itself with juicy meat on the inside but paired especially well with the chili oil it comes with.

The salt and pepper chicken was the main here that really shined. The scallion biscuits was an interesting touch and well appreciated. The chicken was fried greatly. Skin was crispy but not to the point where you just get a mouthful of batter. The meat was incredibly juicy and flavorful, and it went well with the house made jam they provided. 

The short ribs. Wow. Meat was incredibly tender and basically just tore off. Well braised gave it loads of flavor and the portion size was amazing.

For dessert, we had to get the pineapple soft serve with pineapple crumbs. Fantastic way to head dinner. The soft serve's sweetness paired perfectly well with the slight saltiness of the pineapple bun crumbs. Would return to try all the other amazing dishes on the menu!

Delicious new spot in Chinatown! Came here for dinner with friends and every dish was amazing. Favorites were the endive salad, chicken with ginger scallion sauce, rice rolls with hangar steak and tiger prawns (we even got another order of it because it was just that good). To top it off, we had the pineapple dole whip soft serve with the pineapple bun crumbles. It even came with fortune cookies which was a nice touch! The ambiance and decor is reminiscent of Hong Kong and featured nostalgic elements like classic Asian movie posters and childhood snacks. Would definitely recommend!
POTLUCK is amazing ... the best vibes, the best atmosphere, the best salads, the best chicken.. can't complain. EAT EAT EAT for lunch and dinner.

Food: 10/10
Service 10/10
Vibes: 10/10

As soon as you walk through the doors, a wave of nostalgia with a modern twist puts you in its sweet embrace. The fun, hip decor is perfectly done and the restaurant is clean and spacious. 

We dined as a party of 6 and followed our server, Kim's spot-on recommendations--she is the loveliest host (and so are the whole team!) We ordered: all three starters currently on the menu, which consisted of two refreshing salads (yay, shout out to my jellyfish fans) and plump, meaty potstickers--we thoroughly enjoyed them. For our mains, we shared two orders of the fried chicken & biscuits--the chicken was seasoned well, the sauce had a tang and a kick (but not too spicy - fear not my spice-averse, friends) and the biscuits were well executed (flaky and buttery), two orders of the rice rolls with stir fried beef (the noodles were the perfect QQ texture, get in my belly!), shrimp (a new take on the classic Cantonese favorite) which had a nice crunch and a mildly sweet flavor with creamy goodness, the fried rice (each grain of rice was perfectly coated and the pork had a good chew for a fun play of textures in each spoonful), the short ribs (flavorful and tender) and the eggplant (don't sleep on this dish if you're an eggplant fan, or if you're not, it might convert you). Family-style is the way to go! Sharing is caring, betches.

To end the evening, we had the Dole whip-inspired dessert. A nice, refreshing way to end a perfect meal. Hats off to Chef Zhan and Peter for modernizing and putting their own spin on some familiar flavors.  All the staff welcome you and make you feel like family. We can't wait to go back!

Popped into this new restaurant in the Chinatown/Lower East Side area during their soft opening. Love the movie theater decor theme, filled with nostalgic movie references from my childhood. 

The mocktails were very good, with the Old Man Chiu being especially refreshing, and The Landlady having a very interesting flavor mixture with strawberry and plum. 

Tried almost every dish with my group, and found everything to be delicious. Particularly enjoyed the Endive Salad which beautifully combines blood oranges, dragonfruit, and pistachio crumbs. My personal favorite entree was the Rice Rolls with Hangar Steak. Though among the table, most people's favorite was the salt and pepper chicken which comes with delectable scallion-flavored biscuits and a very tasty jam. Honestly, you can't go wrong with any of the offerings. 

Ended the meal with the only dessert option, Pineapple Soft Serve. Nice and refreshing after the meal, and the bolo boa (pineapple bun) crumble was a very thoughtful addition.

For a soft opening, the team has found their wonderful flavor profile and able to share a great experience into the lives of those who served the plates. The fun and whimsical interpretation of modern Cantonese cuisine with soul. This is not your traditional Cantonese dishes, it is the elevated next generation of taste. The enthusiasts' vision of what was to what is to come.

Came to Potluck Club on a Thursday night during soft opening. Right away I took notice and appreciated the modern sleek decor with Chinese and Asian American themes mixed in. They really pay attention to the little details around the restaurants such as Chinese films playing on mini TVs on the wall, Chinese vending machine that displayed popular drinks that dispenses fortune cookies and Asian American art on the walls. They even had a funny Easter egg by the bathroom which was a fun surprise. It just felt like a high end restaurant with a casual laid back vibe. We had a group of four so we were able to order mostly everything. The food was Cantonese cuisine mixed with an American flair. Everything was cooked perfectly in terms of texture and flavors. My favorites were the fried chicken with homemade scallion biscuits and the rice roll with steak and mushrooms which tasted like beef chow fun with a bite. The dessert ended with a pineapple soft serve with a pineapple bun crumble which was fun and paid homage to popular Chinese bun. The staff was very welcoming, attentive and friendly. Can't wait to come back to see what additions they add to the menu and get more scallion biscuits!
Amazing food. The fried chicken and biscuits were the most crispy and delicious chicken I ever had.  Definitely will be back in the near future

Potluck club was founded by native Chinese/Asian -American New Yorkers and is the perfect marriage between traditional Cantonese style dishes with modern flavors. We got the jelly fish tiger salad as an app, which was one of my faves -- very refreshing with some tanginess. So necessary and refreshing on a hot summer day . Potstickers were very meaty and flavorful with a bit of spice (but not too spicy if you're unable to handle spice like me). Chicken was juicy as well with hints of Chinese wine (haha get it? -- DRUNKen chicken). Mushroom and rice roll dish was bomb. Really enjoyed the texture and flavors altogether. Finally the pineapple ice cream was the perfect sweet and tangy finisher as the dessert. Service was great and attentive as well!

I forgot to take pics of the interior, but love the decor. There's a bunch of old Chinese film relics and animated photos (think: kung fu hustle, wong kar wai, Stephen chow movies), so if you're ABC or Chinese American and grew up watching Chinese movies, it'll take you through nostalgia lane 

Def try this place out!

From the team of the popular Milk & Cream Cereal Bar comes a new restaurant: Potluck Club. This is a Cantonese-American restaurant in Chinatown that is one of a kind, a must try. It's just 1 block from the B/D Grand St station, and the decor, food, and service are truly stunning.

We ordered pretty much the whole menu haha but standout dishes are:
- Endive Salad with Dragonfruit 
- Salt & Pepper Chicken + Scallion Biscuits + Chili Plum Jam 
- Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles 
- XO Fried Rice 
- Braised Short Rib
- Tiger Shrimp + Walnuts
- Drink: Old Man Chiu & The Landlady (non-alc)
- Pineapple Soft Serve

We paid about $225 + tax and tip for 7 people, and we left very happy and full. I can't recommend this place enough.

Tip: Book a table on Resy & look for the secret astronaut & two thumbs up Jackie Chan! There are fortune cookies to grab in the vending machine too. Enjoy!

TL;DR - Vibe, service, and food are excellent. Worth the trip.

Vibe - You walk in with a wall playing Hong Kong film classics with some newer films added in. Music was consistently hip-hop, which is an automatic 5/5 stars. 

Service - Front staff incredibly attentive to needs of the table. Drinks, food, and water came promptly on a busy night. They were friendly too, which makes all the difference. 

Food - Family style so you gotta share with your folks. Classic Chinese dishes with a twist and everything we ordered were absolute bangers. Jellyfish salad? Banger. Salt pepper chicken with biscuit? Banger. Rice rolls? Banger. Shrimp? Banger. Beef? Banger. Our absolute favorite for the table was the eggplant. We finished the first one too quickly and we needed an extra. Legit, don't sleep on it just because it's not a meat. 

Drinks - At time of review, had beer and wine. We stuck with the beers and seltzer because that was the vibe. The beer selection was banging. If you want something a little sweeter, the Lychee drink is good. Easily slammed two of these down before I moved onto beer. 

They can expect me here again when I return to NYC.

great food with great atmosphere! they did a great job with representing our traditional cantonese style dishes with a flare of modern techniques and flavor! 

FOOD: 4.5/5
food was very solid! i took off .5 a point only because it was a tad bit too salty for my palette. but that's just my own taste buds of course. must get items: salt & pepper chicken w/ scallion biscuit, oyster mushroom rice roll ADD the hangar steak (nomnom), tiger shrimp, braised short rib with kabocha squash and the spicy eggplant. everything was super well flavored, hit different flavor palette, and just cooked so well. each dish came out HOT which i personally love! ended it off with a pineapple soft serve with pineapple bun topping - chefs kiss! 

SERVICE: 5/5 
everyone was super welcoming, very attentive and had such great service! everything was done with a smile and very patient with our large group of 10 (: 

AMBIANCE: 5/5
reminds me of hong kong, played with nostalgia of growing up american born chinese. music was on point lol, everything was clean and just decor was amazing 

overall will for sure be back!

I don't really write reviews but I couldn't go without writing one for this new restaurant down the block from me! highly recommend the walnut shrimp and drunken chicken dishes!!! excellent customer service and don't forget to grab a free fortune cookie before you leave!!!

Heard about Potluck Club recently opening from a friend, and the backstory really interested me! I love how much thought was put into the decor and menu, as well as the inspiration of growing up in Chinatown. We came on a Sunday night with a reservation, and it wasn't packed but still fairly busy.

Endive Salad: a refreshing salad, with bitter greens balanced by a poppyseed-like dressing and fresh fruit. I really enjoyed the addition of dragonfruit!

Salt & Pepper Chicken w/ Scallion Biscuits: crispy dark meat with delicious biscuits and such an inventive chili-plum jam. The jam was unlike anything I've ever had and really took you on a journey! Would definitely recommend ordering.

Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles: like beef chow fun, but elevated! We added the hangar steak which was a great choice. This is one of the more unassuming dishes on the menu, but probably my favorite!

Spicy Eggplant: a pretty typical dish at any Chinese restaurant, so it didn't feel that worth it. Wasn't spicy at all and somewhat lacking in flavor, imo.

Pineapple Pineapple Soft Serve: sweet and refreshing! I wish there were more of the pineapple bun aspect, but I still enjoyed it.

All in all, the food, service, and ambiance was great. I felt like some prices leaned high and not all of the dishes blew me away, but the ambiance and concept make it a five star! Would recommend checking it out!

Great indoor ambience and delectable items in their menu. One thing I would advise for customers is to make a reservation. They will accommodate walk-ins but I feel wait time will be longer in the future. I look forward to dining here again.

Modern trendy looking restaurant. Food was unique and very delicious. I came with my friend and we both enjoyed it very much. 

My favorite dish was the salt and pepper chicken, the chicken was amazing, but the best part about this dish were the scallion biscuits it came with. Boy, these scallion biscuits blew my mind!!! What a unique take on scallion pancakes. I would have never thought of something like that. 

We also had the riceroll noodles, I went with the option to add hanger steak and it was worth it. The steak was made well and went so well with the noodles. Im drooling thinking about it.

I also really liked the drink selection. They had Young Master beer imported from Hong Kong. Being a beer guy, this was a treat to be able to try this.

Cant wait to come back with a group so i can try their other dishes.

We've seen a lot of modern-Chinese / Asian American restaurants (or "jook sing businesses" as I like to describe it to my parents) open up in the last several years and I have to say this one is one of my favorites. Yes the food was delicious but I'm obsessed with the ambiance/vibes/decor/brand, the story, and wonderful service. I'll definitely be back... often.

There weren't any reservations available for last Friday night but my bf and I decided to try walking in a little after 8pm (after the dinner rush) and thankfully they had an open table - it worked out perfectly! As others have mentioned, I was instantly captivated by the neon sign, HK movie posters, etc. Aesthetically everything about the restaurant screamed ABC and my personal self-identity so of course I was obsessed. In love. Everyone from the hostess, server and busboy were super friendly which added to its greatness. 

As for the food, my favorite had to be the oyster mushroom rice rolls w hanger steak ($25) - a classic but slightly elevated. So delicious. The drunken chicken w shrimp chips ($28) was soo tender and the scallion sauce was perfection. My bf insisted on also getting the 14 oz bone-in cha siu porkchop ($35) which is an off-menu special that I thought was just ok - very meaty but a bit dry. Next time I'm getting the shrimp dish instead. Their cocktails also looked good but we skipped alcohol this time around. 

Highly recommend this gem (esp to my fellow Asian Americans) yet I selfishly hope it doesn't get overhyped. Immaculate vibes; a great spot to chill and grab dinner with friends.

Food was great! Atmosphere was even better! 
Hong Kong style restaurant with 90s hip hop playing! 

They have Hong Kong beer which is such a treat. We ordered doubles of the fried chicken and biscuits. Moist chicken all around and would definitely come back for more! Great introduction to Chinese food!

I was super excited about this restaurant when I heard about the opening - and let me tell you, it did not disappoint!! 

I love how flavorful all of the dishes are and they are all shareable plates like a traditional chinese meal. 

Some of my favorite dishes were the endive salad (superrr refreshing and crunchy), the jellyfish tiger salad (basically the 2 things i love), the rice roll noodles (a traditional cantonese style dish but the char on the rice roll gives it a really nice smoky taste), and the salt&pepper chicken (obsessed with the sauce it comes with).

Was recommended this place from my friend and decided to try it out. Glad I did! You're welcomed by the classic canto movie decor and nostalgia vending machine. 

For food 5/5
We ordered the endive salad (super refreshing and well balanced), tiger shrimp and walnuts (one of my favorites. The shrimps are huge), oyster mushroom rice roll (tastes like classic beef chow fun. Another favorite), salt pepper chicken with scallion biscuits (super tender chicken and perfectly fried), braised short rib (also super tender and recommend with a bowl of white rice) and ended our meal with pineapple dole whip. I would definitely come back for the food. 

For drinks 4/5
I got the old man chiu (a bit sweet) and my friend ordered the land lady (recommend if you like salted plum)

For service 5/5 
They continuously checked on us and asked if there was anything we needed even though the restaurant was packed!

We made a resy here for 7:15 pm on a Friday night! The place was full, but didn't feel super packed. We could tell that they were a touch understaffed. 

We each got an alcoholic Asian inspired seltzer drink and some water for the table. They were not particularly good at clearing the tables of empty cans and cups. 

We got the jellyfish salad and endive salad to start. They were both very fresh. I think we sat by two tables who may have been friends with the owner because their serving portions were much larger! We didn't need more food, but it made us question if we got the short end of the stick. But I think we rightfully concluded that they were friends of the owners. 

The fried chicken dish was amazing but the biscuits were just ok. One friend pointed out that if the dish came with 5 pieces of fried chicken, they shouldn't just give you two biscuits and ask you to pay 3 dollars more per biscuit. The jam was good. 

I really liked the XO fried rice and the rice rolls! But my other two friends didn't think it was anything special. They also weren't impressed with the vegetable dish as well. They rated this place a 3/5 while my other friend and I agreed with the 4/5. Lastly, we had the braised short ribs that came with Japanese squash. We all found the ribs to be delicious, but a touch salty. 

I think two out four of us would come again but the other two would not.

Great ambiance and food! It's such a nostalgic place. Gave me such great memories of my childhood and family roots from Hong Kong,  especially the decor. The food had an American  twist on your classic chinese restaurant dishes. Definitely recommend coming here with childhood friends and reminisce chinatown chinese food and pop culture. I can't wait to go again!

One of the top NYC  openings this year! It took a while to make a reservation, but it was well worth the wait!

Our table ordered every dish on the menu and it was hit after hit! You can tell chef brings lots of creativity and passion to curating the menu since every dish brings something special and unique. 

Potluck serves up equal parts deliciousness & top-notch hospitality and you can feel the good vibes from the moment you enter the establishment.

You can tell the folks in charge are real professionals and care about making sure everyone has a great experience. 

Lookin forward to visiting again soon!

One of the best new restaurants I've been to on my most recent trip back to the city!  I was excited to try this with my group of friends and with this group we were able to sample almost everything on the menu, and boy oh boy it was delicious!

First the decor of the restaurant made me feel at home and seen.  The different movie posters, old theater vibes, the giant mural of the 2 kids from those old Cantonese movies added a touch of nostalgia from my childhood that made my inner child smile.  Even the vending machine made me feel like I was stepping into a time machine.

The food - Fire!!  Everything we ate was great and my compliments to the chefs - Peter and Zhan - but the absolute stars of the night: 

Salt and Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits - the chili-plum jam that came with this, if they bottled and sold it - I'd have left with two!  Ridiculously good!

Oyster Mushroom Rice Noodle Roll with hanger steak - this is the dish I'll be coming back for over and over and over again.  I loved this dish and it's something similar to what we grew up with and taken to the next level!

Braised Short Rib - When it hit my mouth...I could see my childhood, something my grandma prepared for special occasions - I was super impressed with this one.  

The pineapple soft serve at the end was a delicious touch that cooled and refreshed the pallet after the meal.

Yeah if you can get your friends over here for this one, head over as soon as possible.

Really great modern take on Asian food. 
We came during dinner time and didn't have reservations. They were fully booked for the night. I would recommend making reservations if you want to sit at a table. The kind hostess was able to sit all 5 of us at the bar. 

Drinks: the strawberry and salted plum drink was pretty good. They also have a good collection of different beers to try also. 

Food: We got a couple of the main entrees to try. 
-Braised Short Ribs
-Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles add steak
-XO fried rice
-Crispy Drunken Chicken W/ Shrimp Chips

The main stars of the meal were the rice roll noodles and the braised short ribs. These entrees were amazing. The noodles were what I've been craving and the flavor of this dish was a 10/10, we liked it much so that we had to get some to-go. The braised short ribs were super tender and delicious. 

The only thing I would say is the price vs portions.
Portions for the rice and noodles were pretty small for the price. 

Dole Whip dessert: pretty similar to the actual one in Hawaii. Great flavors and mixture of textures. 

Service: everyone was very nice and came to check in a couple times. 

Would def recommend going here and will be back for those noodles.

Came here on a busy Friday night and everything was PERFECT! We had a reservation and they seated us right away. I didn't think they would honor my seat time because busy NY restaurants almost never do, so they had me at hello (literally).

Ambiance is 10/10, Food is 10/10, and service 10/10! 
The food was so good. I came in with no expectations because I grew up eating Cantonese food but this was all with a twist of the new. We started off with a tasty endive salad, moved on to the salt and pepper fried chicken which was so crispy and perfect with jam and biscuit. We also go the rice rolls which was my personal favorite, the rice rolls were soft and silky with the perfect touch of WOK HEI (translated into English means 'wok thermal radiation' or, metaphorically, the 'breath of the wok'). Incoming we're the pea sprouts, and XO Fried rice which was also delicious. 

10/10 would recommend!! It's a cute date night spot too!

Came by with a group of 10. We ordered off their prix fixie menu (good amount of options) which I was so grateful for cause it portioned everything so there was plenty for everyone to try! Some of my favorites:

Endive salad - had dragonfruit, blood oranges and pistachios with a light dressing that went perfectly with it. Forget Sweetgreens, I want this for lunch everyday!!

S&P chicken with scallion biscuits - this dish was good on its own but it also came with this crack sauce jam that I wanted to literally put on everrrrything 

Oyster mushroom rice roll - this was by far my favorite!! Don't sleep on adding the hanger steak, it added more depth to the dish!

Braised short ribs - fall of the bone, melt in your mouth good!

Pineapple soft serve - perfect way to end the meal and read your fortune 

Ambiance and service was 

10/10 can't wait to come back!!

W.O.W. It took me some time to gather my thoughts before writing this review. So happy that this side of LES / Chinatown finally has a worthy restaurant. Once you walk in, you will notice all the thoughtfulness, creativity, and energy that the owners have put into this restaurant. As a Hong Kong immigrant, this restaurant brought back all the memories and culture of an 80s - 90s Hong Kong (and those that remind you of it). 

At 6pm on A Friday, it was already A Full house! (RESERVATIONS HIGHLY RECOMMENDED). I had opted for a seat at the kitchen bar, where I get to see the chefs in action. Very energetic crew, everything was MADE TO ORDER.

started off with some craft beers from Hong Kong. Neon City and Jade Scorpion. Neon City is flavorful, citrus-y, and perfect for the summer. The Jade Scorpion has hints of GREEN PEPPERCORN (Yes you read that right) , it's unique and super refreshing - and no, not spicy.
Had the jellyfish salad and the endive salad as appetizers. The Jellyfish salad is a modern twist to a classic Cantonese banquet dish, where the endive salad is a whole new modern creation with Asian influences. If I had to choose, go with the endive!

Entrees:
We had shared the drunken fried chicken, cha siew bone in thick cut porkchop (limited time special), and stir fried rice noodle (churng fun).
Everything was top notch, but what I really loved were the drunken fried chicken - hints of Chinese wine marinated right into the meat and even the bones - then flash fried to get a texture like a Garlic Chicken dish.
And,
The stir fried rice noodles with hanger steak - what a creation. Perfect wok hei (heat from stir frying) to accompany such a simple but flavorful dish.

Note to the owners: can you PLEASE start selling the crispy chili oil, and the green scallion sauces?!? I could literally eat a bowl of rice just by these sauces alone.

Conclusion: I will definitely be back. I wish nothing but the best for Potluck Club. Hopefully you guys will continue to churn out nice flavorful modern dishes with the HK influence!

Ps- DESSERT: dole pineapple ice cream with pineapple bun crumbs?! WHAT?!

Dinner for five opening week night. Ordered one of everything on the menu. Absolutely amazing variety of flavors and creativity. 

Staff was great. Service was quick. 

Packed house everyone stayed past closing... poor staff. 

Rice rolls with oyster sauce and hanger steak was my favorite. Someone else at the table really loved the chicken. The xo fried rice was also up there for everyone. Honorable mention... those short ribs were so good.

Went the day they just got their liquor license so they haven't set up the bar yet, gotta go back. So many good options posted on social media.

A/C too strong...

This is not only a restaurant, it's a magic land. It teleported me back to my childhood and reminded me of the rich culture that I came from. It feels uplifting to see your culture being celebrated and your identity being respected with a place like this. It makes your existence meaningful. The food is an innovative take on a tradition that's been marginalized by the dominant mandarin culture. The food just tastes amazing, nostalgic but also new! I'm so glad a restaurant like this exists. It is authentic Chinese but also American, traditional but also innovative, blending two impossible forces into a perfect harmony.

One of the best meals we've had in such a long time.  I can't even tell you what to order because everything is incredible.  We decided to try all of the entrees and each was better than the last.  Not only is the food excellent, as is the vibe and service.   I recommend coming with a big group so you can try all the dishes!

First gen Chinese Americans honor their hometown neighborhood and provide a new refreshing experience that Chinatown has been waiting for. 

Atmosphere is on point. The decor blends classic banquet halls with Chinese pop culture references. Music playing late 90's and 2000's bangers. Grab seats at the back bar for a front row seat at the kitchen.

The food still takes center stage. This isn't the run of the mill Chinese takeout. Traditional Cantonese cuisine served with artisanal flair for todays foodie. Can't really go wrong with any of the dishes, but some of the immediate favorites are Hangar Steak with oyster mushrooms and rice noodles, tiger shrimp and walnuts, and spicy eggplant. The scallion biscuits that come with the salt and pepper fried chicken is next level. 

Adding this is my go-to's for downtown spots.
So unbelievably good. Best meal I've had in nyc in a while. The potstickers! THE SPICY EGGPLANT! Go here!!!!!!

The crispy drunken chicken alone is worth going back for. Ambience on point. Great decor and 90's hip hop/r n' b. All the dishes were great. 

And drink selection very unique in terms of selection of Asian beers and seltzers. Very tasty non alcoholic drinks, too. Old man chu.

Food was soo delicious. We got the endive salad, salt and pepper chicken, and rice rolls. All were very flavorful and well prepared. The decor was also spot on. Mix of the old school and new school. Great to see a new restaurant in Chinatown with great food run by Chinatown locals!!

This place is absolutely amazing, probably the best meal I've had in a long time.

My friend found Potluck Club after seeing the review on Infatuation, so we booked a reservation for last Friday night. Everything on the menu looked fantastic, so we ordered... everything.

Well, mostly everything. All the entrees, 2/3 of the appetizers, none of the veggie dishes (sorry mom), and the dessert.

We loved everything we ate, but we all agreed that our favorites were the potstickers, salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, rice roll noodles with steak added, and the braised short ribs.

Not only was it an unbelievable meal, the restaurant itself has a great vibe, and the people who work there are awesome.

They told us that the restaurant was started by a group of friends who grew up in Chinatown and have known each other since they were 13 years old. They wanted to take some of the classic flavors of Chinese cuisine they had grown up with and bring a fresher, more modern take to it. Mission accomplished.

Love this place and can't wait to go back again.

This is a fun LES spot with cool Chinese pop culture decor adorning the interior. It's very vibey and chic - there's a movie reel screen of hits like Enter The Dragon, Kung Fu Hustle, In the Mood for Love and other films as well as a giant double happiness sign, vending machine display of classic products like haw flake, Tiger balm and much more, although I'm not crazy about the food. 

Personally, I'm not a huge fan of the new-wave takes on Asian cuisine and usually prefer the classic no frills restaurant food. This kind of fell into the former for me and I felt myself wanting more from some of the dishes. The salt pepper and fried chicken itself was ok (7/10) but the cheddar scallion scone and chili jam really stole the spotlight, both of which I probably would have ordered again on their own (10/10). The spicy eggplant wasn't really spicy at all, the XO fried rice was good but not that memorable, and the pineapple soft serve barely had any bolo bao influence on it aside from a few dustings. 

The plus side is the total bill was quite affordable between ordering 3 dishes, 2 desserts and drinks. It's a fun atmosphere and the effort put into the interior design is evidently thoughtful! Definitely appreciate those aspects so I think it's a worth a try.

Flavors and quality are there but this is a tad pricey for the portion size.

Best thing I had was the fried rice.  Rice was crispy and delicious with bits of corn and chinese sausage.  Will come back for this.  

Short ribs were flavorful but a bit overwhelming without white rice so be sure to order rice with it. 

Tiger shrimp was big and yummy. 

Salt and pepper chicken was good.  Scallion biscuit was alright.  Jam was good.  Wish it came with more pieces of chicken.  

Snow pea leaves were an interesting twist.  Haven't had lemon tasting snow pea leaves before.  Wouldn't say it's something I crave.  Although every asian meal needs vegetable.

Also disappointed they did not have the lychee drink I wanted.

Made a reservation and came here with great anticipation after all the hype. Honestly ... Potluck didnt live up to the hype. The service was amazing, but the quality of the food was just okay. We expected bigger portion sizes for the price, but each dish (menu stated that the food was family style) was definitely not big enough to share. The flavors were mild and not as flavorful as we hoped. However, the restaurant itself looks beautiful and straight out of a movie.

Potluck was for me one of those "one and done" / special occasion restaurants where it was a notable experience but not really worth the price of repeat admission.  Having high expectations coming here in speaking to my long time friend, I imagined they would have some classic Cantonese fare but upping them a notch with French techniques and unique spins from Global cuisine.  And they did.

Walking in, it was an instant nostalgic feeling as it was a true celebration of Cantonese cinema with all the Hong Kong stars I grew up watching decorated on the wall.  5:30pm and the door was lined up with other people pretty excited to find out what the hype was about.

We ordered the Oyster Mushroom Rice Rolls ($19 while 3- month old website states $17), Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts ($29), Snow pea shoots ($15), and the Pineapple Soft Serve ($7).  The oyster mushroom rice rolls I could tell was inspired by a classic gnocchi dish - portion was small and just needed a touch more garlic flavor which could have been achieved if it was cooked from a wok (which they don't use - ah the younger generation is missing out!).  The tiger shrimp dish was probably the biggest let down at 6 pieces of shrimp - truth be told the customer is paying for the fancy thin-stemmed broccoli-cauliflower hybrid caulilini.  The snow pea shoots was probably my only true favorite as it's value matched what I was getting - the garlic confit was pretty amazing as it had a cream like texture which isn't normally found in this dish.  The pineapple soft serve was a nice end and while my friends debate on the fact that it should be yellow, I tell them that it's just food coloring - however, it would be nice to have an actual pineapple topped, or perhaps a piece of dehydrated one.

Met up with former co-workers at this new place in the LES and we were pleasantly surprised at how authentically good the dishes tasted here. The service is friendly and attentive, and the decor a lot of fun with the theme being Chinese Cinema. Great place to take friends or family who are in town. The place is not super- large so expect a wait if you go during prime dinner hours; best to make a reservation.

My first time at Potluck club was for birthday celebration and the restaurant arrange this cute menu for the birthday girl. The food was delicious and made family style to share.

Everything was so delicious but what kept me up at night and showed up in my dreams was the salt and pepper fried chicken with scallion biscuits served with sweet spicy jam. I must have been drooling  in my sleep. 

I will be coming back with my kiddos again'

There are two types of Chinese restaurants in New York. One is what I'll call "the old guard" - think hole in the wall kind of place where the "menu" frequently consists of words and pictures on a wall, and prices never go above $20. I love these "old guard" restaurants because they are proof that delicious and well-executed food does not have to be expensive, but the downside is that they've made it hard for the general populace to take seriously Chinese restaurants as a category, because price, in the end, is still a marker of status. 

The other type, to which Potluck Club belongs, is the new wave of trendy places that have burgeoned into the city restaurant scene. They are generally more expensive, place more of a focus on presentation and decor, and blend in modern American elements into traditional Chinese cooking. Of course, all of the foregoing can sometimes result in a disaster of a restaurant (I won't name any names here), but when these restaurants are good, they are very good and more importantly, they get noticed by people/institutions that "matter". Potluck Club is one such place and it is fantastic. 

Starting with food: the dishes here are delicious and inventive. Case in point is the salt and pepper chicken served with biscuits and jam. The biscuits are clearly Southern in influence but add scallion and you're suddenly wondering why not all biscuits have scallion. The jam is even more interesting - it is jammy in consistency but tastes just like laoganma (a classic Chinese chili sauce) with a touch of sweetness, which means it goes well as a spread for the biscuits and as a sauce for the chicken. And the star of the show, the chicken, is pretty damn good too. Juicy, crispy, and a little spicy when eaten with the jalapeño - it hits all your taste buds in the best way. 

Onto drinks: when we were here, they didn't seem to have a full liquor license yet, but the beer and wine menu offered plenty of intriguing choices. We went with a makgeolli (Korean rice wine) and a green peppercorn IPA, which turned out to be quite good.

Service is chipper and friendly here. All of the waitstaff seemed excited about the restaurant and offered thoughtful suggestions on menu items, which I generally take to be a good sign of things to come.

TLDR: Potluck Club is an elevated Cantonese concept that looks to invite diners into an immersive space with great food for a good time. Worth checking out.

Had the opportunity to dine at Potluck Club and have to say - pleasantly impressed. Despite feedback from other reviews and acquaintances, I didn't feel bothered by the prices. If the ingredients are of good quality and it's executed properly; that's what you're paying for.

There really was nothing I disliked. Even the most basic appetizer, an order of potstickers that were basically pan-fried wontons were great. The skin was thin and the filling generously porky/bouncy.

The Salt & Pepper Chicken was a creative collaboration of Cantonese/Southern influences. While the rice noodle rolls is basically a chow fun, everything about that dish tasted a bit elevated. The rolls had proper wok hei, the beef was tender, there was a bit of spice and each bite more satisfying than the last. The Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts was a bit less mayo-ish; more lightly battered and for a fried dish; not that heavy. The Dole Whip dessert was a nice way to finish things up.

Lots of credit to the team for having the courage to attempt this concept and for the skills to do a good job pulling it off. I've long thought Cantonese cuisine has so much potential especially in a massive melting pot like NYC. There's just a general lack of awareness around the cuisine and this stereotyped mentality that Chinese food needs to be cheap. Friday nights are typically our time to try something new and date-ish. Potluck Club delivered on all my expectations and I definitely would return.

Ate here the other day. The biscuits are amazing. Recommend ordering extra. The salt and pepper chicken is my favorite. Nice flavor, crispy skin, moist chicken. Also orded the braised short rib. It was tender, but a little too fatty for my liking. Excellent and friendly service. I cant wait to go back.

I hardly ever write reviews but felt that I had to for the meal I had at this restaurant. I have been to many high end restaurants and dive bars but always willing to travel near and far for great food. Only reason why I came to this restaurant is because a friend recommended it. I did not have high expectations as there have been many restaurants that have tried the modern Asian and just doesn't cut it. This restaurant however was amazing.  The decor was original and whimsical, the staff super friendly and knowledgeable. But the food was a standout. We had the salt and pepper chicken, the jellyfish salad, the endive salad, the drunken chicken, the rice rolls with steak and oyster mushrooms and the snow pea leaves. Everything was super fresh, delicious and refreshing. They took the classic dishes and made it their own with a modern take. The owners seemed to have put thought behind everything little detail in the restaurant. I can't wait to go back and try the other dishes.  I neglected to take photos because the food was so delicious and was gone in seconds. This restaurant is a must visit.

Stopped by for a group dinner and had a great experience. The flavors and dishes were well executed takes on many of the Cantonese-American dishes that I ate growing up. I was in a very happy place throughout the meal.

Endive Salad - didn't eat, nut allergy
Dumplings - flavorful sauce, chili oil and toppings
Chicken and Biscuits - light fry on the tender chicken. Biscuits were buttery, and the chili oil sauce (jam?) was on point
Rice Rolls with Hanger Steak - familiar flavors of a beef chow fun in different form. Comforting
Tiger Prawns - I could eat these continuously 
Short Rib w Squash - fell right off the bone, super tender, sleeper favorite bite was the squash
Pea Shoots - good veggie side to go along
Interesting, modern take on Cantonese American dishes. The fried chicken with biscuit and jam was outstanding. It's a must order. The interior looks cool.

3.5 stars - great ambiance and service, okay food

Jellyfish tiger salad (not pictured) - pretty tasty traditional cold dish, felt like they could have put more jellyfish as we were mostly eating scallion by the end.

Oyster mushroom rice roll noodles - we added hangar steak for an additional $8, bringing this to $27 total. It's very pricy for what it is, rice rolls and asparagus are cheap and we didn't feel like we got a ton of steak. Still, this dish had the best flavor of the three we tried and would probably order it again if we were looking for a safe choice.

Dou Miao - not as tender as I expected and definitely could use more garlic. Sauce was okay but overall pretty bland dish. Did have a generous portion size though, enough to split between two people. 

Dole Whip - very standard dole whip if you've had them at Disney, but we did like the crumbly bits on top! 

Overall service was great, servers were attentive and food came out quickly. Would come back again to try some different dishes/if they expanded the menu. Also wish they had more drink options, definitely room to get creative with cocktails here!

I just found my favorite Chinese food in NYC. It's a bit fusion-ey, but the flavors and protein were treated with love and respect. Make sure to get a reservation as it's pretty popular.

Our favorite dishes were the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, xo fried rice (add the runny tea egg), and make sure to add the hangar steak to the rice noodle rolls.

One of the newer Asian American owned restaurant that has come on the scene. Great place for small groups so you can try a bit of everything. We came as a group of 6 and ordered everything except the endive salad (a bunch of carnivores) and the fried a chicken (got the scallion biscuits).

Honestly everything was so good. It was homey, but built for the modern generation. Favorites in the group include: walnut shrimp - sweet, crispy, large shrimps
Rice roll noodles - flavorful and crispy 
Snow peas - the best leafy green at any Asian restaurant (garlicky)
Scallion biscuit - everything you'd expect from a biscuit with an amazing jam

There honestly was no bad dish. Just order things you that sound good and enjoy the decor and friendly service. 

Don't forget to check the peephole across the bathroom for a surprise.

Short Ribs, Rice Roll Noodles, and Pineapple soft serve were stand out. Nice drink selection too. I enjoyed the nostalgic memorabilia and bathroom with a surprise peep hole too :) Super nice service. Excited to come back with friends!
Got the fried chicken and biscuits, and the rice rolls with hanger steak. A++. Food came out quickly and the ambiance is amazing. Highly recommend.
Absolute best food I've had in a VERY long time if not ever. Best service, great ambiance, and every single dish we got was 10/10. I cannot wait to come back!!!

Had a fantastic night with Potluck. Great food, great service and exceptional vibe. The eggplant and the fried rice were delicious... as were the chicken dishes. The traditional Chinese restaurant staples are presented with top quality ingredients then little details to bring them to the next level. (Jalapeño biscuits, crispy garlic and scallions, to name a pair of textural surprises.) Well worth an evening! Thank you, Team Potluck. We'll be back, for sure!

Definitely a cool addition to the neighborhood. This is a more upscale Chinese restaurant, filled with familiar and relatable decor and Chinese pop culture references. Such a beautiful spot to bring family and friends. 

The staff is extremely friendly and everyone was so bubbly and happy! Love the atmosphere, vibes and ambiance. 

All the food we had was good, but nothing outstanding enough to need to come back again. The menu is quite limited and I would have liked some more desserts.

Salt & Pepper Chicken w/ Scallion Biscuit ($25) 4/5 - 4 pcs of chicken that was juicy and cooked well. Comes with a chili-plum jam that complemented the chicken well. also comes with 2 scallion biscuits that I really enjoyed. would have liked the chicken to be a tad more flavorful - the dish is good but probably not something I would crave.

Oyster Mushroom Rice Noodles ($19) - 5/5 - honestly I didn't want to pay this price for the dish because I know how inexpensive it is to make it, but I heard good things. The dish is definitely very tasty (we dipped it in a separate chili crisp sauce that was sooo good) and not often you find a sauteed rice roll dish but just expensive. I would definitely order this again if I came back.

Berkshire Pork & Chive Potstickers ($12) - 3/5 - really nothing special - just pork dumplings. I prefer the other places in Chinatown. skip

Braised Short Ribs ($38) - 5/5 - priceyyyyyy but actually cooked to perfection. falls off the bone and sauce was flavorful and good but I couldn't pinpoint the taste. Not bad.

Dole Pineapple Soft Serve ($7) - 5/5 - can't go wrong with pineapple soft serve. comes with a fortune cookie and some crumble - definitely does not taste like the crumble of a bolo bun (this tastes like stale crumbles). nevertheless, good option for dessert.

Overall, it was a great experience. Everything about the restaurant was perfect. Food is good, no complaints. Nothing outstanding though. Pricey, but definitely good to try once.

I didn't think the food was anything special. I would prefer going to other spots to try first. The flavors weren't mindblowing or memorable. Usually I look for at least one dish or drink that I'd crave in the future but this place gave me none... from what I tried

There are no cocktails here - it's just makkoli, wine, and seltzer. 

Service was good in the beginning but as the crowd started to pick up, we had to flag the waitress down every time. The table next to us didnt get served to the point that someone offered them free drinks

I do appreciate the decor. The decor is prob one of the best I have seen. It's classy, modern Asian. 

Food - was okay. The jellyfish was very lemony and a bit salty. I was really craving that fresh, cold, refreshing feel and it wasn't there.

The chicken and bisc -- the biscuit was super fluffy, flavorful. Prob the best part of the night. The chicken was okay. Nothing memorable. 

The noodle and beef - was okay. Nothing special. The beef wasn't that tender or anything. I would prefer ordering without it.

Great new place in Chinatown by a younger generation of Chinese-Americans from right here in NYC. This place serves delicious traditional influenced food with a fusion-like twist along with an appealling array of wines and mocktails. Staff was extremely friendly and take the time to have conversations with customers while preparing drinks. This definitely made our experience even better! 

We ordered the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles with flank steak and salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits and we were blown away!!! The rice noodle dish had an amazing smokey aroma and taste and the chicken and biscuits were so flavorful! We didn't know what to expect but was very hyped from the reviews. The dinner absolutely did not disappoint! We finished with the pineapple soft serve which was very tart and refreshing! Can't wait to come back and try more dishes!!!

Went in a group of 6 and had about 80% of their menu. I'm pretty new to the city but this is currently my favorite Chinese restaurant. The endadive salad was really nice and refreshing, the pea sprouts were well done. All the other courses were really good, but the one standout that everyone really has to get is the SHORT RIB. So tender and delicious, so good that I almost ordered another order just for myself.

I cannot say enough good things about this place. From the Milk and Cream cereal bar team comes this amazing restaurant that centers around bringing ideas from different cultures to the table, a real cultural potluck and what I love so much about food and America.

The chef, Chinese-American, has training in mediterranean and italian culinary experience and he's using it to take the Chinese/Asian classics we know and love and elevate them, artfully craft them. We almost got the entire menu, and we loved every single one. 

JELLYFISH TIGER SALAD
While I wish there were more jellyfish in this salad, I love that there was so much by way of veggies and herbs in this salad to give you that vegetable crunch, freshness, herbaceousness to pair with the chewy yet crunchy sweet and savoriness of the jellyfish. Sesame seeds for extra crunch. Great flavors

TAIWANESE FRIED CHICKEN W SCALLION BISCUIT***
My favorite dish of the night due to how creative it is, it's an American South-Taiwanese fusion; fried chicken and biscuits meets Taiwanese fried chicken. Scallion flavor deeply imbues the fresh warm biscuit for you to pair with the umami taiwanese chicken thigh that is so juicy, and thick chili jam for sweetness with some heat (not too spicy at all) and combine for a perfect bite. Yum yum yum

XO FRIED RICE***
Do I dare say - the best fried rice I've ever had as as Chinese American person? texture is king here and you get so much crunch from the crisped garlic and the rice seems to be short grain japanese rice. Delectable, salty, savory, crispy, amazing texture! Not spicy but there's a bit of heat mixed in with the other flavors here. 

OYSTER MUSHROOM RICE ROLL NOODLES W OPTIONAL STEAK ***
They're doing a modern take on the beef chow fun we know and love by using tender steak pieces, umami oyster mushrooms, delicately cut veggies and bunching up the rice rolls and cutting them into mini cylinders that is very popular right now in China. They're perfectly crisped on one side to give you that delicate crunch preceding that tender chewiness you want from these noodles. Savory, salty DELICIOUS. 

Tiger Shrimp w Walnut
Walnut and shrimp makes a comeback in a form that is a perfectly cooked set of tiger shrimp with a freshly fried, frittery coating and toasty walnuts decorating it. Not as sweet or creamy as the traditional version but delicious and deep in flavor nonetheless.

DOLE PINEAPPLE SOFT SERVE W BO LO BAO CRUMBLE
Yes it tastes exactly like you want it too, not too sweet either, and comes with fortune cookies pp (one decorates the soft serve itself) and the crumble over it is inspired by bo lo bao (chinese pineapple bun, a fan favorite item of chinese americans when visiting chinese bakeries). DELICIOUS

The mocktails - DO NOT SLEEP ON THEM!!! They were both absolutely delicious, sweet, and refreshing. Nothing was too sweet; the flavor profile of all these items were so well balanced. I also got the soju seltzer which tasted just like melona ice cream bars  (get the honey melon flavor).

I cannot recommend this place enough. This place stirred up all the nostalgia feels as a Chinese American kid. I really admired the film exhibit and medicine cabinet/fortune cookie vending machine. Be sure to check out the peephole near the back.

We were a group of 6 and ordered basically everything off the menu. Highlights were definitely the potstickers, walnut shrimp, and the scallion biscuits, but everything was great. 

Plus, the owners are local Chinatown kids and you really can tell that they care a lot about the neighborhood. I can definitely say that this place is an amazing addition to the food and culture scene in the LES/Chinatown.

This is not your typical Chinatown asian restaurant. This is elevated Cantonese cuisine sprinkle with some old school nostalgia in the decor with modern spin in the menu. The menu is not extensive but the offerings are well thought out with unique twist to classic dishes.

We ordered the following: 
- potstickers (5 to an order) they were huge and flavorful
- 2X salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, we loved the first one so much we had two orders of it. The Chicken was juicy and the biscuit is not dry
-XO fried rice - they use some japanese rice to make these bomb dish
- rice roll with hanger steak - the mushrooms is a bit salty but who doesn't love rice rolls 
- lastly end the night with dole whip rice cream - very creamy and rivals Disney's 

The owners are local Chinatown kids who grew up wanting the neighborhood to thrive. You can see from the service, the menu and the decor. 

Bonus is the location is not central Chinatown so you can still find street parking.

Between the two of us we ordered

- Salt and Pepper Fried chicken and Scallion Biscuit: (5/5) this was our favorite dish by far! The chicken was crispy and juicy and the scallion pancakes were tender on the inside with a crispy exterior. The star however, was the chili jam. When spread on top of the chicken, it made the dish so flavorful and the perfect balance between sweet and salty.  
- Pork and Chives Potsticker (2/5): this one was very mediocre. It tasted really no better than any other dumplings from a dumpling specialized shop. The skin was almost even a bit tough, which was disappointing and the filling not super juicy. 
- Rice Roll with Flank Steak (3.5/5): the rice roll with flank steak was pretty disappointing! The flank steak was +8 extra but there was barely any meat. The rice rolls themselves were okay but nothing really special compared to other rice rolls I've had in Chinatown. The flavors were relatively similar to what I grew up with at home for 4x the cost.

Service was friendly and efficient and the space had great ambiance. I love the little easter eggs inside the shop (check out the peephole near the bathroom!). The decor is really cool and the people are clearly passionate. Not sure I'd come back for the food but I'm glad I tried it once.

Ambience and decor was eye catching for sure. But the most important part, the food, was nothing special -- almost disappointing:

Pork and chive potstickers: 1/5 -- better (and cheaper) at any other chinatown spot

Walnut shrimp: 3/5 -- great flavor but way too much chili aioli

Braised short rib: 4/5 -- super tender, but unmemorable

Creative Cantonese food with a little spice added. With a kitschy interior on Chrystie Street, Potluck Club offers an enjoyable evening in an interesting space. The menu and wine list are very limited. With a few upgrades it could be five stars.

We came here with friends to share a bunch of dishes and thought the food was really good! My personal favorite was the salt and pepper chicken with the scallion biscuits (the jam that came with them paired really well), but I really did enjoy all the dishes we got!

One thing to note is that a few tables are close to the entrance, so I would recommend trying to get a table near the back if possible.

The decor here is spot-on. The more you look around, the more you'll notice how much detail went into everything. I felt very immersed in the dining room, which filled up slowly throughout the evening (we arrived at 5:45). 

The dishes were great. You can tell a lot of thought went into the preparation and execution. The braised short ribs were very tender, the rice roll noodles were pillowy, and everything was garnished beautifully. The only drawback was I thought everything was a tad too sweet.  I wish I had ordered a bowl of rice to complement everything (although I'm not sure if that was an option). The only dish that fell flat for me was the eggplant. 

Not pictured here: the jellyfish appetizer which was my favorite dish! It was citrusy and had a lot of textures which made my tastebuds very happy (: The only thing I wish that could have made a marginally better was the ratio of jellyfish to garnishing. 

Service was excellent. Our waiter recommended a great drink for me and came to check in periodically.

Okay so my wife and I ate here months ago and it was so good I had to review the spot because not doing so would be an injustice to mankind. It was absolutely delicious. Heard about the place from a Fung Bros video about up and coming restaurant concepts in Chinatown and knew we had to check it out.

Ambience - Modern but low brow aesthetic making it perfect for a bit-more-than casual date spot. Great music not too loud.

Pricing - $$.  Well worth it

Food - Straight . Like so freaking good. Please do yourself a favor and go. Rice noodles were kissed perfectly with wok smokiness. Hangar Steak cooked to perfection. Tiger Shrimp were huge, juicy and delicious with a sauce that balnces the crisp so well. Not to mention the brocollini (in think?) that lent a complimentary vegetal bite to an otherwise richer dish. Spicy  was def one of my favorite renditions of this dish. So meaty and umami, im salivating thinking about it. 

Drinks - When we went they werent serving Hard A but the non alcholic cocktails were fire!  Old man chiu and Pink lady were so refreshing delicious and well balanced. Cant wait for their real cocktail program. Give em a liquor license NY!

Overall 5+/5. Will be back in a heartbeat!

Came with a friend to celebrate good news and it was such a cute place. We made a reservation for dinner and I'm glad we did because the place got packed really fast. The menu is a pretty short list, something around 3 appetizers and 10 entres to choose from. Everything is family style! The food was alright - the dishes were a little too salty for my liking. However, I really liked the Jellyfish Tiger Salad (has cilantro fyi) and the kabocha squash in the Braised Short Ribs dish. They have a pretty extensive drinks menu here - I ended up getting the Makgeolli and my friend got the Lunar yuzu drink. 

I really enjoyed the ambience of Potluck Club. The decor here made me reminisce about childhood - from the movies referenced to the medicine cabinet on display to the lychee gummy at the end of the meal. I'm hoping the menu will be on rotation and I look forward to coming back to try dishes I didn't get to try my first time here.
Yes it's everything healthy to eat and enjoy I love the potluck club is good choice  And the people r very nice

Came to Potluck Club not long after it opened with as a group of six and we literally ordered every single thing on the menu, and not a single thing disappointed. The standout for most of us was the salt and pepper chicken. The chicken was nice and crispy, the chili jam sauce was super addictive, and the scallion biscuits were light and fluffy and perfection. Other personal standouts were the braised ribs, potstickers, and the tiger shrimp. Honestly though, it was all tasty, and considering the restaurant had only been open a couple weeks that speaks volumes. Service and timing of the dishes coming out was also on point for being new. Great new spot and I can't wait to go back again!

I'm sad to say the food was straight up bad.
We got the xo fried rice, nothing special.
We also got the rice noodle oyster mushrooms stir fry,  The rice noodle didn't pick up on any flavor. However the other things like the asparagus and the mushrooms was so salty up to the point where it was bitter.  The snow pea shoots. Why can they not just stick to garlic? Honestly it was flavorless and also burnt.  The Berkshire pork dumplings was also a disappointment because the skin was very dry.  I've had bad food before but not as bad as this where I couldn't finish it.  The only reason why I didn't give it a one star was because the atmosphere and decorations were very good.
Ambiance and decor was immaculate. Definitely recommend reserving a table. Really enjoyed the salt&pepper chicken with scallion biscuits and their desserts.

This is a cute and trendy place with great food and even better service! We came on a Sunday evening and it was busy, but we were able to get a spot at the bar without a reservation. However, I would recommend making one just to be safe. 
There was a pretty good menu selection, though it's a bit on the pricier side. We got pork and chive potstickers, salt and pepper chicken w/scallion biscuits, and oyster mushroom rice rolls. My friend thought the potstickers were a little dry (I thought they were ok, but maybe that's because my mom makes them like that so I'm used to it), but other than that everything was tasty and well seasoned. While nothing particularly stood out to me, I would definitely come here again!

Amazing service! The team, especially the guy at the front with the cap went out of his way to make sure with the chef to make something that could accommodate us. My husband cannot have refined sugar due to a medical condition. Surely Chinese food is not suitable as every sauce has sugar added. However, the team made an xo sauce free fried rice for us and had the sauces on the side for the snow pea leaves and salad. Something that's hard to find in most Chinatown restaurants. My personal favorite was the scallion biscuit and endives salad. The eggplant was nice and garlicy.

I was hyped up on this place after some online reading, but my expectations outweighed the reality of the experience.

We walked straight in and found seating easily at the bar.  The layout is modern and hip, paying homage to Hong Kong cinema.  This is a charming place and would win praises from any visitors who are from out of town.

You eat family style here.  We ordered potstickers, XO fried rice, and oyster mushroom rice roll noodles.  Out of the dishes we ordered, the rice roll noodles was our favorite.  That said, nothing really WOW'd us and everything felt okay.

Service was friendly, but they weren't the most attentive.  From the bar, you have a view into the kitchen and can see the chef cook.  It was a little underwhelming to see the chef mostly pulling pre-cooked containers to assemble the dishes on the menu.  Not expecting a Benihana experience at all, but watching the chef cook resembled the assembly line at Chipotle.

I would come back, but wouldn't say it's a priority.  With the higher price point and the close proximity to Chinatown, I'm more interested in exploring other restaurants in the area.

I've been excited to try this spot after reading a bit about their story on a few food blogs and believe it lived up to the hyoe! The space is super cool and definitely adds to the experience. We tried a good portion of the menu, with my favorites being the fried chicken and biscuits take and the rice noodle rolls. For the negatives, XO fried rice was the only lackluster item and the walnut shrimp was tasty, but way too small for the price ($29). Prices have also jumped significantly since they opened just two months ago, so be aware of that. With that said, I would love to go back and hope they add a few more items to the menu! I can see this place becoming an impossible reservation very quickly.

Such an amazing spot ! None of the dishes disappointed us and beach bite had us wanting more! It was so flavorful and unique in taste. By far, one of my favorite spots this year! You must not skip out on their dessert either ! Also, the interior is super nice and ambience was great.

Pros: 
The decor of this restaurant is amazing and staffs were super accommodating! The waiter explain to us which were their popular dishes and what was included in each dish. 

My family and I enjoyed the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits a-lot. The chicken was super  juicy and crispy. The biscuits that came with it were soooo buttery soft. 

We also enjoyed their shrimp walnut dish, we loved the kick of spice it had to it compared to traditionally made shrimp walnut ( which is a bit of the sweeter side).

Cons:
Jellyfish tiger salad had a great flavor but it was 90% cilantro & scallions while only have a super small amount of jellyfish! We thought for $14 the portion of jellyfish should be larger! 

Oyster mushroom rice roll noodles had a mediocre flavor,  the asparagus were under cooked so we ended up not really eating that dish. I also feel like the dish itself was a little to char, it kinda tasted too burnt for me. 

Spicy eggplant was undercooked as well! The skin of the eggplant was so hard it felt like paper in our throats! They were also not spicy at all.

I love this place. From the food to the decor to the friendly service. I just love the modern take on Cantonese cuisine. There's not enough of that here! My favorite thing is the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles with hangar steak. The rice rolls are seared, which gives them a smoky flavor. The berkshire pork and chive potstickers are SO good as appetizers. I would order one for myself. End your meal with a pineapple soft serve!

Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles + Hanger Steak - 6/10
I really enjoyed how the rice noodles were cooked in this dish. They were chewy and full of flavor. My only complaint was that we added the hanger steak for an additional $8 but there were barely any pieces of steak. We kept picking up mushroom thinking it was steak but were let down each time. 

Salt & Pepper Chicken W/ Scallion Biscuits - 9/10
This was the shining dish of the night. The chicken was extremely juicy, no dry parts at all. The scallion biscuits were extremely buttery but it did get a bit dry at the end. However, slap a little bit of the chili-plum jam on it and you're good to go. And the chili-plum jam was absolutely delicious!!

Came here a couple weeks ago and was absolutely blown away. The food is excellent, the staff is wonderful, and the vibe is immaculate. Between the nostalgic/retro movie decor, and the modern spins on classic dishes, Potluck Club speaks to the Cantonese-American experience. Will definitely be back soon!

This place is OUTSTANDING. My friend and I stopped here for dinner and was blown away. Such kind and thoughtful service, the vibe was immaculate and the food was phenomenal. 

We ordered:
- endive salad: highly recommend, you haven't had anything like this
- oyster mushroom salad: sooooo goood! Get the steak with it
- salt and pepper chicken: yummy fried chicken 

Definitely coming back!

Eating food at a restaurant is a privilege shared between two parties. It can be a great memory or a horrible one. As you can guess by my rating this one was a horrible experience.
We had the potstickers, the jelly fish salad , fried chicken and the roasted chicken. My favorite was the potstickers.
We came in 15 min late and after 1.5 h while eating our desert the host star ted harassing us that we should leave because they want to seat someone else. They told us we have the seat until 8 when we were seating. The host basically was yelling at us and he was telling us that we have 5 star reviews on Yelp and us reporting this wouldn't change anything.
I will NOT recommend this place as they don't have any idea that they are in hospitality business. They are trying to turn as many table as possible.
Service and food were great. Enjoyed the salt & pepper chicken, XO Fried Rice and the Short Ribs.

The food here is delicious, here are the items I'd recommend.

Endive salad
Fried chicken biscuits
Oyster mushroom rice roll noodles

Others recommend:
Dou miao
Crispy drunken chicken with shrimp chips
Tiger shrimp

We unfortunately did a walk in and waited 30 mins for bar seating, would've definitely preferred a table to share items. The pineapple soft serve tasted like dole whip. The space has pretty cool decor.

Food: 9/10
Service: 8/10
Ambiance: 9/10

Reality rating would probably be 3.5 stars. First off, the ambience and aesthetics was phenomenal, it was modern, chic, and hit the hong kong nostalgia just right---Lo fu zi/Old Master Q, Bruce Lee, Shaolin Kids, etc.  If you want an instagrammable place, this is your best bet.  During the dining experience there were a bunch of people pacing throughout the restaurant taking videos and photo.  So yeah, this is definitely a place to get your photo ops in and take a few IG posts.

Onto food:
Jellyfish salad $14- taste was overall fine, it's just I felt there was a lot of reverse garnishing going on---the jellyfish seemed like the garnish and the dish was basically a load of cilantro.

Crispy Drunken Chicken $28 - presentation was great, I thought the flavor was good but my friend said it was too salty.  But one thing we both agreed on was that the ginger scallion sauce was lacking.  There was no punch or much flavor going on.

Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts $29- overall good dish, there was a definite kick and an interesting take on the usual sweet mayo walnut shrimp.  The spice definitely hits the tongue so for anyone who isn't into spicy, just be wary.

Overall it's definitely a chic and hipsterish place with interesting modern interpretations of Chinese dishes. Service was decent, the server was courteous.  I really liked that they gave a cool postcard with the check.  Initially my friend and I went into the restaurant about 5 minutes early since it was a bit cold outside and the door was opened but we were told to stay outside, we waited outside for an additional 10 minutes with another party and we didn't go inside until we had to ask the worker if it was ok to go in.  Anyways, definitely foreigner friendly and perhaps a decent place to introduce to someone who hasn't tried cantonese food.  Not exactly my cup of tea, I feel like if I were to take my family to a joint like this they would obsess over the price/portion and continuously talk about old school places in Chinatown being better.  Overall I feel like the interior design was the main attraction rather than the food.

Run, don't walk to Potluck Club!! Upon entering, I felt like I was reliving my childhood. Between the 90's R&B playlist, Bruce Lee posters and nostalgic food, Potluck Club is a first-generation Asian-American's paradise. They opened ~4 months ago, has very well trained staff and an efficient kitchen. I made reservations for my husband's birthday and originally, was concerned about the portions based on pictures I'd seen, but was pleasantly surprised. TLDR; if you're looking for Pineapple Dole Whip in New York City, come here. If you're looking for a place to hang with good friends and good food, come here. What stood out to me was that though most diners were in their 20-30s, there were also people in their 50-60s from the Chinatown area that were also enjoying the food. #authenticity

We ordered:
-Jellyfish Tiger Salad ($14) - very well seasoned with generous portion (more than your average dim sum place), I thought it was a bit heavy on the sesame oil but my husband loved it and it was very flavorful
-Salt and Pepper Chicken w/ Scallion Biscuits ($25) - 4 large chicken thighs with a non-spicy chili-plum jam that was scrumptious and addictive. The scallion biscuits were great and balanced out the chicken. The Salt and Pepper chicken is made with the same rub as (椒鹽豬扒) with jalapenos though it's not spicy at all
-Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles ($19) - thick cheong fan rice noodles with oyster mushroom, flavorful sauce and seasoning with asparagus and garlic chives. You can add steak for an extra $8. It was my favorite dish of the night tied with salt and pepper chicken
-Tiger Shrimp w/ Walnuts ($29) - I had seen pictures of this and was concerned there were only going to be 2-3 shrimp but there were 6-8 and the caulini (cauliflower broccolini mix) was AMAZING. Note that they are tiger shrimp so they're bigger and meatier than a regular shrimp. I loved this sauce the most out of all the entrees with the calabrian chili aioli + hot honey. Delish.
-Spicy Eggplant ($16) - Felt like I needed a vegetable to feel healthy at tonight's dinner, but really could've left it out. The eggplant cuts were a bit long, seasoned well but I think I was so full by the end of the meal I didn't have much appetite for spicy eggplant. This is one of the dishes I didn't feel were too different from other restaurants / Chinese takeout places whereas the other dishes had elevated Chinese classics significantly
-Pineapple Dole Whip ($7) - absolutely delicious and very authentic! Same thing as Disneyworld/Disneyland's itself and the only place I've found in NYC that has it. 

Their drink menu is super extensive with cool craft hard seltzers like Lunar and Hummy, pale ales with jasmine tea, makgeolli, sanzo, hot oolong or chrysanthemum tea. It's also nice they have non-alcohol signature drinks like the landlady (strawberries, plum and sprite) and old man chiu (citron honey, green tea, lime, soda). Definitely ordering a landlady next time!!

A bit of nostalgia fused with a modern take on traditional Chinese cuisine. We had walked past this place as it was being built, so we're happy to see it up and running. It was perfect all around, and the staff was fun with a birthday celebration. If you're having any reservations, don't! Great for dates, groups, etc. can't wait to go back! They're starting up a brunch service too, so plenty of reasons to go again and again.

I came back last weekend for dinner with a bigger group and got to try pretty much everything on the menu. Everyone had a great time. Out of the dishes I didn't have the first time, I liked the XO fried rice and braised short ribs the most. Service was consistent - friendly and attentive. Another great meal at Potluck Club!

A friend brought us here while we were visiting NYC and I'm so, so glad he did. It sounds like brunch is a new endeavor for them and I hope they continue so I can come back the next time I'm in town. The interior design, atmosphere, and service were on point, while the food was perfect. I got the salt and pepper chicken sandwich while the rest of the table got, well, everything else. There wasn't a single thing we thought could have been better (we were all baffled how radish could taste so damn good). Based on this experience, I greatly look forward to giving their dinner a shot some time soon.
ehhhhhhhh there's better food at lower price in chinatown ... a cool vibe / decor tho and appreciate the creative vision

Great people, great food, great time! I came with a bigger group and got to try pretty much everything on the menu. The service was wonderful, food was exceptional and everyone had a great time. You can see the detail and love they put into the experience, the food, the presentation and the atmosphere. Will definitely be back!

Walked in with 3 friends on a Saturday night for dinner and surprisingly were able to get seated at the bar after about 20 mins! We ordered the salt & pepper chicken w/ scallion biscuits, the xo fried rice, the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles with hanger steak, and the snow pea shoots to share.

My favorite dish out of everything we tried definitely was the chicken w/ biscuits. I especially enjoyed the biscuits, but I do wish the chili-plum jam had a bit more of a noticeable spicy kick to contrast the relatively neutral flavors of the chicken and biscuits.

My least favorite dish, however, was probably the fried rice because it was a bit on the blander side for my taste. I also prefer my rice a little more cooked. But I really do think the flavor of the corn adds a lot to the dish and thoroughly enjoyed it! Personally would pick a new dish to try over reordering this one if we were to come back though.

Both the rice roll noodles and the pea shoots were solid as well. Definitely add the steak to the noodles because it was so good and tender!

After everything, we of course had to finish off with the pineapple soft serves. It's good to share between two people imo! I loved the crumbles on the dessert, but the flavor itself was a bit too sour for me.

The biggest find for the evening for me though was probably the hummy soju seltzer. I ordered the asian pair flavor, and THIS hands down is the best asian flavored hard seltzers that I've had so far! So shout out to the server who recommended this drink to us.

Overall, good spot but definitely didn't blow me away like I was expecting after all the raving tiktoks that I've seen. However, the decor is truly amazing, which makes it worth visiting. And make sure to grab a fortune cookie in the vending machine on your way out!

I came here with a party of 2 on a Sunday evening. We made reservation a week prior through Resy. I've been wanting to come here since hearing ravishing reviews from my friends.

The decor is your modern take on the classic HK restaurant atmosphere. There were a few memorabilia from the older days predating back to the 70-80's.  The servers were all very nice and helpful!

As for the meal; I really enjoyed the quality of the food. I can see where the hype came from. The price you're paying is a bit higher than your typical chinese cuisine, but if you want good quality comfort food, Potluck Club is what you want!

We ordered a lot for 2 people, but surprisingly we finished 90% of it!
- Berkshire Pork and Chives Potstickers
- Endives Salad
- Salt and Pepper Chicken w/ Scallion Biscuits
- Oyster Mushrooms Rice Rolls w/ Hanger Steak
- Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts
- Pineapple Pineapple Soft serve (dole whip with bolo-bao crumble)
 
In short: I really liked every dish they served. It was better than your typical chinese cuisine meal. The Endives salad and the Salt & Pepper Chicken were definitely the two show stoppers of this meal!
The Endives Salad -- consisted of dragonfruit, endives, and cara cara oranges.  It was a very refreshing dish to everything else that's savory. It's the perfect balance!
