The Salt and Pepper Chicken was also really good. I would say it's as good if not better than most S&P Chicken dishes I've had from Taiwanese restaurants. Definitely a MUST at Potluck Club. 
I also liked the Oyster mushroom rice rolls w hanger steak and the the Berkshire pork and chives dumplings. Both were flavorful and full of umami. 
I thought the Tiger shrimp with walnuts could've been a bit more savory. It wasn't terrible, but I feel like it definitely could've been more flavorful.
Lastly, for the pineapple dole whip w/ bolobao bread crumble, it's a nice light soft serve to end the dinner! Not overly sweet, but enough to enunciate the pineapple flavor, which is a good balance in my opinion.

Overall; Had a positive experience trying the delicious food. Would come back on another occasion.
Delicious! Wonderful atmosphere. The staff is precious. We stumbled upon this place on a freezing cold evening and we are so glad we did! Don't miss this yummy spot!

Came here with a group of 4, we came right at opening and were fortunately able to snag a spot, but would recommend making a reservation if you have a larger group. The interior of the restaurant was really pretty, it felt modern but still had that "cantonese asian banquet round table" flair in the back. 

In terms of food, the portions are pretty small so even though it's supposed to be "family style" (as marked in the menu), you might want to get at least 1 main dish for each head. However, everything we got was pretty good. We got the 

-dumplings 
-salt and pepper chicken with biscuits 
-oyster rice rolls with the hanger steak addition
-pea shoots
-pineapple ice cream

The dumplings were decent, but it felt like we got them served a bit cold/too late as the skin was a bit thick/hard but also too chewy. The flavor on the dumplings were good.

The salt and pepper chicken was by far our favorite, the chicken was really crunchy, moist and perfectly fried. The chili jam was the star of the show in my opinion, it was very tasty (reminded me of hints of Lao gan ma) and worked really well when together with the biscuit and chicken. 

The rice roll dish with the steak was also good and flavorful but nothing too crazy. The pea shoots were also good, there seemed to be some sort of citrusy sauce drizzled on top, which tasted good on top of the typical garlic pea shoot dish. The vegetables were cooked well (not over cooked or undercooked). 

The dole pineapple ice cream was also very tasty! It tastes like the canned pineapples and I liked the tartness of the ice cream mixed with the crumbles of the pineapple bun. Also liked the touch of Asian gummy's at the end of the meal with the Bruce Lee postcard, it was a nice way to end the meal! 

Overall, Everything we got was good, though some dishes did leave me wanting for something more / different from the typical Cantonese version of the dishes. Nothing particularly wow'ed us, and given all the other available Chinese food nearby, I wish the portions were a bit bigger for the price, but if you're looking for a nice vibe I would recommend coming here!

Brunch was a solid 4.

The classic Chinese bakery drinks like yeen yeung with oat milk felt slightly exorbitant at $5-$6 :'( plus it looked/tasted watery. 

Chow Mein was my favorite - tasty and smoky. Expensive relative to traditional Chinese but you get a better cut of steak!

Endive Salad with Fried Chicken - the ingredients are so interesting with dragon fruit and pistachio. This was good and is also served during dinner. The fried chicken in this salad is bite sized. Good mix of something acidic and light with something breaded and fried.

Bolo Bao Milk Toast - I liked this one for it's uniqueness! Came with a side of red bean paste that definitely should add.

Sunny Side Eggs over Radish Cake hash - I recall liking the radish cake but there was not very much of it in this dish. You can order this as a side instead.

Taro Shrimp Fritters - I remember thinking it was fairly good at the time but unfortunately I can barely remember it now. 

French Toast with Longan/Blueberry Jam - was recommended this and it was good but very decadent with whipped cream.

We also ordered the pork belly sandwich but I did not try it.

Total ended up being $45 per person including tip for brunch with no alcoholic beverages.

We went for brunch and overall had a great experience. We started with a few of their drinks: the Old Man Chiu was sweet, sour, and complex, the Landlady was fruity and salty, and the Yeen Yueng was very solid. For entrees, we got the Hong Kong French Toast, Salt & Pepper Chicken Sandwich, Chow Mein, and a side of Radish Cake Hash. The Hong Kong French Toast which was like a custard bao in french toast form. Creamy, sweet, and decadent. The Chicken Sandwich was very solid. Juicy and the mustard green aioli was a welcome and interesting condiment. The Chow Mein was the star of the show. It was savory, umami, and satisfying. The noodles were al dente with some crunch bits. It also came with some chili oil which was great. The side of Radish Cake Hash was also amazing and can't miss item. Very excited to come back here for dinner

Great spot for brunch! The food came quickly and the service was fantastic. For the atmosphere and decor, this restaurant provides an elevated dining experience -- I will note that the price is slightly higher than Chinatown. For two people I would recommend sharing 3 items!

Honestly.. I didn't want to join the club. The trend of TikTok/Instagram friendly restaurants has me disheartened. So many focus on style vs substance with décor and food made to look great on camera while neglecting to produce delicious, well made food. Thankful it is not the case with Potluck Club.

From the moment you enter the asymmetrical entryway you are transported into a dreamlike movie theater with impressive murals, stylish and whimsical decoration, posters & screens highlight now playing/coming soon (Enter the Dragon!) and even a theater marquee reminding you that we are here for a good time, not for a long time - indeed! 

My group of 4 arrived at opening (5:30pm), but with no reservation on a Friday night the only thing we were offered were seats at the chef counter or a table at 9pm. We opted for the counter. This was fortuitous since we were seated on the left side where the counter rounded the corner our group was able to face each other with us all having a front row seat to view inside the kitchen. 

We all ordered drinks - sparkling flavored soju cans for my friends, a sour ale for me and we are off to the races..

Jellyfish Tiger Salad out first is fresh and delicious. I would have liked to seen the cilantro cut into smaller bite size pieces with whole branches a little awkward to eat. Berkshire Pork and Chive Potstickers were excellent - the firmer texture than you would expect for a dumpling and flavor of the juicy pork made it memorable.

Generally not a fan of rice roll noodle (niangao) since they tend to be too gummy and chewy, but the Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles were cloud-like reminding me of well made gnocchi. Salt and Pepper Chicken with flaky Scallion biscuits made with juicy dark meat - not too spicy chili plum jam and jalapeño make a nice accompaniment. The Braised short ribs were tender and delicious - not super fall apart tender, but more of a steak like chew the flavor was balanced highlighting the meat. Unfortunately the kabocha squash was inedible with these since they were overcooked to the point of being grainy and dry  - a surprising disappointment, but a refreshing Pineapple Dole whip rounded out the night with thoughts of Disney.

Really at a 4.5 stars but damn Yelp doesn't allow halfsies. My friend remarked this would be a perfect date spot and I agree, but maybe better to come with a group to share more. All the elements are there as I described along with friendly potlucking club members you should make your reservation and join today!

Food ranged from okay to good, depending on the dish. Service was bizarrely terrible and left a bad taste in my mouth. I rarely have service issues that bad in NYC. I won't be coming back here.

On food alone, I would probably give Potluck Club 3 stars. The pot stickers were great, as were the rice roll noodles with steak. I wasn't a huge fan of their salt & pepper chicken biscuits or tiger shrimp. The drink menu was quite poor...it's a choice as a restaurant to only serve beer and funky natural wines. I was not impressed. 

We were a big group there for a birthday dinner. About 20 min before the restaurant was supposed to be closing, we asked to order a bottle of sparkling wine for the table. We hadn't yet received our last dish. The restaurant gave us a lot of trouble and told us no to the bottle of wine because they were closing soon. The issue for us was that they never informed us of last call. We basically had to beg them to give us a bottle of wine, which is crazy! They finally relented after 10-15 min of us asking. We drank the bottle quickly and were wrapping up dessert, and they then turned on all of the lights to shoo us out. If you want to close your restaurant at 11pm, maybe you shouldn't seat a large party at 9pm...pretty basic to understand that a large birthday party will take longer than 2 hours. Anyways, I am super disappointed in the service we received here and would recommend others to avoid this place. 

If you are looking for comparable food, I had a great experience at Bonnie's in Brooklyn. The food, drinks, and service are all better there.

Came here on a Friday night with a reservation but still had to wait 15 minutes to be seated because of a reservation mix up. The tiger shrimp with walnuts was just ok for the price at $29. The best dish we ordered was the chicken and biscuits ($25). The chicken was really crispy and seasoned well. The scallion biscuits were a creative twist. I feel there are better restaurants in Chinatown for classic Cantonese dishes but I guess given the decor, ambiance, and the fusion "modern takes", this place does this job. Also, they still don't have their liquor license so they are currently just service wine and beer.

Pretty solid!  I came here for brunch on a Sunday with a buddy and the atmosphere was really cool.  The place has a lot of vintage references to media from Hong Kong in the 70s/80s with pictures/videos surrounding the dining area.  The food itself was pretty good - I got the pork belly cha siu egg sandwich with fries which had great bbq flavor, but honestly had less meat than I would've liked compared to the egg (it also was pretty expensive at $21 for the size of the sandwich).  I got a yeen yeung for a drink which is a blend of coffee and tea that's apparently a popular drink in hong kong.  To be honest the drink mostly tasted like tea and looked like coffee, so it was a little disappointing but not bad.  Service was also good - the folks were nice and attentive to the table.  I would come back if I was in the area and there was availability for a walk in.

It was on the harder side to get a reservation here given the popularity but I got lucky with a cancellation and snagged a table for 4 on a Sunday night. We ordered the salt & pepper chicken with scallions biscuits, oyster mushroom rice roll noodles, braised short ribs, and spicy eggplant. The food was a solid 4 - nothing was mind blowing, but everything was delicious, reliable, and homey. The chicken and especially the ribs were a tad on the dry side, but were still good. Service was terrific and the ambiance was modern and welcoming, both easily a 5/5. Settling on a 4/5 overall since the food seems a bit overpriced for what you get, especially given it's nothing innovative and you could get similar dishes in the surrounding Chinatown area for much less. Would definitely skip the $40 short ribs, but else I wouldn't mind coming back.

Lord have mercy. This new Cantonese spot in LES is fire. From the vibe of the decor, to the awesome staff, to the impeccable food, this meal was one for the books. Of note, we first ate at Estela the same night (don't ask, sometimes you and your friends just want 2 dinners) and it was twice as expensive as Potluck for half the amount of food, although solid. Do not skip the potstickers , the salt and pepper chicken, and the Chinese sausage fried rice. Pineapple soft serve  was soft and creamy, tangy and not too sweet. 13/10 would recommend. Coming back for brunch asap.

I would give The Potluck Club 5 stars but for the saltiness of some dishes and this is from someone who loves salt.  This new Chinese Fusion hotspot has a small, but well curated menu.  Plating was as modelesque and hip as everyone there including the staff, but the servers were super friendly and the place has a great energy. Half white, half Asian patronage. Not your typical C-Town restaurant.  This place is sleek and clean with a mod open kitchen.

Hesitant before visiting this place because of all the hype from TikTok but I was pleasantly surprised! The decor inside is really cool and the staff are friendly. I recommend getting the oyster mushroom rice rolls and the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits - it comes with a peppercorn chili type sauce that's really good.

Went on a weekend for dinner and unfortunately had an issue. We ordered multiple dishes, which were great, until the salt & pepper chicken. I ate 1 piece and didn't notice anything amiss, my partner had a piece and noticed a pink area, but we thought it was just a vein. But then the next piece my partner had was literally raw. Completely uncooked chicken - I mean fully pink, transparent, shiny, etc. My partner had taken a bite of it before seeing it. We immediately notified our server who couldn't have been more kind. They refunded us for the dish and apologized repeatedly. But this feels like a pretty serious issue - how is the kitchen not noticing when chicken is severely undercooked? The rest of our food was great, but the chicken - and our concern over my partner eating raw/undercooked chicken and potentially becoming ill - kind of put a damper on the meal. Hopefully just a one off...

The potluck club catered an event at my office, and the food was so good! My favorite dish was the fried rice. It was nothing like any others I have had before. There was plenty of Chinese sausage (my favorite), corn, and some dried onions. That was all that was in it! It was a unique take on the dish and quite delicious, making me want to go to the Potluck Club to try more!

I'll start by saying it wasn't easy to get a reservation for dinner on a Saturday so try to book it at least a week in advance. That said, I really loved everything about the potluck club. The space was modern and chic, with a traditional Chinese flare. The staff was super friendly and polite. The food was unique, flavorful, and authentic. 

We had the:
- xo fried rice (classic fried rice dish + corn, Chinese sausage)
- oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (reminiscent of tteokbokki) 
- braised short rib (tender, fall off the bone, served with squash)

I'll have to come back to try the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits (every table had it!) Overall, the food, service and experience were exceptional and I'm already planning my next visit.

Potluck club was super hyped up for me as new chinese food so I was excited to go. The service was so kind and attentive and the interior is incredible and well thought out.

For food we got:
- potstickers: these were my fav of the night! super juicy, packed and well fried
- salt & pepper chicken w scallion biscuits: really well fried (boneless) chicken and had a distinct salt and pepper taste. i really loved the fluffy biscuits with a hint of scallion flavor
- oyster mushroom rice rolls: everyone raved about these but i didn't enjoy them as much. the rice rolls texture was chewy and soft but some were burnt. also the sauce was good but i didn't really taste it unless i ate the veggies/beef. 

overall id come back to try the other dishes! wish i had a bigger stomach lol

Good vibe, good alc selection, and good food! Love the atmosphere here and staffs were also very friendly! For food, we got one of their salad, salt and pepper fried chicken with scallion biscuits, rice roll noodles, braised short ribs, and pineapple soft serve. I especially recommend their fried chicken and short ribs. I thought their pineapple soft was aight. I also highly recommend trying their natural wine! I especially liked their hawju and takju (makgeolli based). 

Overall good spot to come for dinner with anyone / for any occasion

Ambiance 10/10, food overall was very good, but nothing blew my mind to the point that I'd come back again immediately (my expectations given the hype were quite high, and this didn't quite meet it). The best dish was absolutely the oyster mushrooms rice noodles. However, everything seemed incredibly over priced for the portion size. We added steak to the oyster mushroom dish for $8 and it was barely any steak. They also said they couldn't serve us the dole whip because they needed to save it for two large parties that were seated near us, which was a bit weird, confusing, and disappointing. 

Overall would certainly recommend trying once for sure, but not a repeat spot for me given all of the other fantastic food in the neighborhood.

Come with a big group so you can try everything! There's a big variety and nothing was a disappointment. Portion sizes are also pretty generous! 

* = favorites
- jellyfish salad
- endive salad*
- salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits*
- crispy drunken chicken w/shrimp chips
- oyster mushroom rice roll noodles*
- tiger shrimp w/walnuts*
- braised short ribs
- spicy eggplant
- snow peas
- old man chiu

LOVED my experience at Potluck Club! 

I met up with an old friend here a month ago for Friday night dinner. The murals on the wall are so fun and the bar area reminded me of a theater sign. I wish I had taken pictures of the decor. 

The server graciously seated me as I waited for my friend. Once he came, we ordered the crispy drunken chicken, tiger shrimp with walnuts, and snow pea shoots. I love how the food stuck to Cantonese classics but made their own spin on it to really elevate each ingredient they used. Each piece of shrimp was way bigger than I thought, the sauce of the chicken paired well with the chicken, and the snow pea shoots were seasoned just right. I cannot emphasize just how much each item was perfectly done. We also ordered a bottle of Hwaju makgeolli, which paired well with our meal.

In summary, I'm grateful to have friends with great taste in restaurants. Next time, I'll definitely try their pineapple soft serve!

Made it out to the Potluck Club after seeing it all over socials and was lucky to be seated after walking in with out a reservation on a Sunday evening. The restaurant is decorated with some really cool décor and the seating arrangement is really well organized. We were seated at the bar and had a really cool view of the kitchen.

We started off with the Scallion biscuits which may have been the highlight of the meal. The biscuits were paired with a spiced jam, and was one of the best bites I have had in a while. For the mains, we split three main courses including the Oyster Mushroom Rice Rolls which was incredibly textured and flavorful, the Tiger Shrimp and the Spicy Eggplant side which was a very large portion.

Overall, the vibes and the food at Potluck Club are spot on. This is a spot that I would bring friends in from out of town and I will definitely be returning very shortly.
Food was delicious, the modern decor was refreshing and the total ambiance was a delight. We thoroughly enjoyed the endive salad and the rice rolls (definitely get it with the flank steak)

Love the vibe of the place. The portions are generous. Endive Salad, great. Extremely refreshing. The S&P chicken? Get it. Put a dab of jelly on the chicken. Put a slice of chicken on the biscuit, and have a good time. The shrimp, delicious. Nothing necessarily innovative about the dish, but the execution is excellent. Great service as well.

This place got game. I'm impressed. It's not easy to put modern twist to old classics, but I'm glad they shot their shot. 

Their most popular dish was the salt and pepper chicken w scallion biscuits, and while the fried chicken was very good, it's the biscuits that stole  the show and elevated the dish. This isn't really a Chinese dish, but it's a very American dish, glad to see it on menu. Pro tip make a biscuit chicken sandwich instead of eating it separately, douse on their house chili sauce, and it was one of the best bites I've had this year

Second popular is their oyster mushroom rice roll noodles. This I found mediocre, beef was a bit dry and chewy, rice rolls texture not as soft as I would have liked, asparagus were ok actually. Points for creativity though, I think they were trying to give a modern take on the classic beef chow fun, but for me that dish is irreplaceable. Nice try though

Switching over to their brunch menu, their Hong Kong french toast was awesome. I'm a fan of salted egg anything, so their salted egg lava inside the toast was mind blowing

Their take on the radish cake was good. The sunny side egg, diced bacon, shishito peppers and arugula paired well with the bite sized radish cubes. I would have preferred more radish cakes though 

Lastly, the endive salad was phenomenal, a must try. Sure it's one of the more bitter tasting salads, but the dragon fruit, orange, pistachio, and pecorino all complimented each other very well, made for a very refreshing dish. This you don't really find at a typical Chinese restaurant, so I'm glad it made the menu. Pro tip here is adding the fried chicken leftovers to the salad! 

Beverage wise I only tried the yeen yeung, somewhat disappointed that it was from a tea bag and not from a tea master sifu in the kitchen, straining the tea the authentic way. Jokes aside it did taste good, and I understood the profit constraints from making it old school, so I'll give it a pass

Being inventive when it comes to food is very risky, especially Chinese food, you can't please everyone, and not every dish will be a hit. I'm glad they are going for the hail mary though and I hope there will be more restaurants like Potluck Club in the future!
Great place to catch up with friends and feel some nostalgia! Love the interior design.

Potluck Club is meant to be enjoyed by a group. In fact, if your dining party is not at least 3-4+ people, you should hold off and visit this place once you've convinced a few more friends to join you. It truly is a family style restaurant, and you just won't get the real experience unless you are able to try a large assortment of dishes. 

Luckily, I visited Potluck with 14 other people, so we ordered multiples over every dish on the menu! And there wasn't a single disappointment among all of the selections. Some of my personal favorites included the Berkshire Pork Potstickers, the Fried Chicken (some of the best I've ever had), the Rice Roll Noodles with Beef, and The Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts. If you look at my photos for Potluck on Yelp, you'll see shots of many of these dishes! 

At first, you may be confused by Potluck Club's menu (I certainly was). On their menu, each selection appears as a single-priced entrée. I thought it was confusing because it didn't clearly lay out how many people each dish truly serves. I later learned, however, that they adjust the pricing incrementally based on the number of individuals in your group. So, in the end, it all works out. I just wish they had listed the selections as "price per person," so it would have been easier to sort out.

Note that, currently, Potluck Club only serves beer and wine. I surely hope they get a full bar liquor license at some point.

Final thoughts: I really, really enjoyed Potluck Club, and I cannot wait to return (with a group).

We're definitely coming back for the dinner menu! This restaurant and menu draws on inspiration from growing up in Chinatown. Coming into this restaurant was like watching a film of my early childhood. Although I'm surprised that the well-known canned dace fish with black bean isn't on display lol. I was so impressed with everything we ordered and definitely have it on my planner to go again for the dinner menu! Our favorite was the HK condensed milk french toast followed by the fried chicken sandwich. The cocktails were also light and refreshing. Service was fantastic. Loved everything!!

***Closer to at 4.8***

Finally made it out to Potluck Club! I originally tried to snag a walk in with a friend but we didn't check their website and they were closed to prep for their Lunar New Year event. 

Was on Resy searching for a lunch review with I saw some dinner slots available! Snagged a 3 person table for 8:15 PM same day. 

Love the inside vibe of the place! Some cute additions like a vending machine that housed classic treats/remedies from my childhood. When you open the flap, there's fortune cookies! So cute. 

What we tried-

Endive Salad:
Our waitress highly recommended this salad and gave us the pro tip to order the chicken and eat it with the salad. Thankfully we were already planning to get the chicken dish. I was skeptical about this dish. It sounded like it had a lot going on and I was worried it would be bitter. This blew me out of the water! Sweet, savory, sour and a slight tang of bitter. It was delicious and crisp. Definitely order this! 

Spicy Eggplant:
The sauce was a nice consistency and was reminiscent of mapo tofu. Didn't seem too spicy to me. Eggplant was really soft, a little too soft for my liking. Still enjoyed this dish! The crispy shallot bits were yummy.

Salt & Pepper Chicken w/ Scallion Biscuits:
Probably their most iconic dish. This was delicious! Nice, juicy pieces of chicken with crispy skin. My friend thought this was the best fried chicken, she was impressed! Came with 2 scallion biscuits with an option to add more for $. Enjoyed the biscuit but the chili sauce/jam it came with wasn't for me. 

Oyster Mushroom Rice Rolls:
We opted to add hanger steak to this dish. I was also a bit skeptical about this dish. I was worried there wouldn't be enough flavor and another Yelper said it was reminiscent of chee cheong fun but not as good. I was impressed with this dish! Nice caramelized pieces of rice rolls. Hanger steak was yummy and so were the mushrooms! Wish there were more mushrooms though, we couldn't find much of them in the dish. Would def order this again too! 

Tiger Shrimp w/ Walnuts:
If you're expecting honey walnut shrimp, this is not it. I was excited to try this thinking it was. It's nice big prawns but the sauce is more like bang bang sauce/spicy aioli. I was hoping for more sweet! Shrimp were cooked nicely but I would skip this next time. 

Pineapple Pineapple Soft Serve:
Dole whip with bolo bun crumbles. This was good! I'm not a huge fan of pineapple but still enjoy the flavor and texture of the soft serve. It's also vegan which we didn't know! The crumbles were good, wish there were more and bigger chunks. 

Milk Tea Tiramisu:
This was a special dessert of the night. I liked this more than the soft serve! Didn't really taste the milk tea flavor though. There were also almonds which I liked but I think they should give a heads up that it comes with nuts in case people have allergies. 

We also tried a variety of drinks. Note that they don't serve cocktails, just beer/wine/NA. We tried the Landlady & Old Man Chiu (NA) both were refreshing. We also tried Hummy seltzers (Soju based) for the first time and really enjoyed them! 

Our waitress was also super sweet, attentive and great at her job. She was quick to give recommendations, give us more info and we did not feel rushed at all. Shout out to her!

I would give this a 5 stars but the only thing stopping me was that not every dish we tried was amazing, but a majority of them were! Definitely will go again since there were some menu items that I missed and wanted to try! I def recommend this restaurant! Give it a try and make sure to make a reservation (they do take walk-ins for the bar seating and chefs counter but it's limited).

I simply cannot say enough good things about this place! The design is super cool and unique, the service is awesome and the food is absolutely delicious! Definitely make sure to try the salt & pepper chicken, endive salad and short rib. Highly recommended!
Wonderful experience at Potluck Club. Server was so sweet and made excellent recommendations. Food was outstanding. Highly recommend the potstickers and tiger shrimp

Run don't walk to this spot! This twist on traditional Chinese dishes was on point. Everything had its own twist and I loved it! The drinks were also amazing. Order the landlady, which had both fresh strawberries and pickled plum. Fries are crispy and salty. The hash was real star though. 10/10 on everything.

Solid brunch menu! I enjoyed my pork belly and egg sandwich, and got to try some of the salt & pepper chicken sandwich (also very good) and the HK french toast. All were definitely on the sweet side - the french toast, which had a salted egg yolk filling, was overall so sweet that I would not recommend just having that by itself. For the pricing (~$20 each) I thought the sandwiches could have been larger with fewer fries as filler on the side. 

I personally think the restaurant's beautiful and cohesive theme is the best part - an elegant, retro aesthetic of classic Hong Kong cinema. When it comes to the brunch food I think there may have been a slight case of style over substance, but the dinner menu looks absolutely mouthwatering and seems more popular so I would come back to try that.

Loved how creatively delicious the food, friendly and excellent service and the cultural atmosphere was at the Potluck Club! We were seated promptly with a dinner reservation once we arrived. Our waitress was extremely kind and helpful in suggesting what we should try our first time there. Of course, do try the tiger shrimp with walnuts, and salt and pepper fried chicken w scallion biscuits! The tiger shrimp has a little bit of a chipotle sauce so has a kick but not bad at all. It comes with soft broccoli and cauliflower bites and candied walnuts, which paired well with the shrimp! There are about 6-8 jumbo shrimps per order which can be shared. The salt and pepper fried chicken was pretty standard (crunchy out and tender in), dip it in the bbq-esque sauce. We also ordered the pork chives dumplings and loved how it with the savory chili sauce. Each dish is slightly on the pricier end (minimum ~$20). The only thing to recommend is a side of complementary rice. Overall, highly recommend for dinner hangout!!!

This Cantonese inspired restaurant is super nostalgic of our childhood but in a more upscale and upgraded version.  It's a set menu, and it's pricy, but the value is really good, in my opinion, since there's so much variety. I loved every single dish that was placed infront of my face. I loved the vibe, and I loved the atmosphere. The transparent kitchen concept and the whole layout are so nice. We were there for a birthday party and it was so much fun. I would definitely go back. Service is amazing, but there is a time limit to how long you can stay.

Came here with high expectations as I've seen and heard the hype. The food was mediocre... but the service and ambiance were great. There was a lot of aesthetic throughout... almost experiential. 

The service was great, they were prompt and attentive and all worked together instead of one server per table. 

The food is the most disappointing. The pot stickers and salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits is the only thing I'd get from here again... if I ever came back. 

The short rib was very disappointing.. the squash was dry and there was virtually no sauce in the dish. The oyster mushrooms were really unique and good - think of individual strands of drunken noodles rolled up.... It eventually did get boring and heavy that's why I didn't include it up there with the re-ordered stuff. And my boyfriend got a fried rice to go and he said it was unique... he can't necessarily say it was good or bad.... He emphasized on how it's different.

Came here for brunch finally! My partner and I were so excited to try. First off, coming in the place is so inviting, great ambience, amazing playlist of early 2000s hits if that's your jam (was mine). Staff was so helpful / friendly / attentive. Made the experience so amazing right off the bat. 

Now for the food:

Drinks: 9/10
sake cocktail - was a little sweet but SO REFRESHING. would absolutely get again as it was balanced and went perfectly with our meal. 

French toast: 10/10 this was just pure heaven. The toast was just crispy enough on the edges and SO soft in the middle with the yolk surprise. The condensed milk wasn't too much at all. Overall if you're looking for a sweet treat - THIS IS IT 

chicken sandwich: 9/10 SO crispy and juicy when you bite into it. The aioli is such a nice touch with the peppery arugula. To make this 10/10 though I added their Chili oil and made it chefs kiss 

Chow mein 9/10: noodles were crispy on some areas, flavorful, the meat was at some points too overcooked for me but wasn't a huge deal breaker. The overall flavor with the grilled green onions was honestly my favorite and no need for the meat. To make even better recommend putting the chili oil!  

Am absolutely coming back for the service, vibes, and food. Can't wait to try for dinner!

Really loved the vibes at this restaurant. It's bright, well decorated, and feels very upbeat. The service was also good. The menu is small, and as a group of 6, we were able to try almost everything. 

Endive salad (4/5) 
Pretty expensive for a salad with no meat, but it was very aesthetically pleasing. Flavor was decent, but nothing amazing. 

Salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits (5/5)
This dish was very solid. The chicken was very juicy, and the breading was super crispy and flavorful. It also went really well with the chili plum jam, which added a touch of sweetness. I liked the scallion biscuits, although felt they were a little heavy and slightly doughy.

XO fried rice (5/5)
Personally really liked this dish, although other people at the table thought it was underwhelming. I thought it had a really great umami, Smokey flavor and loved the balance with the sweetness of the corn and Chinese sausage. 

Oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (5/5)
Waiter said this was his favorite dish, and I can definitely see why. The rice rolls were fresh and chewy, and perfectly coated in the sweet and savory sauce. Mushrooms were well cooked, and we also added the steak, which was nice and tender as well. 

Tiger shrimp with walnuts (4/5)
I thought this one was a little overpriced, since it only came with 6 shrimp, although each shrimp was pretty big. I personally prefer the more traditional honey walnut shrimp to this version, which was less sweet, less saucy, and more spicy, although other people at my table really liked this.

Crispy drunken chicken with shrimp chips (3/5)
Definitely our least favorite entrée. The chicken was a little bland and didn't feel like anything special. The shrimp chips were also a little confusing since they didn't really seem to go with the chicken. 

Spicy eggplant (3/5)
Didn't really like this one either. Traditional Chinese Yu Xiang style eggplant (鱼香茄子) is much better imo. This one was pretty bland and a little too oily. 

Overall, most of the dishes were pretty solid and worth a try. Definitely an interesting departure from traditional Chinese/asian food, although some were underwhelming. It's on the pricier side for Asian food, although you're also paying for the ambiance and vibes.

Interesting themy spot in LES.
The space is huge and the layout provides different dining experience which is fun.

Friendly staffs.

No liquor nor cocktails, but serving wine.

We only tried 2 dishes -
*Mushroom Rice Roll Stir Fry - pretty good. Wish there's more crispy parts of the rice roll or more vegetable.
*Crispy Drunken Chicken - I'm not a chicken fan but this is executed pretty well. Slightly salty but good for sharing.

Menu is small but I guess they tried to perfect each dish.

Most likely I'll visit back!

Good vibes, bad food

Exactly what you would expect from a modernized spot

Lava toast $15 4.5/5 expensive but tasty

Salt and Pepper Chicken Burger $21 2/5 pale and bland fries (McD does it better) and the burger was mid 
Pot Luck Chow Mein $22 1/5 so salty and the hanger steak was chewy and gamey

Yin Yeung $6 1/5 flavorless and watery

Cute HK movie theme but go literally anywhere else in CTown to eat Chinese food
Food was excellent. Felt the service could have been a bit stronger. Bathroom is cold.

This was really excellent. We went with a group of four and ordered most of the menu: potstickers, tiger shrimp, salt & pepper chicken, short ribs, fried rice, rice noodles + steak, snow pea shoots, and pineapple soft serve for dessert. Every single item was great, with the biggest star (and thing I'll be thinking about until next time we come) was the rice noodles with mushroom and hangar steak, which is worth the visit on its own. Of the others, I'd probably try the eggplant over the snow pea shoots next time, and might actually skip the short ribs, which was the only dish that wasn't as otherwordly as I expected. I'd also consider skipping dessert next time, only because there's such amazing dessert at other places in that neighborhood. The chicken, shrimp, potstickers, and fried rice are all very strong re-order candidates.

Vibes and aesthetic were great and perfect for grabbing dinner with friends. The plates were all shareable and got a variety for our table. Food was good, nothing stood out. 

We got the 
- potstickers (which were our least favorite)
- salt and pepper chicken (was our favorite, the pepper jam and biscuits were a great flavor combo) 
- rice rolls with steak (these were also really good and flavorful) 
- spicy eggplant (was more sweet than spicy)

Very trendy and popping, vibes were great. But food was pretty average, they have some good in on the menu but nothing tasted all that much beyond average. Would recommend going at least once for the experience, but idk if I'd go again

Incredible spot. Every single thing we ordered - drinks / apps / entrées / dessert was absolutely delicious. I HIGHLY recommend getting one of the mocktails as they were super refreshing and not too sweet!

We shared the endive salad and it was the perfect app to get us started. Crunchy, flavorful, and light. We then shared the oyster mushroom noodles, fried chicken, walnut shrimp, and fried rice and they were all incredible. FYI the shrimp and chicken were both heavy due to the breading, but the flavor was amazing on both. The chicken and the fried rice were my personal winners!

The vibe of the place is open and inviting, and the staff was super nice. It's brightly lit up and has a bit of a escalated-diner vibe. My only advice is to allot a good amount of time for your meal as the service could be a bit slow at times, and also book a reservation ahead of time!

We ordered the entire menu and every single dish was delicious!  Short ribs so tender, fried chicken crispy, nicely battered, shrimps slightly spicy, curry tofu very flavorful and more!  did not have one favorite because they were all amazing!  Spacious, cool decor, wonderful vibe and a great service team.  Highly recommended!

Not sure why I didn't try this place earlier. The food was so good. Staff was super nice!!!
We tried the short rib - banging. Had the fried chicken with the scallion biscuit (brilliant combination!) and the ginger chicken. All in great portion. 
The place also has a great happy hour vibe to it. 
I bought my 5 yo daughter and no one was staring at me (to give foodie parent some perspective :) my daughter also enjoyed the pineapple sundae. 
Will return many times!

Decided on a last minute adventure out to the concrete jungle for brunch and landed potluck club. As we've had dinner here previously, we were interested if the brunch would match the Ah-mazing dinner and it did not disappoint.  The staff was welcoming, friendly and showed a love for the establishment you don't usually come across. The ambiance is reminiscent of days gone by in Chinatown with the Chinese theaters. I half expected Kurt Russel to break out into Big Trouble in this Little China. The way the chefs were able to blend textures and flavors of Asian and American is more than artistic and bordering magical. The Hong Kong French toast and bolo bao is a classic example of such. The blueberry longan jam was as soft and airy as the French toast itself. Sweet yet not overpowering. We did not feel too heavy after this smorgasbord. Sunny side eggs over radish cakes with the bacon flavor bomb was a favorite of the kids as well. Potluck chow mein a throwback to days of finishing dim sum with my grandparents.  Fried chicken was perfectly crispy and juicy. There's too much to say in such a little post much like how they are able to fit so much goodness in this establishment. Will end by saying we will def be back.  And the drinks were da bomb.

Delicious take on a fusion Hong Kong Cafe! Thoroughly enjoyed the food but definitely excited to try the dinner menu. The vibes and decor were immaculate, and service was great.

- Hong Kong French Toast ($15): sweet with that savory salted egg kick, wish it was a little softer though! but really liked it
- Potluck Chow Mein ($22): crunchy and soft noodles with tender beef, good with the chili oil 

The milk tea coffee was also great! Looking forward to returning.

Nice ambience, very cute and chic. Food was delicious. Loved the Hong Kong French toast. Went for brunch would like to try dinner to try the pineapple soft serve. They were show to accommodate us without a reservation on a busy Saturday.

I definitely should have trusted my gut on this one. Potluck Club is a great concept, but didn't deliver for me. 

When my girlfriend and I arrived, it took several minutes for us to be greeted and then another 5 minutes for us to be seated even though we had a reservation and tables were open and available. 

The food is average at best and in no way as good as what social media makes it out to be. Think traditional dishes with an upscale and expensive twist without the quality. 

Overall, this place was a big miss for me. I expected more.

3.5 but I round up. I think this place is very good for western palates and as an introduction for Asian food, but I feel like as someone who grew up eating Cantonese food, it kind of missed the mark. 

The salt and pepper chicken was dry to me and not juicy enough, and it lacked more salt and pepper oomph. It just tasted too much like regular fried chicken for me. I did like the jam though, that had a lot of flavor. The biscuits were nice, but as scallion biscuits, they didn't taste strongly of scallion at all. That being said, I still love a good biscuit, which they delivered if you're not expecting any scallion. All the Asian flavors seem really, really, mild, except for the jam, which was disappointing. 

The tiger shrimp was better - I see some reviews saying that it was spicy, but I got none of that in mine. It was drenched in aioli and the shrimp were plump, but I think I was really looking forward to a sweet kick to the dish, which this lacked. As it is a take of the traditional honey walnut shrimp dish, I was really hoping for some kind of sweetness, but it didn't have that. Still, a good dish! I loved the veggies with it. 

The service is lovely and the ambiance is great, there's a great display vending machine with all of these Chinese trinkets and treats, as well as super popular Chinese movie posters from the 00s. 

I think I had higher expectations or just different expectations for this restaurant, but if you're just trying out some Cantonese food, this is still a wonderful place to go to!

TL;DR - Cool concept, come expecting Asian fusion.

Food (5/5) - All dishes were canton-inspired but not classic. Walk in expecting Asian fusion and you're good to go.

We ordered a bunch of dishes to share but I appreciated the jellyfish salad (this is just quite hard to find, to be honest) and the salt and pepper chicken the most. The chicken was served with chili oil that had a dash of honey in it, thought it evened out very well - and the chicken itself was quite juicy, and the skin was crispy / well fried.

We also tried the pineapple soft serve that had pineapple bun topping / crumble on it. I liked the slight savoury touch.

Service (5/5) - Quick, unintrusive and very helpful with recommendations.

Ambiance (4/5) - Really, really liked the decor! I'm from Hong Kong and everything reminded me of home, from the fake vending machine, to the landscape wallpaper, to the decorated tiles. It was very unique. That being said, it was quite loud and tables were seated quite close. Found myself shouting at times.

Price (4/5) - Portions were on the smaller end though prices were largely affordable, 15-25 per shared dish.

I had a great dining experience at Potluck Club! I walked in on a weekend with a party of 4 right when the restaurant was opening, and everyone there was super kind and accommodating. We were seated almost immediately, which was a great start to the evening.

The restaurant was decorated beautifully and was full of people, which created a lively and welcoming atmosphere. They also had a great selection of mocktails and cocktails to choose from.

We ordered several dishes, including the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, oyster mushroom rice roll noodles, the tofu special, and the crispy drunken chicken with shrimp chips. Everything we tried was absolutely delicious and the portion sizes were great. 

I highly recommend Potluck Club for anyone looking for an amazing dining experience. The food was outstanding, the service was exceptional, and the ambiance was lively and fun. It's the perfect spot for a night out with friends, and I can't wait to come back!

I came here to celebrate my close friend's engagement and she recommended this place to us. I made reservations on resy it's a 90 min limit eating time, which is already long enough time to eat. Our reservations was for 6:45pm today, we were seated immediately. The staff was really sweet and open to giving us recommendations on the menu and some off the menu items that wasn't on the menu. We ended up getting the zo fried rice, salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, it already came with two but if you wanted to add another one it would've been an extra $3. The off the menu item we got was the coconut curry tofu, bravo it was so delicious! The oyster mushroom rice noodles + hanger steak was phenomenal it was definitely very flavorful. My top two favorites has to be the coconut curry and the oyster mushrooms, I was honestly just a huge fan of it. The decor inside is so freaking cute, I was fascinated about how cool it looked inside they even had like pictures of very old Chinese movies on the wall and a huge wall paper of bruce lee, I was just loving it all. Highly recommended! I would definitely go back to try other items on the menu! The menu is very small too!

It's always busy when we try to eat here!
This is our third attempt without reservations. Third time is the charm.

The servers were very friendly, can speak English and Cantonese. We were able to get a table but there were seats at the chefs' counter (there's hooks for your bag underneath the counter-- in front of your stool).

We ordered three entrees.
- Salt & Pepper Chicken with scallion biscuits: the chicken are really crispy and the biscuits tasted like Popeyes' biscuits. You can add additional biscuits for $3
- XO Fried Rice: taste like nostalgia. You can add tea egg for $3
- Oyster mushroom with rice roll noodles: Delicious! We added hanger steak for $8 but you cannot tell whether you're eating the steak or oyster mushroom until you bite into it.

The place has cute designs and there are 3 bathroom stalls in the back.

When you pay at the end they give you a post card with an individually wrapped Japanese gummy candy.

Would recommend coming here but make reservations beforehand because this place gets packed!

Really enjoyed all the food here. Strong dishes included dumplings with chili oil, oyster mushroom rice rolls, eggplant dish. Unfortunately, least favorite were the pea shoots. I usually love sautéed pea shoots, but the slightly sweet sauce they used were not my fave. Worst dish was the milk tea tiramisu. 

Overall, loved the fun modern takes on Chinese dishes and the atmosphere matched. Great spot and will definitely return to try more dishes. I've got my eye on that fried chicken.
Banger restaurant, amazing people and food! I highly suggest the tiger walnut shrimp, an updated classic.

Food is so delicious and loved the vibes with their awesome playlist! Really enjoyed the oyster mushroom rice rolls, XO fried rice, salt & pepper chicken & special curry tofu appetizer!  Loved that it's family style and got to try a bit of everything, which had so much flavor!  Staff was very friendly and attentive, they do have a time limit, but was able to get the tiramisu dessert & finish our drinks. Will be back again!

I would strongly recommend coming to this restaurant. The ambiance is lovely. The staff is kind and the food is GREAT. 

I can recommend the pot stickers, the endive salad, and the yellow tail crust.

This place lives up to the hype. It has top notch Chinese dishes with a modern spin and decor. Definitely a vibey restaurant in the best way possible. Service is also phenomenal as the hostess and servers are extremely friendly.

Came here with a group of 5 and ordered the pork and chive potstickers, fried chicken with scallion biscuits, XO fried rice, oyster mushroom rice noodle rolls, coconut curry tofu, and tiramisu dessert. Everything was seriously fantastic! The fried rice and curry were my favorites, but truly nothing was a miss. Even the drinks were great, but they don't have any cocktails (just wine, beer, and hard seltzers). There was a Hong Kong beer that my husband really liked. 

You can tell they were very thoughtful to have this represent a homey and comfortable spot for Chinese culture as they have a lot of items and decor that remind me of childhood. They combined that with some cool and edgy twists to make it modern. Food quality and creativity will definitely have me coming back to try everything on the menu.

I LOVE this place!!! Both times I've been they've seated me at the chef's counter immediately (even on busy nights), and the food has been stellar.

We had the oyster rice roll noodles (5/5) and the endive salad (5/5), both AMAZING. The salad was composed beautifully, the dressing was perfect and the fruits contrasted the bitterness of the endive. The rice roll noodles were just the right consistency and the sauce was light and flavorful.

We also had the curried tofu (4.5/5), great flavor but wasn't particularly unique, and the XO fried rice vegetarian, which we liked a bit less than the other dishes (but they customized it vegetarian for us which was very sweet).

For dessert we had the milk tea coffee tiramisu, beautifully light.

Also the place is STUNNING, gorgeous interiors and we loved the service and ambiance. Also my boyfriend is allergic to nuts and they were so accommodating. We'll definitely be back!!

If I could give this place more than 5 stars, I definitely would! It's super rare that authentic chinese food + decent ratings come in hand, and even when a place checks off both boxes, it's usually a pretty dingy place (especially if it's in the midst of chinatown). But this place does both and has a really aesthetic cute modern vibe - definitely check out their bathrooms (they were so cute and it felt like you were in an aquarium!)

I came in expecting a ton of small eats and a family style menu, but their lunch menu actually featured more American sized portions and servings. There weren't too many options which made life a lot easier! I went with the salt and pepper chicken burger and it was amazing. It was the perfect amount of crispy, salty, and sweet and it wasn't that greasy. It was served in a egg-washed brioche bun that had a slightly sweet tang to it too! The portions are enormous, and I'd subsituted the fries for a side salad, which definitely made the serving size a bit more doable. My friend ordered the radish cake with eggs and it was such a unique dish though it could have used a bit more radish cake (the radish cake was just tossed around in the salad - I was expecting more of a radish cake base for the eggs).

Great ambiance, and decor. Would definitely come again and try their other dishes (they had pineapple baos which I didn't get a chance to try)! Very reasonable pricing (around 25 for an entree)

What a gem to Chinatown. This is what it's all about. How to respect the culture and take it forward at the same time. Cory, Ricky, and the team are doing something so amazing for the community. The store design is just beautiful. A great layout with so many little great details. And the food wow. Just one of my favorite meals of my NYC trip. The Jellyfish salad and endive salad were mind-blowing. And yes I'm saying that about a salad dish. The salt & pepper chicken with biscuits is a must order. The chili-plum jam is so addicting. I need jars of that back home. The mushroom rice roll noodles were really good. Great texture. The XO fried rice is a must! I didn't have one bad option here. The service was also on it. They took great care of us. Very fun and forwarding menu. Cheers to Potluck Club

Recommendation: Salt & Pepper chicken w/ biscuits, Endive salad, rice roll noodles.

Came here for brunch and loved the interior. I appreciated the dedication to concept and design and the nostalgic aspects of it. We got the salt and pepper chicken sandwich, pork belly sandwich, Hong Kong french toast, and radish cake hash as well as the Hong Kong coffee milk tea. The sandwiches also came with french fries which were nicely made. Overall, it's a good fusion spot for those craving Cantonese food.

I have not written a Yelp review in a LONG LONG time but I had to come back on here to write this. From the moment you walk into this establishment, you notice all the details.  Every item welcomes you.  They say, a great restaurant is not just about the food but also the experience.  I can say, that this place is that and much more.  So so so happy such a place exists! The food to get is the rice rolls with mushrooms and please don't forget to add the steak.  They have DOLE soft serve for dessert!!! What a treat! Extra points when you find Jackie in the bathroom  ;)

I've been wanting to try Potluck Club since it opened and I finally got to go.

The food is really tasty here and the ambiance adds to the experience.

My absolute favorite dish was the oyster mushroom rice rolls -- delicious!

I want to come back and try their other dishes, specially the walnut shrimp and the salt&pepper chicken.

Cute restaurant with great decor. Very busy - I'd recommend a reservation.

Food is good - the salt and pepper chicken was kind of dry. But the rice rolls, pea shoots, and shrimp were great. 

Service is kind. Food comes out a bit slow and not altogether. 

It's just super loud.
The food and the service were excellent. The ambiance was unique and pleasing to the eye. A really great experience!
Good fusion food that is well thought of and balanced, with resemblance of hk style food.

I came to Potluck Club hearing a lot of hype and was glad to find that it lived up to its expectations. 

We booked somewhat of a last minute same-day reservation here and were seated promptly on arrival. There were so many things I had heard about trying but we ended up trying the endive salad, oyster rice rolls with hanger steak, and tiger shrimp. All dishes were fantastic. The endive salad was particularly unique with its variety of textures and flavors - not sure if I had had something like this before. The oyster rice rolls were hot, savory, umami. The tiger shrimp - albeit a bit pricy, was delicious and probably bite for bite my favorite of the meal. The only critique I have of the actual dishes we got was that I wish the rice rolls themselves had a tiny bit more texture to them (like tasting multiple rolls/sheets of the rice rolls in my mouth instead of just a chewy rice cake) but honestly that's a pretty minor gripe in the grand scheme of things. I also tried a Chinese beer that was supposed to be tea-infused -- didn't get the tea flavor so much but it was good nonetheless! We ended with the pineapple soft serve which was just ok, but in no way detracted from our fantastic experience.

Service was excellent, very friendly, considerate, and efficient. Can't really expect any better from this standpoint. I have to come back to experience brunch here sometime. Can't wait!

Love the environment of the place - it's like a blast to Hong Kong. We walked in around 8pm on a Thursday evening and was seated quickly right after some table cleaning. Service was quick and food came out quickly. 

We ordered two mains and one dessert for two people:
-oyster mushroom rice roll noodles: I love oysters and I love rice rolls. However, this dish may need a side of rice. By itself, the dish is way too salty but it is good overall. 
-salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits: The scallion biscuits were soft and tasty and the scallion chili plum jam was amazing that I wish I could get bottles of it!  The chicken however, breading was too thick and too crunchy for a lot of it that it hurt to chew. 
-tiramisu (earl grey I believe): could use more earl grey flavor but it was pretty good and not too sweet

Portion sizes were decent. We came out of that meal very stuffed. 

Tip: Look for the surprise in the vending machine!
Beautiful indoor decor and pretty yummy food. The Dole Whip is a MUST! The perfect pineapple flavor with a small twist: bolo bao (pineapple bun) crumbs which add the perfect crunch!

I loved the fusion concept behind the food and this restaurant! I very much enjoyed seeing how my Cantonese/Chinese heritage was celebrated while still incorporating Western elements. When I first entered, I found immediate connection with the classic HK films, comics, and herbal remedies showcased on the walls. I loved the vintage-y/retro cinema decor in the front with more street style vendor 大排档 vibes in the back. 
Their food was also DELICIOUS! My absolute favorite was their hong kong french toast. The name may fool you a little bit because while its not "authentic" (aka french toast in HK is not made like this), it is novel and yummy! I loved the incorporation salted egg yolk - in a melty, lava form!! It really came running out when I cut the toast open and each bite was a little mixture of sweet condensed milk, chewy bread, and the egg-y flavors from the salted egg yolk mixture. 
The salt & pepper chicken sandwich was also very tasty! Appreciate how their chicken was very nicely marinated and had that shaoxing wine flavor. It was fried in a nice light but crispy batter which went really well with their green aioli and arugula. I also enjoyed the eggs over radish cake hash and the caesar salad with a tea egg but with a molten yolk. Their yeen yeung was a little watered down for me but I still enjoyed my overall dining experience!
Had to get a late reservation for the weekend but service was pretty solid and food came quick! Their menu isn't super big but I definitely want to come back to try other things!

To start off, the ambience and decor of the place is very tastefully done! It's quite loud, but I can see this place being a fun place to get dinner with friends.

I was a little disappointed by the food. I was looking forward to the salt and pepper chicken and biscuits dish, but the chicken was a bit dry and the biscuits too underbaked, resulting in a mushy texture that stuck to the roof of my mouth. The chili-plum oil it came with was delectable, however, and added a nice sweet spice to the rest of the dish. 

The endive salad was also just ok, and the xo fried rice was too salty. 

If you're craving Chinese food, I would go somewhere else.

Potluck Club has been on my list for months and I'm so glad I finally had the chance to visit.

Before I got there, I skimmed through reviews pre planning what I'd order and foolishly on my part, I totally missed that brunch had a different menu and everything I prepicked was from the dinner menu! It ended up working out bc we enjoyed everything we ordered.

Salt & Pepper Chicken Sandwich with fries: we were kind of worried the chicken would be dry but it was actually really moist! The aioli also helped make sure every bite was perfectly moist. It also came with a huge amount of fries.

Potluck Chow Mein: my boyfriend LOVED the steak. I enjoyed this dish too and it's a pretty hefty portion size. I also liked the chili oil that came with it on the side!

Hong Kong French Toast: I'll never say no to salted egg yolk. We actually got this item for free (kitchen made an extra one by accident) and while we liked it, it was our least favorite of the bunch. It's a bit small for $15.

Both my boyfriend and I agreed that Potluck Club exceeded our expectations and we'd be back to try out dinner sometime!

Went on friday night for dinner w my girl friends after seeing tiktok going crazy for the food here!! we ordered plates to share OBVIOUSLY by the title - its family style

upon entering the ambiance is really cool here kinda like an adult movie theater theme. nailed the decor and lighting

the staff was insanely friendly too. we showed up on time for our reservation but weren't seated for about 15 minutes which tbh is fine esp since they were so cool about it. we immediately ordered when we sat the oyster noodles with hanger steak, fried rice, and chicken (salt and pepper)

guys the food was BUSSIN!!! really loved the biscuit with the chicken and the noodles were my fav!!! would recommend doing without the fried rice its nothing special. they even gave us complimentary dessert for a friends bday. love!! 10/10 would recommend + come back for brunch

Located in the lower Eastside adjacent to Chinatown , Potluck Club is a phenomenal restaurant that everyone should experience at least once. I would recommend making reservations, but they except walkins.We sat at, what I'm gonna call the kitchen bar where you can watch your food being made, and their kitchen is spotless. If I'm going to make any suggestions for food, it would definitely be the potstickers, salt and pepper fried chicken with scallion biscuits, and the mushroom rice roll noodles with steak.  They also specialize in nonalcoholic drinks, the landlady and old man Chiu are refreshing and delicious. The landlady is strawberry based and the old man Chiu is citrus based. The service was fast ,friendly and efficient. I would highly recommend this restaurant. Sidenote, they open up at 5:30 to 10 and closed on Mondays and Tuesdays.

This was an incredible dining experience! The food was amazing and the service  was so accommodating (gluten free, nut allergies, vegetarian). Cory was our waiter and he was great!!!! 10/10 experience highly recommend.

I have to say that this place was bustling with a lot of people constantly going in and out. (They are open from Wednesday to Sunday from 5:30-9pm.) I can see why there are people of all ages here as the interior of the place is nice and the music was pumping. Plus the exceptional service. They could use more servers, but they did their best. We tried to make reservations in advance, but nothing was available, so we decided to do a walk-in. Once we checked in at this cute booth, my name was put in a list, and a text message was sent. I was told it would be a 45-minute wait. However, it wasn't that long as it ended up being around 15 to 20 minutes. It paid off to wait by the front where they could see us. 

We got a table instead of the counter, and that was nice. We did sit right by the air conditioner, and it was so cold, and they fixed that for us right away and redirected it away from the table to the ceiling. I wasn't too pleased by the wait to get our order taken, but the waitress profusely apologized. She was very attentive afterward even though we didn't complain. The dishes that we ordered were the potstickers, which was pretty amazing as it had pork and chives inside of it. Got two mains, which were the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles with hanger steak and the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. The chili plum jam complimented the biscuits. I also got the jade scorpion, which I was told is the most popular drink ordered. It tasted like a blue moon, and I enjoyed that beer, so that was good. The waitress said that since our order was taken so late that the dessert was given on the house. The dessert was a Dole pineapple with bolo bao crumble (pineapple bun). We ate that ice cream really fast and didn't leave a drop unfinished. All in all, it was a good meal and great service!

Amazing amazing food, best pea shoots I've ever had at a Chinese restaurant. The chicken is flavorful and the scallion biscuits are so fun with the chili jam. Xo fried rice was addicting. Friendly service, cool mocktails and love the Hk cinema decor

One of the best dining experiences I've ever had. The design and atmosphere of the restaurant is excellent but the food is next level. The pork belly and egg sandwich has to be the best egg sandwich I've ever had and the endive salad with salt pepper chicken (which our awesome server recommended) is exceptional, totally unexpected flavor combinations that mix perfectly. The French toast offerings are extremely good and like no French toast I've had before.
Can't wait to go back as there were so many other things I'm dying to try.
Cannot recommend highly enough!

Love the vibe at this joint, fun and energetic atmosphere with super great service! 

Hubby and I came in for a quick bite on Saturday and the place was packed! Luckily we were able to be seated right away at the chef's counter without reservation. 

I have high expectations after seeing all the hypes but was underwhelmed by the food. We ordered the Hong Kong French Toast and Potluck Chow Mein. The center part of the salted egg york lava french toast was alright but the rim was hard, I never had HK French Toast with such hard/chewy rim. As for the Chow Mein, it was tasty but too much sweetness on the sauce they use/make. Coffee milk tea was okay but hubby didn't like the lemon tea. 

Overall, we enjoyed the venue and service, but sadly not so much on the food.

This is such a well done restaurant! From the decor and vibe to the specialized menu, it was a really enjoyable meal.

We were able to walk in for a party of 2 with about a 25 minute wait. The waitress was so sweet and super helpful when ordering! 

The appetizer was really flavorful and refreshing. The rice rolls had just the right amount of chewiness. The tiger prawns were not the best I've had but super juicy and the shrimp was great quality. The chicken was well seasoned and had a great crunch; loved that there were some pickled jalapeños that paired so well with the chicken and biscuits

We are staying in New York for a week and we're researching places to go and the name and reviews of this fantastic restaurant got us excited to go, and it was really amazing!

We had their Chinese and Japanese beer selection, the favorite for me being the green peppercorn beer. Food was so delicious, which we watched from the seating by the kitchen. Service was really helpful, attentive, and we even got a complimentary dessert because our server thought they hadn't been attentive enough.

It was a lovely experience and I would love to go again!

Just went there today after reading reviews in the times Justin the owner real nice and the staff very friendly. Had endive salad rice noodles with mushrooms and steak and pineapple softserve all for a great price

All the dishes we ordered were delicious, but taking 1 star off because they were overpriced for the portions, service wasn't very attentive, and the restaurant was insanely cold. 

Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits - 4.5/5 delicious seasoning and smelled divine; the scallion biscuits were really unique with the plum jam

Snow Pea Shoots - 4/5 standard veggie dish, texture was nicely al dente

Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles - 5/5 best dish of the night; you can really taste the wok hei and the noodles were soft but springy 

Tiger Shrimp with Candied Walnuts - 4.5/5 probably the best tasting walnut shrimp variation I've had; the breading wasn't too thick, sauce was nice and creamy almost like spicy mayo, and the candied walnuts weren't too sweet. But the fact that this was $32 for 5 pieces of shrimp was a huge turnoff

Some of the mixed reviews and tepid NYT account by Pete Wells almost had me second guessing my own star rating, but Potluck Club hit all the right notes for me. The playful and modern twists on classic Cantonese dishes perfectly married my inclination toward comfort food with my desire for novel dining experiences.

Backlit Hong Kong movie posters and marquee lettering had me feeling like I stepped into a vintage Hong Kong theater, with no detail spared, including a pagoda-topped ticket tollbooth. There's even a [display] vending machine featuring traditional Hong Kong treats. The vending machine doesn't work and is just for show, but it does spit out fortune cookies and this simple pleasure brought me so much joy.

Onto the food-- the oyster mushroom rice rolls stole the show for me, with just the right amount of seasoning and the perfect amount of chew. Their walnut shrimp, XO fried rice, salt n pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, and endive salad were also all slam dunks for me. I only dined with one other person but felt I was able to sample a wide array of dishes, and yet there are still more I want to return to try, like the HK toast.

The cherry on top was the lone dessert on the menu, the pineapple soft serve. To me, this was more reminiscent of Disney World than it was the Chinese restaurants of my youth, but if the target demo for the Potluck Club are ABC's (American Born Chinese), then I fit squarely into it and they have me tied around their finger. Take a journey to old HK via a meal at Potluck Club and you'll see what I'm talking about.

Good servers, always serve you with smile and polite words.
Good foods, not too many items on the menu but all are tasty.
Good ambiance, love the design and the theme when I first stepped into the restaurant.

After seeing so many videos about this place, we finally were able to try this place for brunch on a Saturday. We got there around 12 and there were a lot of empty tables available. Host was a bit rude but maybe it was just an off day for him. We got seated at the counter so it was cool to see the chefs cook the food. The interior was really neatly decorated and love the posters of old school Hong kong movies. The playlist they had on was cool as well. We ordered yin yeung, salt and pepper chicken sandwich, salted egg yolk Hong Kong style French toast, chow mein. The best thing was the salt and pepper chicken- so crispy and flavorful and also the chili oil. Everything else was just ok.

Good food and service.  Liked the salt and petter fried chicken, with its very crunchy crust and juicy chicken, the tiger shrimp, and the pineapple pineapple soft serve.   Service was excellent.  Atmosphere was great too.

100% positive experience.

We walked in just before 7pm on a Sunday night, and was offered two seats at the chefs counter. I had hoped for a table but the counter turned out to be an excellent option. Comfy chairs, and a great view of chefs cooking up a storm. 

Endive salad - A HIGHLIGHT. Dragon fruit, grapefruit, pistachio, a mustard based tart dressing that I am willing to buy jars of. A light drizzle of olive oil and Parm. DELISH - so not miss.

Salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits - 10/10. The most crunchy fried deboned chicken, the scallions added so much flavor to the biscuit. It also came with this chili jam that was out of this world.

Tiger prawns with romanesco broccoli - solid

The pineapple ice cream - the fortune cookies were a great touch.

From peeks at other tables, the short ribs looks AMAZING, and the so did the noodles with mushrooms and steak. Next time, hopefully soon. 

Also the waiters and the host were all supremely organized as well as kind. Thank you!!

the interior of this restaurant was absolutely beautiful. all the decor was really creative

*salt & pepper chicken sandwich w/ french fries: the chicken was absolutely breathtaking, so crispy and super juicy.

*pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich w/ french fries: the egg made this sandwich the best, super soft and fluffy

*the land lady mocktail: this added a great highlight to our overall brunch. this drink has a fresh strawberries, salted plum and sprite. (definitely recommend getting this)

*my tips: make sure to create a reservation 

would I go again? Yes

Awesome cantonese-style Chinese food in the east village! The wait staff and service are incredibly friendly and welcoming. The interior is very aesthetic and cool. I appreciate that their menu isn't too extensive, it doesn't overwhelm you but at the same time you have some variety and options to choose from! Really enjoyed the chow mein and the HK toast. I will have to come back and try the other dishes such as the sandwiches!

CINEMATIC ! Theatrical vibes with modern Chinese tastes. Some would say CHIC. I'd say it's worth a visit for first time. Excellent service. 7/10 food, ABOVE average, on the PRICIER SIDE. 

Make reservations before coming, place is beyond packed on a Wednesday night.

Let's cut to the chase. Everything was great!
Rice Rolls with oyster mushroom and steak were such a hit. That's a must have every time.
The king prawns were so crispy and lathered in a sweet aioli! Soo good!
Short rib with the pumpkin was such a nostalgic dish to me. Every bite reminded me of a real Chinatown taste.
Also the fried salt n pepper chicken and biscuits!!! Don't question it. Just get it!! Cmon! It's fried chicken!!!  
Ordering was nice and easy. Good beer and wine. Concise menu and everything came in reasonable fashion. 
 As soon as it hit the table- chow was on!!!

I love the feel with the good music, decor that reminds me of all the movies I grew up watching and loads of hidden gems like the peephole and classic dim sum wall!

Didn't even make it past the door. We had drinks in our hands which I understand would not be allowed in certain restaurants but the way the host with tattoos and a hat on Friday addressed us was just uncalled for. Literally just stepped into the doors and the first words were "we don't allow that here". How is he allowed at the host stand?? Really wanted to give this place a try but after today, no thanks.

Dropped by for lunch/brunch on Sunday after seeing this spot pop up on socials and was not disappointed. The spritz was refreshing and easy to drink. Got the hong kong french toast to share and split the pork belly & egg sandwich and salt & pepper chicken sandwich. Between the two sandwiches, the chicken sandwich was more enjoyable (both of us agreed). The pork belly and egg was salty and sweet but the salt and pepper chicken hit the spot. Splitting the french toast was the way to go - sweet and slightly salty. When we cut into it, the salty egg yolk oozed out and was a sight to behold. The condensed milk topping gave it the sweet kick that it needed. Will come back again to try out their dinner menu!

It's funny how this Chinese restaurant is DISCRMINWTING ASIAN PEOPLE. 

When I walked in and asked for a table. The guy told me it's gonna be a 20 minutes wait, without asking me if it is okay to be the kitchen bar.

After 5 minutes, when a non-Asian group came in, he asked them if they are okay with the kitchen bar. And after 30 minutes wait, the guy asked me if I wanted to sit at the kitchen bar. I said no and he told me it would be another hour wait. So 

Seriously it's really fucked up. He could have told me in advance when I was expecting a table. So I just walked out and will never come back to this place again.

Okay, absolutely amazing...I was very very impressed in all aspects. First off the decor and vibe is very very well thought out -- old time Cantonese/Chinese pop vibes. Creates such a wonderful environment and you can tell a lot of thought was put in. The food...AMAZING. Fusion spots can kinda be hit or miss but I feel like potluck club took all the best aspects of iconic dishes and just amplified them. The biscuits and fried chicken were amazing -- definitely a must get. Perfectly cooked chicken and the MVP is the sauce...so freaking good. Walnut shrimp was also delicious, pretty hard to go wrong. Highly recommend and will be going back for sure.
A little pricey but the food was tasty and service was great. A cute place for a date night for sure. Make a reservation as they were packed on a Thursday.

I recently came here and already can't wait to come back. The dishes are essentially Chinese comfort food but with a special twist that makes it taste better somehow! The portions are decently big too, which is a plus. The interior is really fun and unique, with classic Chinese decor mixed with fun neon signs and posters.

I looooove potluck club and I cannot rave about it enough. The flavors here are solid. I wouldn't say it's a place to try experimental flavors, but rather a place for comfort and pure enjoyment. All the dishes we got were so so amazing. 

We also got a few beers and drinks and love how they incorporate some Asian flavors and partner with AAPI brands. I think this really sets up the tone for the restaurant and I always enjoy supporting the community. 

I also really love the interior decor of the entire restaurant. The waitstaff were really helpful and patient. I can't thank them enough for accommodating us. 

I would highly recommend making a reservation! I made mine about 2 weeks out for a table of 4 on a weekend.

hands down one of my favorites in all of nyc, from the interior to the food, i love it here!!!!! the menu is fairly small but it's perfect for a big group and indecisive people hehe 

the food: the absolute MUST orders are the endive salad and oyster mushroom rice rolls. endive salad is the most amazing explosive taste of your dreams!! also got the scallion biscuit salt and pepper chicken which was sooo good. my least favorites that were still yummy were the eggplant and walnut shrimp 

the interior: so cool and neon-trendy!!! 

the service: standard!

What a find!

I think this must be a trendy new place.  I didn't realize at the time but I was lucky to get a reservation because so many people tried to walk in for dinner and were told an hour and a half wait.

My friend and I started with the endive salad.  It was a decent portion!  I never thought I would spend $21 on endive, but they did give us a lot.  The oranges and passion fruit were a nice and refreshing touch.  The pistachios complimented the dish nicely.  I just wish there was more cheese!  The dressing was throughout the salad and was on every bite.

The oyster mushroom rice roll noodles were delicious.  They were nice and crispy with a good sauce on top.  There was also a good amount of mushrooms and asparagus.
