We also enjoyed the braised short ribs.  I almost wished we ordered a side of white rice to pour all of the sauce on top of it.  They were delicious and flavorful.

The service was great!  I was worried we wouldn't be out by the time the restaurant needed the table for their next seating, but it worked out.

I would only say that the restaurant is located in the street a bit, I almost walked right by it 

All in all I really enjoyed it and I would like to try some other items on the menu.
Came for brunch and was happy with each item ordered. Wait time was set for 30mins but was able to get a walk in seating within 20mins. Will be back to try the dinner menu.

We went for their brunch menu - the Salt & Pepper Chicken Sandwich and Hong Kong French toast are 2 MUST HAVES!! The Bolo Bao French toast was pretty good and unique too, but compared to the HK toast, it felt a bit drier. 

I'd skip the Sunny Side Eggs Over Radish Cake Hash, since it's basically egg with arugula. The Potluck Chow Mein and Pork Belly Cha Siu & Egg Sandwich were both just ok. 

The servers are very friendly and attentive, and the interior is very aesthetic! Overall would come back!!

I really wanted to like this place after I saw a video on YouTube about the restaurant and reading the reviews. 

That being said, I think the food here is really mediocre for high prices. We ordered the walnut shrimp which was 6 shrimps for 19$. I know this is New York but I felt like I had to eat toddler portions in order to not break the bank. The walnut shrimp was also slathered in mayonnaise, overly so. Fried rice was decent but nothing special. 

The ambiance was really unique and creative, which I liked. Service was great as well! But food is always the main thing and this place was really disappointing. There are a lot of other restaurants in the area that are delicious and not extremely overpriced.

The restaurant looks great but the serving sizes could be bigger for the prices that you're paying for. 

The dishes are reminiscent of classic Chinese dishes but you're in Chinatown and you can explore other options within the area for cheaper prices.

Great place if you're trying to pay entree prices for appetizer portions. $30 for 6 pieces of walnut shrimp didn't sit too well with me.  I'm confused as to why everything is supposedly "family style" (according to the menu) but you're basically getting tapas-sized servings. If you want classic Chinese family style and support OG businesses, just walk a couple more blocks.

Biscuits with the chili-plum jam were alright, but charging an additional $3 per is kinda wild (margins must be insane).

At the end of the day, you're paying for the aesthetic and a modern take of classic chinese dishes. Food was disappointing given the price point, nothing to write home about.  I don't seem to be the only person voicing my concerns about the portion size at this establishment, and I do hope that the owners take it into consideration.
Noodles, meat, decor, food - bravo. Still dreaming about these dishes because they were all so yummy. The restaurant had a really fun vibe and even a vending machine of fortune cookies!

The Potluck Club is a delightful establishment that beautifully combines American and Chinese flavors in a fusion cuisine. The moment you step inside, it becomes evident that they've put considerable thought and effort into the restaurant's design. With a spacious layout and meticulous attention to detail, it's easy to see why it has become the new hot spot in town.

From the very start, the service was outstanding. The staff was attentive, friendly, and truly added to the overall dining experience. Their attentiveness made us feel welcome and well taken care of, setting a positive tone for the meal.

Now, let's dive into the food. I decided to go for the Chasiu burger and the Old Manchius, and both dishes left a favorable impression. The drink I ordered was not only visually appealing but also deliciously refreshing, a perfect start to the meal. The Chasiu burger, while undeniably tasty, left me with one tiny wish - for it to be a bit bigger! The flavors were fantastic, but a heartier portion would have made it even more satisfying. The Old Manchius was a real treat, showcasing a creative fusion of flavors that left me eager to explore more of their menu.

In conclusion, I'm definitely planning to revisit the Potluck Club in the future. With such a warm and inviting atmosphere, exceptional service, and food that's nearly perfect (if only they'd super-size that burger!), it's a restaurant that warrants multiple visits to sample more of their intriguing menu. If you appreciate innovative fusion cuisine and a trendy dining environment, this spot should absolutely be on your list to explore.

The weekend brunch is recommended, the food is delicious and the decor is very unique to be in Chinatown.
You need to make a reservation before you go, we went without one and the lady that help us tried to accommodate us.
The staff was very friendly.

From the beautiful grand exterior and after watching their interview, I was excited to try this viral spot. But the moment the owner approached us and just stared at us waiting for US to speak first, my skepticism towards this place went up. If you're a walk-in, prepare for bar seating or what they call the chef's counter. He initially offered us a table until 6:45PM, but withdrew the offer after checking again.

I don't know what he was saying, but I saw that supposed unavailable table. And that table remained empty the duration of our meal.

The food was absurdly overpriced, ranging from $20-$30 for small portions. And if the dishes are meant to be shared, why are there so many bar seatings anyways? We were seated in the back and got to watch the chefs hard at work, but it was not comfortable dining with a bigger party. 

While I was fortunately full from the dishes, I was left needing several rounds of water from the high intake of sodium. They could have at least thrown in bowls of rice if they wanted to keep some form of Cantonese tradition in this. 

Price aside, the food was good, but salty. I can't stand by pretentious restaurants who think their popularity could excuse the need for kind service.

I believe this restaurant has potential to improve. I was hyped to check out this place after watching their interview on YouTube and learning about their story. As a customer, it is important for me to let you know about our experience at your restaurant and its food for your to become better. I enjoyed the decor, the ambience, and the service. But, the tiger jellyfish salad was salty and I think the cilantro could have been chopped in small pieces so it's easier to eat and blend better with all the flavors. The walnut shrimps had too much mayonnaise covering them. It was overwhelming. The mushroom with noodle and steak- some of the noodles were burnt, some steak meat was hard, and the sauce you put in the dish wasn't so good. I don't know if it's that you use too much dark soy sauce or put too much soy sauce. It wasn't tasty for me. I noticed that other reviews felt similar to how I felt. Please, pay attention to these reviews. 
I wish you much success!

This place has been on my list for a while. Cantonese food with a modern American twist. Checked it out for brunch (since it's just plain hard to get a res for dinner):

1. Endive salad: added the popcorn chicken and it's the move, you guys. I'm a sucker for a good salad and this was pretty great. Good to balance out all the other dishes 
2. Bolo bao toast: ah saw this on tv and been wanting to try this. Crisp on the outside and fluffy on the inside. Good, but not as omg yum as I thought it would be. 
3. Radish cake hash: lighter mani on the menu. Pretty good. Not much to say

Overall, Potluck Club just screams cool and modern. Enjoyed how they played around with familiar ingredients and flavors and turned it on its head to come up with somewhat familiar yet modern dishes. I would not mind coming back, especially for dinner for that rice cake dish. Service was also great and friendly and the entire place just felt welcoming.

made reservations for their brunch service at 11:30am on a saturday for a party of 3. arrived on time and was seated immediately!

endive salad with chicken - 3.5/5

hong kong french toast - 4/5 (definitely the unanimous favorite of my group!)

salt & pepper chicken sandwich w/ fries - 4/5

iced hong kong milk tea - 4/5

definitely on the pricier side but a nice spot for solid fusion food. loved their lively atmosphere and neo-cantonese decor, very reminiscent of OG hong kong cinema with a modern twist. very busy, attracting a mostly younger crowd. friendly and fast service. they also played chill rap and r&b in the background which i loved!

I'll give this place a 5, but I'd probably give it a 4.5/5 if possible. I came here for lunch and dinner (separately, of course) and ordered the pork belly cha siu and potluck chow mein for brunch, and the endive salad and the oyster mushroom rice rolls for dinner. I picked these items because they were the top ones on Yelp and they did not disappoint. They were all so flavorful and the portions were honestly quite large, both times having some leftovers to eat the next day.

I think one of my favorite parts of the restaurant is the vibe - the decor really sets the mood for a "classic" Hong Kong restaurant. It's a great place for a date and the servers are also very friendly!

Despite its name, you're not required to bring your own homemade dish to this place, so you can put away your Jell-o mold tin and your mom's lime Jell-o salad recipe. No, this is a hipster-centric spot that serves up contemporary takes on traditional Cantonese dishes in not Chinatown but the Lower East Side. Jamie W. and I were looking for something different, and we got it.

It was certainly a cool-looking place with ornate Chinese lanterns, a movie theater marquee wrapped above the bar, and a mural from the 1994 martial arts classic, "Shaolin Popey". We were seated at the horseshoe-shaped counter which looked into the prep area of the kitchen. Instead of dim sum on a Saturday, they were serving a brunch menu that mixed a new American style into the dishes.

We started with the $21 Endive Salad, which mixed dragonfruit, cara cara orange, pistachios, and pecorino into a uniquely fresh combination ladled with an unnamed dressing best described as a remoulade (photo: https://bit.ly/3sK3KNb). I think I would've preferred the dressing on the side. We then shared the $21 Pork Belly Cha Siu & Egg Salad Sandwich with French Fries (photo: https://yelp.to/8U335kU0D2).

The sandwich was tasty with the fatty pork, Dijon aioli, arugula, and what tasted like a Hawaiian bread roll. The fries were standard shoestring and quite endless. The weakest dish was the $24 Potluck Chow Mein which featured pieces of hanger steak, garlic chives, scallions, and frustratingly long and chewy noodles that eventually land in your shirt (photo: https://yelp.to/PDl02U5DyQ). 

I liked how the counter stools were well spaced apart, especially from other customers who preferred to give us small-mouth than smile. The server (who was likely one of the owners) told us we should come back for the more extensive dinner menu when they feature their signature salt-and-pepper fried chicken. We may just do that if we can get our groove back on.

FOOD - 3 stars...some elements (pork belly, dragonfruit) worked better than others
AMBIANCE - 4.5 stars...a fine job on the retro-hip front
SERVICE - 3.5 stars...brash youth
TOTAL - 3 stars...I think some plates need rework to match the fabulous ambiance

RELATED - Exploring NYC's dining and drinking scene? Here's a collection of places I've patronized and reviewed: https://bit.ly/2YS9ELs

We came here on a Sunday evening at opening and it was pretty busy but we're able to get a table for an hour walk in. The vibe is really cool in there and I loved the decor. For food, I recommend the salt and pepper chicken - just a classic Chinese flavor and the sauce paired perfectly. Also loved the scallion biscuits that came with it. We also got the vegetarian fried rice which was honestly just fine and the oyster mushroom rice rolls - sauce was very flavorful but also a bit salty for me.
I had the Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles with hanger steak and they were delicious. Can't wait to go back with a large group to try more of the menus

Decor was certainly attractive and trendy, with homages to Asian cinema and other cultural elements.  Potstickers were very tasty, although lacking in quantity.  Salt and pepper chicken was wonderfully fried and crisp and the viscous chili plum jam complemented well.  The braised short ribs was somewhat disappointing; while it was quite tender, the sauce was too salty and overpowered the meat, potatoes and carrots.  It was thus hard to justify its $40 price.  Service was excellent.

My sister and I got here around 5:15 without a reservation to see if we could walk in. There was already a line forming and we were probably the fifth or sixth party in line. We managed to get a table right near the door which was very lucky. We ordered the jellyfish appetizer, the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (we added beef), and the pineapple soft serve for dessert. The jellyfish appetizer was vey good and a great size for sharing. I haven't had jellyfish in a while so this dish was definitely bringing me back to childhood Chinese banquet meals. The oyster mushroom rice roll noodles was very good but I don't think it's worth adding the beef since it's pretty expensive for the amount of beef that's added and the flavors of the dish are already quite good without the added beef. The pineapple soft serve was very icy and tart and I probably wouldn't get this again if we came here. 

The service and the ambience were great. Since it was only the two of us, we couldn't try that much stuff so I'd be curious to try some of the other dishes. I don't think I would wait in the line again though, so hopefully it'll be easier to get a reservation next time!

food here was so good! interior is so cute- modern take on traditional chinese colors and culture. the fried rice was amazing, the eggplant was a bit too oily for my liking but my favorite thing had to be the scallion biscuits. so so buttery and flavorful! 
pro-tip (as recommended by a worker): create a mini sandwich with the chicken, sauce and biscuits for the perfect bite!

great place to grab a dinner with friends to catch up or a more casual date. i would recommend grabbing a reservation as the place gets pretty busy

The decor is cool, the vibe is nice, and the service was good. We had higher expectations for the food but were a little disappointed. We went on a Saturday around lunch time and were hoping to try the main menu but they only served the brunch menu which is pretty basic and limited. Bo lo bao (pineapple bun) was interesting but too pricey for what it is. Hongkong milk tea is super light, the worst I've ever had. Can't taste shrimp in the shrimp fritters. Radish hash browns are unique. Overall, it's an interesting fusion place but not worth the wait or price.

This restaurant definitely lives up to all of the hype I've seen it get online and on TikTok! Not only does it have the fun, unique aesthetic of a theater in Hong Kong, but the food is also innovative and so delicious! Places like these make me wish my stomach was larger :)

The salt and pepper fried chicken that comes with scallion biscuits is a must try (sadly not pictured). I'm not lying when I say that this is the best fried chicken I've ever had, and I don't like chicken that much to begin with! The crispiness is unbelievable and it was perfectly seasoned--super flavorful and yet not too salty. I loved having the chicken with the biscuit and chili-plum jam as a sandwich to get all of the flavors together. After tonight I think going to KFC will be a sin.

My second favorite dish was the mushroom rice noodles, which were soft and chewy, and flavorful from soaking in the sauce with the mushrooms. The jellyfish salad and yellowtail crudo were also pretty good and provided a nice spicy/sour taste to complement the rest of the meal. The yellowtail crudo is not on the menu, but our server told us about it as soon as we sat down!

We had weekend brunch. Interior has a unique Hong Kong vibe. 
coffee milk tea - cute cups. perfect on a cold day 
Taro shrimp fritters - perfectly done. comes with 3 pieces.
Endive salad + salt and pepper chicken - a bit heavy on the sauce but still really tasty with the chicken. definitely recommend pairing with the chicken
Hong Kong French toast - salted egg yolk with toast is delicious and extra yummy with the condensed milk and butter
potluck chow mein - love crispy noodles and the hangar steak was a nice medium. 
Sunny side eggs over radish cake hash - least exciting dish.

There were some hits and misses during brunch today. The noodle dish was delicious. I highly recommend it. The bolo bun milk toast looks way better than it taste. The toast was hard. Everyone at my party enjoyed the french toast. Any my two friends enjoyed the chicken sandwich. Unfortunately, one of our taro shrimp fritter dishes came out raw. And the chef forgot our chicken in the salad (no pic of the cesear salad). The restaurant ended up giving us a plate of the chicken at the end, but we were already full. I would recommend my friends to come here and try their noodle dish, but not if they have to wait more than 10-15 minutes for a table.

Alrighty, I won't lie a little disappointing. I wanna give this place more of a 3.5 but we'll round up. 
Got super excited because of all the hype on TikTok and was a bit of a letdown. We started off strong though. Our favorite item was actually a special that was off menu which was the tuna crudo which was deliciousssssss. We essentially licked the plate clean. We also had the potstickers which came with a great chili oil that we literally put on everything. They asked to take our plates away like 3 times but we crept moth because of the sauces which we needed for our mains tbh. We asked for recs for the mains and our lovely waitress gave us a bunch of recs and confirmed what I knew to be the more popular dishes. So we got the salt and pepper chicken and the tiger prawns. The chicken was good but very very dry. I tried to put the jam on it for moisture and more flavor but it barely helped so I ended up using that chili oil from earlier. The biscuits were great when you used the jam. But the chicken needed a sauce. The prawns were good but nothing special. Needed more flavor so again I used the chili oil for that purpose and then they tasted great. 
The dessert was basically a dole whip which was good. 
Overall, the space was very cool and I liked the apps a lot. Not so into the mains. Did feel overpriced for what we got.

We literally devoured every dish that came. There was an Endive salad - not pictured due to said devouring. From beginning to end with the soft serve, everything was delicious. Having consumed more than our fair share of Cantonese and other Asian cuisine (from SF Bay Area), we were a bit skeptical of the hype. But this place didn't disappoint. Their take on all the dishes were surprising and so tasty.  Our favorites were the Endive Salad, the Salt and Pepper chicken, and the Rice Rolls. The pineapple soft serve was not at all like a Dole Whip - we were all stunned by how fresh it tasted of pineapple and the super creamy texture. This restaurant stands out amongst so many good ones we visited during our trip.

Food is overpriced. Walk over to Chinatown and locate a Hong Kong cafe for similar food at a lower price. I ordered an iced HK style coffee and it was diluted. Food tasted decent and we ate everything. Staff was friendly. Would not return, nothing amazing stuck out.

This review is only for the Brunch menu. We were not able to get a reservation for dinner so I cannot comment on their dinner menu. As a side note, I do think that their dinner menu looks more impressive than the brunch menu. 

First of all I have to say that their decor is fabulous. It's obvious that meticulous attention to detail went into decorating this place. Love love love the vibe here. I do have to say that the bathroom is too dark for my liking though. It has dark blue lights, which in theory looks cool, but in reality makes me uncomfortable bc I can't see if the bathroom is clean or dirty. 

For brunch we tried their HK French toast with salted egg yolk lava (unfortunately it did not lava  if you know what I mean), salt & pepper chicken sandwich with french fries, pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich and we switched out the fries with taro shrimp fritters, sunny side eggs over radish cake hash, and we all had the lemon iced tea. 

HK French Toast tastes good, but I've had better ones in Toronto. The salted egg yolk is supposed to ooze out as their menu had described it as "lava", but it did not ooze out. 

Salt & Pepper Chicken Sandwich with fries: I liked the salt & pepper fried chicken, it was crispy and flavoured to my liking. The fries are McDonald fries, which I really don't love and is nothing special. 

Pork Belly Cha Siu & Egg Sandwich: I didn't love this one. I didn't really like the way the Cha Siu was flavoured and it was very salty to me. Our friend loved this sandwich though so perhaps others would enjoy it. 

Taro Shrimp Fritters with Cilantro Aioli: I'm glad we switched out one of the fries with this side dish. We all liked it and it was good, but I think if we're calling it fritters it would be even better if it was shrimp filling covered with shredded taro then of course deep fried. The slivers of taro on the outside would make this very crispy and textured. It's currently the same texture all throughout, which although not bad but could be improved upon. 

Sunny side eggs over radish cake hash: this dish I was very excited abt however was disappointed by. I was interested in their American fusion take on radish cake and wondered what radish cake hash meant. I'm still not sure what radish cake hash means bc it was just radish cake cut up into smaller cubes. The radish cake cubes, although grilled very well and was very crispy on all edges, but by itself had almost no taste. Note the name of the dish as eggs OVER radish cake hash, making me think that the star of the show would be the radish cake, however the radish cake cubes were actually sprinkled over a salad and the radish cake is more akin to croutons on a salad. There was a sauce that was drizzled on the radish cake/salad that gave it flavour, but the sauce is like a fusion salad sauce (a lighter vinegary version of the usual sweet soy sauce paste that we dip radish cake in) and so this dish is actually a salad and should more accurately be called salad with radish cake cubes and sunny side eggs. 

Lemon Iced Tea - good and refreshing, but flavour could be stronger

This is an interesting take on the HK cafe bc it's a HK / American fusion restaurant, which is unique on its own and enough to warrant a visit. It is higher end than most HK cafes. I like the creativity. I wish that we were able to try their dinner menu though. I'll have to come back again to try their signature dinner mains.

Came here for a brunch and had no clue how much it was coveted. The vibe here is IMMACULATE. I love the movie theme throughout from the host stand to the bar to the little screens to the bathroom, like ICONIC.

This is a menu where you can't really go wrong. 

Some highlights were:
Salt and pepper chicken sandwich- SUPER CRISPY
Chow mein- look for 24 dollars I was like what tf but the second I had a bite, it shut me up. Recommend. Their chili oil also has a slight kick but isn't too spicy for those that can't handle it... loved it 
Milk/French toasts- get those. They have a milk tea butter on it that elevates the dish so much. 
Radish cake hash- bit lackluster on the radish cake but it was well dressed and balanced 
Landlady drink- good but I wasn't a fan of the salted plum- personal preference
Overpriced! $3x for 5pcs of shrimp. Nothing special about this dish. So many more better places in this area

The decor of the spot is quite cute upon walking in as there is a screen with the classic Hong Kong movies that are now considered "retro" probably (Shaolin Soccer, Kung Fu Mahjong, A Better Tomorrow, etc) 

Service was very fast. We were able to order and the food came out quickly. 

There was a special for that day which the server described. It was a yellowfin tuna jalapeño sashimi entree. It tasted fine, akin to other similar dishes that can be found out sushi spots.

We also go the salt and pepper fried chicken with the scallion biscuits and jam. The biscuits were quite dry on their own and I did not think there was anything special about the biscuits. The scallion flavor also does not come through. With the jam however the biscuits are more special. The jam is a spicy chili jam. The chicken in contrast to the biscuits was very good! Still moist but also very crispy on the outside. A good mixture of fat and meat on each piece. The salt and pepper flavors were very umami.

We also got the rice rolls with oyster mushrooms and that was very good as well. The sauce is akin to an oyster soy sauce of sorts and the flavors reminds me of the Cantonese chao ngau ho/Beef Chow Fun dish. They have a beef add on to the dish which would make it very similar. The mushrooms and rice rolls were chewy and delicious. 

The rice roll with mushrooms dish definitely made me see how they are a modern twist on classic Cantonese banquet food.

The venue is cool, but the food doesn't match it unfortunately. It's just too hyped because of the venue, and the food isn't bad at all, but it's just average. I was hoping for a bit more authenticity with the food, with more memorable flavors, but this place seems to be more driven by the media attention it gets from what they've done with the interior. Worth a shot if you've got friends who wanna try it!

3.5 because I was unimpressed by the brunch, but feel like the dinner menu might be better. Nothing about the brunch really blew me away and seemed a bit overpriced, given how much cheaper you can find all these other items, anywhere else in Chinatown. I mean a bolo bao "French toast" for $15?! That was insane to me, considering I had delicious bolo bao for less than $3.  

If you're coming here to experience the brunch, I urge you to reconsider and try booking a dinner instead. The only thing I truly loved was the coffee milk tea, and that is quite difficult to mess up. 

What made up for the lackluster brunch was the gorgeous and interesting interior and decor. I appreciated the little stand in the front, the various pictures of old Chinese movies that I recognized from my childhood, and the cool booth in the back. 

The servers were quite nice, and very attentive - no complaints there. I did find it funny that they gave us fork and knives instead of chopsticks - which we had to ask for. Come on - we're Chinese American, and I consider this to be a Chinese American place. Give us both!! 

I would probably come here again to try their dinner, which I have higher expectations for.

Very underwhelming, especially after reading so many good reviews. There were no oyster mushrooms in our Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles dish, just asparagus... I even peered inside a noodle because I was confused. Noodles had a nice texture.

The two Salt and Pepper Chicken pieces I tried were tough to chew and had incredibly hard/inedible bits. My party of 2 didn't opt to take the last piece home. The biscuits with the jam were solid. The jam itself was stellar.

The Berkshire Pork Dumplings were fine, but 5 for $14 is steep. Would not return.

Ahhh I'm obsessed with this place. This review is for dinner only. My only qualm is that they have timed seating. I understand the reason for this, but 60 minutes for dinner feels really rushed and isn't the best customer experience - I felt like I had to chow down on my food. I think 90 minutes is better for 2 people. 

Ambiance/ Service: love the vibe of this place. I don't really know how to describe the decor or ambiance, but it's just a fun trendy casual cool (without trying) vibe. They play hip hop and it's lively. Place is bigger than it looks - you could easily do groups of 6-8. Service was great. 

Food: portions are decent sized and could be shared between 3-4 people. Don't forget to ask for a side of their homemade chili oil - it's sooo good. 

-Endive Salad: just order this. The more I ate it, the more addictive it became. It's super refreshing and love the crunch of the endives. 

-Jellyfish Tiger Salad: refreshing and was good to try, but if I could only order one salad I would definitely go with the endive salad. Don't order if you don't love cilantro - hugeeee pieces. 

-Salt & Pepper Chicken: OMG SO GOOD. You have to order this. Chicken is sooo flavorful, crunchy, and not oily. It doesn't even need the sauce it comes with because it's so well seasoned. 

-Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll (added steak): this was good. Well salted, but needed a bit more sauce (noodles were a little dry). But the steak was super tender and I would still order again.

Finally snagged a spot at the bar and was super happy with all of the dishes we were able to try.

A standout and MUST order is the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. These make your own sandwiches we're SO flavorful. The chicken is coated in seasoning, a bit spicy! The biscuits were soft but dense enough to withstand the chicken.

Another MUST order is the pineapple soft serve. I feel like this dessert has an online reputation for a reason. It's so light and the perfect amount of tang and sweet. The flavors truly dance in your mouth.

The potstickers were also quite yummy. I love the chili oil. 

I was also happy with the tiger shrimp. These really are huge pieces of shrimp that are delicately coated in sauce and paired with candied walnuts.

My entire group thought the xo rice was good, but not memorable.

We each got a different wine. I tried (for the first time) a rice wine. It was unique and I enjoyed the experience of trying something new.

Service and ambiance both work super well. I love the layout and decor of this space. It feels super modern while clearly paying homage to the owner's roots.

Keep this on your must try list.

4.7/5

I went to the Potluck club for an anniversary trip and was excited to try given the hype on social media for the restaurant. Upon entering, the restaurant is very aesthetically pleasing with so many homages to chinese cinema and a distinct Wong Kar Wai vibe. We were seated on time for our reservation, and ended up ordering the pork dumplings with chili oil and the iconic salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. Both were really spectacularly seasoned, and the salt and pepper chicken really was exceptional. It was very crispy on the outside, but incredibly tender and juicy inside. The scallion biscuits had a great aroma and scallion taste but they were slightly stodgy (I still really liked them). Definitely would go back here and reorder the salt and pepper chicken.
Food is a new style different traditions Chinese foot .Taste is average level. Th dish is middle size and prices has little higher.

A fun, modern Cantonese/HK restaurant. Would recommend booking a reservation at least a week in advance; it was busy, even on a weekday. 

I'd highly recommend the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits because the sauce was really good. I would probably get this again just for the sauce. We also ordered the oyster mushroom rice noodle rolls which were good but not unique or outstanding in any way. Overall, love the vibes of this place...made me really miss Hong Kong!

My friends and I made reservation for the weekend after hearing many good things about the resturant. Since we came in the afternoon, only the brunch menu was avaliable. We ordered one of each of the main entrees avalible and the Hong Kong French toast to share. For drinks, some of us ordered the lemon tea and others order the coffee milk tea. The brunch menu is limited compared to the dinner menu so we would need to come back another time to try those dishes. 

Everyone agreed that the toas was good and the potluck chow mein. As for our individual dishes, we did like it as well, but I felt the sunny side eggs over radish cake hash was slighly oily.

Overall, we enjoyed the meal and the service there was really friendly and relatively quick. The decor in the resturant was also nice and reminded me of Hong Kong.

This place is a true gem. I was impressed the moment I walked in the entrance. Lovely staff. Great decor. Fast service. Everything on the menu was incredible (especially all of the veggies!!) very spacious, not too loud, spaceship looking bathrooms. Cannot go wrong here. One of the best Asian restaurants i have had in a very long time. Also get their mocktails! Both delicious

I was curious to try what kind of food they could dish out in this hip, modern HK restaurant. We arrived on a packed weekday evening, so we grabbed seats at the bar area. I felt the atmosphere was what you would expect from the bustling city center of Hong Kong; bright colorful decor and indoor neon signs, loud chatter from sides, and frequent foot traffic around the premises. I reminded myself to stay focused as I cracked open the menu, and as I looked at the food associated with dishes, I could not help but assume that the hipster tax was in the double-digit percentile. I picked a salad for starters and then XO Fried Rice and Tiger Shrimp w/ Walnuts as mains.

The salad came quickly, and it was nothing to write about it. The Tiger Shrimps were good; the sauce was not too overpowering and the size of the beefy shrimps was fair given the hefty price tag. The XO Fried Rice however was a bit overpowering, but it's fair to assume that it's their interpretation of what fried rice should be as a standalone dish. Generally, I find fried rice dishes with all its condiments in harmony, but this XO Fried Rice dish felt like a warzone in my mouth, with each ingredient fighting for the spotlight. The Chinese sausage stood out and I can tell it was carefully cooked to bring out that intense smoky flavor, which I found interesting.

Overall it is a fun, lively retro Hong Kong-themed establishment with decent food, perfect for groups!

Honestly some of the most disappointing I've had in the city period. Ate here a while ago but I'm seeing this place get a ton of positive attention online recently and wanted to warn people.
Jellyfish salad- sooo salty and sour, to the point where it was almost inedible
Mushroom rice rolls- also inedibly salty, no wokhei, no mushroom taste at all
Tiger shrimp- the aioli this comes with is so bland and thin and the shrimp aren't even crispy and the walnuts weren't candied, I'm not expecting it to taste just like normal honey walnut shrimp because this is a fusion dish but you gotta at least kinda hit the  flavor profile.
Pineapple soft serve - best thing we ate all night, really refreshing and not too sweet.
And it was pretty price $50+ per person after tip, I can get a way better meal at an oldschool canto joint for half this price so it makes it extra disappointing.

The positives - the restaurant is genuinely beautifully decorated and the service was great! I think this place has all the ingredients to be a really great place but it really misses the mark in execution

Cantonese is cuisine is honestly one of the best cuisines in the world because of the delicate balance of flavors, it's all about seasoning something just the right way to highlight the freshness of the ingredients, the wokhei, the umami. Potluck's club fusion dishes really did away with all of that and it seems like they really don't understand the essence and soul of Cantonese food. It's Cantonese food for Americans who want a trendy new place to eat.

Food was delicious, interior decor was full of characters with cultural references, seats are comfortable and our waitress was sweet and friendly! But I found it to be on the pricier side! We might still come back to try the rest of the menu but need to save up a bit lol  it's definitely not a place I could go too often as I would probably find similar quality dishes a few blocks away in Chinatown for much cheaper prices

Love the modernized Cantonese American theme throughout the decor and menu. They're clearly paying homage to their roots, but with a modern American spin on everything. Service was friendly and attentive. I made a reservation weeks ago and then they were recently added to the Michelin Guide, so this place is catching on. 

Yellowfin Tuna Crudo (off the menu special): 10/10
This should be added to the regular menu. It was my wife's favorite dish of the night. As for me, I normally don't like crudo, but wowza this was delicious. It had a beautiful melody of sour, spicy, creamy, savory, and fresh.

Oyster Mushroom Rice Rolls with Hanger Steak: 9/10
This dish reminded us of XO Rice Noodle Rolls served at dim sum restaurants. Easily the 2nd best dish of the night. Perfectly cooked noodles and the flavor was addictive. A small handful of mushrooms were extra salty from absorbing too much seasoning, but everything else in the dish was excellent. I noticed the 5-star reviews got this dish and the lower star reviews didn't. Don't skip it if you come here...

Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits: 8.5/10
The biscuits are unique. They're like scallion pancakes but in the form of biscuits. The chicken was nicely seasoned and crispy. You could enjoy it by itself, but adding the sauce on the side makes it even tastier. There was a bit of bone and non-chewable bits in some chicken pieces, which is why I docked a few points because it's supposed to be boneless. Generally not a big deal for the average customer, but these details matter if they ever want to shoot for a Michelin Star one day. They seem to have the potential to realistically shoot for it if they keep improving and getting better, but they only serve family style and probably won't do a tasting menu. Too bad, because their chef is talented.

Tiger Shrimp with Walnuts: 8/10
Tasted like standard walnut prawns to me. Overall good, but not the best version of the dish I've had nor was it particularly elevated. I live within driving distance from San Gabriel Valley in California, which has a high density of excellent and authentic Chinese restaurants, so I have a pretty high bar. We could've skipped this and wished we tried their Endive Salad instead, because it has rave reviews.

Overall, we're happy we came here and would certainly recommend it to tourists and locals.

I made a reservation for 2 a few days ahead for brunch on a Saturday. We were really impressed from the second we stepped in. We ordered a hot and a cold coffee milk tea with oat milk. It was so delicious and definitely appreciated the dairy free option! We also ordered the radish cake and chow mein. The radish cake was nicely fried and egg was perfectly cooked. The combination was amazing. The chow mein was so crispy and the beef was really tender. Flavors were great and the chili oil was the perfect topping. We had some left over chow mein and it was delicious as left overs too!

The decor inside is very nostalgic and so much fun. The hostess is in a booth and it all feels like an old Hong Kong movie theater. Right after the hostess booth there's a little vending machine like thing and inside is fortune cookies! Such a nice little touch. Really enjoyed my time here and already want to come back to try the rest of the menu!

This place is a vibe. The interior design is quite cool offering family style seating in some areas. My friends and I came for brunch. The staff was incredibly kind in helping me pick an option given my dietary needs and craving for savory breakfast. I opted for the potluck chow mein but substituted meat for mushrooms and shishito peppers. Additionally, I shared a bolo bao milk toast. The food was great, a little difficult to eat - but definitely tasty. Portion sizes are massive, I had a second meal for myself.
I am intrigued to try their dinner menu as I am a big fan of eggplant dishes. My friends enjoyed their meals as well. 
Definitely request their tea in the beginning of your meal and check inside their vending machine for a surprise at the end of your meal! :)

Everyone thought Potluck Club was really good! The decor was both trendy and kinda authentically Asian American.

Food:
-Oyster mushrooms and rice rolls was my top dish!! The mushrooms were so well cooked and the dish had great flavor
-Salt and pepper chicken was perfectly cooked and the biscuits were so fluffy
-Drunken chicken was also a good dish, although the breast was a little dry
-Pea sprouts were a little tough/overcooked and could use more flavor

Drinks
-old man chiu was basically more citrusy sprite but it was good
-the landlady was very fruity and sweet and delicious 
-puffed rice Chinese pale ale you couldn't really taste the rice but it was a good ale
-ribena sprits was very delicious 

Service
-super appreciate their awareness of allergies and checked in on us the perfect amount
-food came out really quick 

Would come back

While visiting a friend in NYC Chinatown, I decided to come check out this restaurant as we had seen this place recommended on a social media video. The inside has a really cool vibe, with some very unique asian inspired decor around. We were able to be seated pretty quickly since we had made a reservation, and the service was excellent.

 We decided to get the XO Fried Rice, tiger shrimp with candied walnuts, and the salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. I have to say, all these dishes were done very well and I enjoyed each of them. The XO Fried Rice had great flavor, and I would recommend getting the tea egg with it. The shrimp tasted fresh, and the sauce added onto it definitely elevated the taste. The fried chicken is also a must-try here, as it's crispy and full with flavor (especially with the provided sauce). The biscuits also hold their own here and were quite good!

 If you're in the Chinatown area of NYC, really recommend checking it out!

Excellent modern Cantonese food, very thoughtful touches inside, very friendly staff - probably the best modern take on beef chow fun I've ever had along with the best fried chicken and scallion buns.

Potluck Club is recognized as a Bib Gourmand on Michelin, and was on my hubby's list to try and we finally got to go on a Friday night. We arrived right at opening at 5:30pm and was able to snatch amazing seats right in front of the chef/open kitchen area. Within minutes of us sitting, the restaurant filled up! 

We wanted to order a variety of dishes on the menu, including the snow pea, spicy eggplant, crispy drunken chicken and the rice rolls with beef. They were all so delicious and portions were huge! 

Because I have been trying to curb my gluten, they were accommodating, not all of the dishes were able to be gluten-free, however where they can, in the rice rolls with beef, they were able to make it gluten free. And of course the snow pea was also gluten free! 

Overall, lovely Friday evening date-night restaurant with delicious and creative dishes!
Great service paired with lots of comfort food and a unique aesthetic. We went for lunch but the dinner menu is a bit more extensive which is a benefit. Definitely try the crispy chicken sandwich.

First off, super cool vibe and aesthetic. Giving retro chinese american feel. I feel like that is also reflected of that in the food, I liked the spicy eggplant but I wasn't a huge fan of the salt and pepper chicken. It was really salty to me. We also got the bolo dessert and it was just solid, nothing notable.

I would hit this place soon before they get their Michelin Star, which i think they will, and it gets hard to get a reservation. It was an amazing, amazing meal and even more amazing staff. The service was above and beyond and super friendly. The food is Cantonese with a modern twist. I didn't go in with any expectations but left with complete satisfaction and with thoughts of the next visit. We started with the Endive salad, which was so colorful, and all the ingredients went well together. I loved the dressing of the sweet savory, which is in line with Chinese cooking. The Rice rolls and Crispy chicken were simply amazing. Both were season just right. The hanger steak complimented the rice rolls well and very tender. The ginger scallion sauce for the chicken was a nice elevated touch with it slightly blended. They should bottle it and sell it. My favorite dish was the Pea Shoots. Instead of raw garlic going into the oil, they use roasted garlic. The first bite, you get a hint of sour Chinese cabbage and then blend into the flavor of the shoots and garlic. This definitely worked and elevated a simple traditional dish to another level. We finished off with the desert special of Ovaltine pudding. It was another delicious dish to finish off an over the top meal. I can't wait to go back.

Really enjoyed all our dishes and would love to come again to order our favorites!

We started with the day's special which featured a sashimi crudo with a super refreshing and tart yuzu sauce - absolutely delicious! 

We initially ordered only 1 starter and 3 mains (XO fried rice, Salt & Pepper chicken, Spicy Eggplant), but our server recommend we order one more dish for a party of four and boy, I was glad we got his recommended Coconut Curry.

But overall our favorite of the night was the crispy, flavorful, juicy Salt & Pepper chicken - so perfectly cooked and tender with a crunchy skin exterior, and the savory jam worked surprisingly well with the soft buttery biscuits. 

The interior is super fun and modern, and most importantly, spacious! We were seated after waiting in line before opening at 5:30pm but would recommend reservations.

Came for dinner with a friend and had a great experience! We shared:

+ Salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits
+ Xo fried rice
+ Tiger shrimp with candied walnuts 
+ Endive salad
+ Pineapple soft serve

The highlight was the chicken, followed by the endive salad. Soft serve was also great (should hope so, considering this place is run by the Milk & Cream people).

Would return!

First Impressions - stopped by for dinner and drinks with a girl friend and this place has been on our list of spots to try for a long time. Loved the vibes and ambience. The signage is super dope and the decor throws me back to my childhood memories 

The Noms- 
XO fried rice was fucking delicious! One of my fave fried rice dishes overall. Just a tad bit too oily though. 
Tiger Shrimp with candied walnuts... my fave dish of the night... really enjoyed the candied walnuts and the sauce was perfect... not overly sweet or too saucy 
Drunken chicken with shrimp chips - loved the nostalgia of the shrimp chips... but the chicken wasn't anything special. 
Chocolate dessert (sorry forgot the name) tastes like a Ferraro rocher ice cream bomb. Soooo good, and perfect ending to dinner 

In Conclusion - loved this spot and would def come back again

Came for dinner with a friend and we shared:
- Oyster mushrooms and rice rolls: our fav dish!! rice rolls were so chewy and nicely absorbed the umami flavor 
- Salt and pepper chicken: chicken was perfectly fried and the chili plum jam was so unique! only wish the scallion biscuits were fluffy

Ontop of the delicious food, this place is such a vibe! Love the retro chinese american film aesthetics with fun attention to detail - literally from the host ticket booth to fortune cookie vending machine to the dark bathrooms filled with easter eggs

Will definitely be back to try the rest of the menu and for brunch!

Excellent meal was had here. Taking a new spin on old Chinese favorites. The menu is pretty small, but focused and filled with can't miss dishes. If you're a fan of real Chinese cuisine you should be sure to leave here happy for food and experience.

Hip, hip hurray, it's another hipster Chinese restaurant!

At least this one tastes better and is less of a schlep than its Williamsburg counterparts. It took me longer than necessary to check out Potluck Club for just this reason, but I'm glad I finally did.

- Endive Salad: Creative, fresh and tasty. Why dragonfruit isn't an essential part of more salads is beyond me.

- Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits: I hate scallions. But I enjoyed these biscuits. Do I...suddenly like scallions? Or are these biscuits just that good? TBD. The chicken batter could've used more seasoning, though.

- Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles: Their best item, IMO. Cheung fun rolled up like nian gao (or tteokbokki), stir-fried to delectable char, and served with a crunchy medley of mushrooms and asparagrus. Everything about this was savory and memorable. Don't even hesitate--order this.

- Chocolate Ovaltine Pudding, Mousse, Black Sesame Macadamia Nut Brittle: An impulse decision considering they only offer one dessert item, but it was a fun, refreshing way to end the meal. That brittle especially--they should sell that by the pint.

And if you're playing Sober Sally for the night, definitely get both of their delicious mocktails made with fresh fruit.

In sum, come here if you're in the Chinatown area and want tasty, slightly overpriced Canto fare with lovely decor and staff you don't have to worry about speaking English to.

When you walk in you are immediately greeted with swanky, modern chinese design. The inside is so cool, and we got to sit at the bar seating looking into the kitchen which added a nice touch. Seeing them chef it up, we knew it was gonna be bussin'. We ordered the jellyfish salad and you must get this!!! So tasty and the texture was perfect. Also highly recommend the salt and pepper chicken. Perfectly seasoned and accompanied by the scallion biscuit and sauce. I want to go back and order this every time! Bonus points no bones in the chicken.

It's really as simple as this: every single thing on the menu is delicious. Yeah, it's a bit expensive, but with a group of friends this place is such a fun eating experience. Love the environment, the service is great, they have a pretty fun selection of beer and natural wine, it's just really hard to think of anything not good about Potluck Club.

Very delicious! I feel like there isn't a bad choice when it comes to the food here. My friends and I went for dinner and loved everything. The standout is supposed to be the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, but I enjoyed the flavor of everything, even the vegetables. We got the chicken, tiger prawns, pea shoots, fried rice, potstickers, and crudo special. Note that it's a small beer and wine menu only.

I definitely want to return and try their brunch menu!

A modern take on Chinese cuisine - potluck club is a cute date spot if you want to impress! The decor of the restaurant is super cute and nostalgic and the seating is ample yet spacious. It's not surprising why it is hard to score a resy here.

The food was honoring to the classic Chinese cuisine yet still had its unique flair. The potstickers were unexpectedly the star of the show, we really enjoyed the chili oil that we kept it to dip the rest of our mains in haha. We also got the tiger shrimp and candied walnuts and the rice rolls. The tiger shrimp is kind of a play of Mayo shrimp, my personal favorite dish at a Chinese restaurant! The rice rolls, was surprisingly both my friend's and my least favorite of the three. It was decent and had a good mushroom flavor, but was a bit salty and the steak (add-on) was quite gamey. 

Although on the slightly pricier end, portion sizes were for the most part justified. We left very full! The service was attentive without being overbearing. Don't forget to take your fortune cookie at the end!

We arrived early and Cory got us seated real quick. The vibe, decor and music were on point 10/10. They seated us at a comfy table with enough space for all the dishes we ordered. Every dish was perfect, fresh and came out super quick. Potstickers were the best I've had. Absolutely worth a visit and then another visit...then go back again!!

A quaint little Chinese dim sum place in Chinatown, Potluck Club is usually packed with people. We made a reservation on the weekend and was seated pretty quickly. In terms of food, we ordered a few things - the hong kong style milk tea was delicious as well as the egg toast. We also ordered the pan fried noodles dish with beef on top. 
 
This is the best place to serve your food family style and try a variety of different foods at once. The prices are standard to Manhattan pricing (which isn't always very friendly) but the food was delicious. 

The ambience was typical brunch in NYC - it was loud inside and the decor was very cute as it pays tribute to Hong Kong cinema which you see from the front all the way to the back in the bathrooms. Overall, I would come back again and try some of the other items on the menu. 

Food: 4/5
Service: 4/5 
Ambiance: 4/5

Potluck Club is hip and well decorated on the inside! It's a super cute place for photos, and even the restrooms are aesthetically pleasing lol. We came for brunch and it was pretty crowded, but luckily we had a reservation. We ordered the radish cake hash, pork belly sandwich, chicken sandwich, and bolo bao milk toast. My favorite was the chicken sandwich, which had an Asian inspired and flavorful breading on the chicken. I also thought the radish cake hash was good, but it came with a lot less radish than I was expecting. The radish cake tasted almost identical to a potato, which is always delicious, but I thought it would come out to be more like the huge radish cake rectangles that you get at dimsum. The pork belly sandwich was a little too fatty for my taste, and the bolo bao milk toast was good but super buttery -- I could definitely feel the butter coursing through me after. I loved the fries, they were salted well and perfectly crunchy! Finally, I also ordered the landlady drink, which was so good -- I love sprite and strawberries, so it was the perfect combo. It was a bit salty at the bottom of the drink though, so mix it well! I've heard dinner is really spectacular here, so definitely would like to try it sometime. Brunch was good but not sure if I would come back again for brunch given the menu is pretty short and sweet, and I do feel like I was able to sample all of the items that I was interested in already. Only thing that I would come back for is the chicken sandwich!!

Came for brunch but would return for dinner! Ambience is unparalleled and everything on the menu felt like a hug from my childhood. 

+ pineapple bun toast - amazing, loved that they had milk tea butter pats on the side

+ char Siu pork belly - egg on this was the perfect texture (only wish that they could have a different side instead of fries)

Every dish was exceptional. It's a small menu so you can't go wrong with picking anything off the menu. I would be interested in trying every dish.

Service was attentive and not intrusive. Beer was beer, not much to say there. Atmosphere is laid back and chill. I'm typically not a fan of elevated chinese food but this place did it right matching flavors and theme. Would definitely go back.

An interesting modern take on Chinese food, although the prices would probably make my parents disown me if they found out. I was super excited when my friend scored a highly coveted reservation at Potluck club, since it's been on our bookmarks for a while. Highly highly recommend reservations - they were packed within minutes of opening, with very few spots open for walk ins.

Between my friend and I, we decided to split the berkshire pork and chive potstickers ($14), oyster mushroom rice rolls with steak add on ($23 + $8), and the tiger shrimp with candied walnuts ($32). The potstickers were definitely the highlight of the night. Each potsticker was packed with a generous and tasty filling within a perfectly crispy wrapper. The chili oil paired wonderfully with the dumplings and our other entrees. A bit pricey for what it is, but quite tasty. The tiger shrimp is a play on the classic mayo shrimp with walnuts typically found at Chinese restaurants. As for the oyster mushroom rice rolls, this was the dish that I looked forward to most, but perhaps the one that I was least impressed with (and quite honestly a bit disappointed with). To their credit, it's exactly what they say it is, but I'd much rather stick to my street cart rice rolls with peanut sauce. The dish was quite salty, and the steak was VERY gamey. I was looking forward to their pineapple soft serve dessert, but unfortunately, they didn't have it that night. 

Service is attentive without being overbearing. I really appreciated the honest opinions that our waiter provided when we had questions about drinks & portion sizes. 

Decor is really cute and nostalgic, and truly pays homage to the Chinese childhood experience. Super fitting for a casual & cute date night without being too intimate. 

Overall, a bit pricey for Chinese food, but somewhat justified by the portion sizes. We were quite full! Worth a try, and if nothing else, we left with a postcard of a young Jackie Chan rollerskating and a fortune cookie from the vending machine.

Potluck Club is my current obsession. Been seeing a lot of modernized and slightly fusioned Korean and Japanese food that still contains a good amount of authenticity and nostalgia. However, most Chinese restaurants I see going the same route ends up being far from passable and grossly high-priced, and very few succeed. However, Potluck Club takes the Canto cuisine, innovates it, and executes it so well. Yes, price point is higher than your Chinatown restaurants, but service is great, venue is great, and food fun and delicious.

10 STARS FOR THE VIBESS!! It's so nostalgic, the music and art plays homage to old school Hong Kong media. So homey for all of us 80's and 90's babies. 

We started off with the endive salad (3/5), which was very aesthetically pleasing, but a little bland in flavor. The dragonfruit was refreshing though. 
The Salt and Pepper Chicken (4/5) was pretty good. The batter was crispy and well seasoned, while the chicken was juicy on the inside. The jam compliments the chicken really well too! My favorite of the night of the Braised Short Ribs (5/5). It was soo delicious! The ribs were sooo tender and the sauce was amazing. Order a side a rice to go with it, and you won't regret it. 

I really have to give it to the Potluck Club for the amazing service they offered. Their cocktail menu was small, but we saw that they had an interesting non-alcoholic drinks selection. We asked the waiter if they would be able to make one of those drinks (the landlady) with alcohol and they were totally able to accommodate. It turned out to be soo good! 

Overall, the potluck club is a fun new restaurant to check out in the city. The menu takes a cool spin on chinese food. But, it is a little pricey for what it is.

I had Potluck Club on my "to-try" list for the longest time and it's almost impossible to get a table.  The hype for this restaurant is real and we were lucky to grab a table for 4 on a Friday night!  This restaurant was definitely a vibe and the noise level wasn't bad, so you're able to have a conversation.  The service was amazing and they kept refilling our water, so definitely a plus on the service.  

Now the food in question... we ordered a lot of the popular dishes and we all agreed that the food was really average.  We ordered the oyster mushroom rice noodles with the add-on steak (+8 dollars), salt & pepper chicken (not shown), potstickers, snow pea shoots, and the fish crudo.  The Oyster Mushroom with rice roll noodles was a little too salty and the steak had a really odd funky taste (like it was almost past its date).  The salt and pepper chicken was okay... not exactly salt and pepper flavor you.  The potstickers were okay, nothing special about them.  The only thing that was actually decent was the fish crudo dish. 

While I appreciate what Potluck Club is doing in terms of modernizing old school traditional Cantonese food, I feel something was missing.  For the price tag of each dish, we were really expecting a lot in terms of flavor but it was a miss and the portions were small... My friend joked that if our parents found out how much we spent on some riceroll noodles, they'll call us crazy and it's absolutely true!  

Overall, Potluck Club can be a nice introduction to Cantonese food and it's definitely worth a try.  But don't expect a lot if you grew up eating Chinese food.

Make a reservation if you can! They are usually booked every night (especially on weekends). We arrived shortly after they opened at 5pm on a Saturday to see if they had any availability for a group of 6 and they could squeeze us in at 7:30. We walked around Chinatown and went to a bar nearby in the meantime. Arrived back at 7:30 and didn't get seated until after 8 - so the timing estimate could have been better.

Very modern retro vibes inside that brings back childhood nostalgia. The menu is pretty small but solid. Their small family-style serving sizes are perfect for groups. Service is amazing - they're great at walking you through the menu, giving you recommendations, and letting you know if you've ordered enough for the group.

Oyster mushroom rice rolls: Probably my favorite! Super flavorful and good portion of mushrooms and meat as well. Noodles weren't overcooked.
Salt & pepper chicken with scallion biscuits: Nicely fried and tender chicken. The scallion biscuits are also a hit - you can order additional biscuits as well so there's enough for the group.
Curry tofu: I would pass on this in the future. All the flavors in this restaurant are bold and this one didn't seem to fit in with the rest of the menu as much. Curry was a little thin and flavor wasn't memorable.
Eggplant: Very saucy and a great vegetable dish.
Endive salad: So refreshing and a great starter! 
Tiger Shrimp: Can't go wrong with this dish! Crunchy exterior and not soggy.
XO fried rice: Also a crowd favorite. Chinese sausage, xo sauce, and fried nice - what more do you need.
Braised short rib: Delicious and the meat fell off the bone but also one that I would pass on in the future as the other dishes just stood out more and felt more on-theme. 
Dessert: Pineapple dole soft serve. Very refreshing with a pineapple bun crumble. 

To sum it up, great service and a great meal especially for groups as you can try basically everything on the menu! A little on the pricey side for the area but not a complaint compared to the service and food we got. Flavors are traditionally Chinese, but kicked up a level.

Potluck Club embraces a Hong Kong cinema theme with posters and decorations from iconic films. The dishes are a twist on Cantonese classics, feeding on nostalgia and the chef's own creativity. My favorite was the Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll

Service: Great
Quantity: Good
Cleanliness: Great

Food: Jellyfish Tiger Salad ($14) , Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits ($25)
Drinks: The Landiady ($7) ,Old Man Chiu ($7)

Came here with my girlfriend after our Paint night and had to try this place out. because there is not much Cha chaan tang's around.  we did not make a reservation but was luckly to get a spot in the back call chefs counter.
we had the Jellyfish Tiger salad which was awesome and refreshing. This is far the best jellyfish i've had so far. you are able to taste the jellyfish's fully marinated with flavor. 

Now lets get down to the star of this whole night Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits. i was in shocked when i took that first bite. The salt & pepper chicken was full of flavor and it was not dry at all. The skin was so crispy it was like i was eating chips. The biscuits that came with it could have been better if it heated up more. My girlfriend paired this with her Old man Chiu drink and it was just the right touch. I had the Landiady which i though was good but my girlfriend said it was a tad on the sweet side.

Overall we would recommend this place to anyone who wants the Cha Chaan Tang theme. i would highly recommend to make a reservation as this place before going as it got packed really quick. A recommendation i would say is if you are looking for the Toast with Condense Milk or the Breakfast items you can only order this during the Weekends. If you come during the weekdays these items are not available. I was also looking forward to the 70's-90's classic Canto songs because of the Cha Chaan Tang theme.

We came here on a weekday night for group dinner. It's pretty packed. The decor and food are Chinese American fusion, and it's family style and good for sharing food. 

The menu was small, and we ordered a few drinks, one appetizer and every main course on the menu. The Berkshire pork & chive potstickers are pretty good. It's very tasty and wrapper is thin. The main courses all taste good, but the oyster mushroom rice roll noodle barely had any mushrooms. I'd like to come back again and try their brunch menu someday.

Reviewing this while still sitting at the table--

If you were going to ask what my last meal would be, it is, without question, the Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits & Chili Jam from Potluck Club. It's crispy. It's crunchy. Yes, those are two different adjectives with different meanings. It's just savory enough and not salty. The biscuits remind me of scallion pancakes but tastes like southern breakfast. Uncle Roger might hate chili jam (sorry not sorry Jaime Oliver) but even he would approve of it with this dish.

The jellyfish salad is a must order. No, rice doesn't come with anything but I will happily pay for it without shade bc fuck, inflation, & also the meal absolutely deserves to charge for rice. 

Service is humble and generous and kind and timely! I could rave about this place for ever. The vibe is how I feel--2nd gen Asian American. Traditional in taste but updated in feel. I want this to be the place I take my kids to and grow up going to. 

Walking in is a risk and reservations can be hard to snag for a group but the wait is worth every single second.

I always wanted to come to this restaurant, but the time they are opened are limited. I love the retro decor a lot. There is limited amount of servers 4 total, & they do pretty much everything from booking a table, tabling, serving, ordering and keep asking you through out if you are happy with their service. 

Food I had the following : (portion is decent size for 2 people)

-Berkshire Pork De Chive Potstickers
-Crispy drunken chicken w/shrimp chips
-OX fried Rice with tea egg

I can say, I can't even taste most of the food flavor because all I can taste was salt. I was most disappointed with the tea egg, I can't even taste any egg other than soy sauce. The OX fried rice saving grace was that they added corn, it helped with flavor. But overall I would say it's a gimmick. I wish I had went to an actual chinese restaurant because it would had tasted better for most of the things I wanted. 

-No I would not go back after the first time, because literally I can go to congee village across for better food.-

I haven't been down to Chinatown in a few years. It's a trip from Northern Westchester. That being said, I will be driving down again and again to eat at the Potluck Club. The fried rice is second to none. The spicy pot stickers to start are to die for! Then you get to the main menu! FUHGETTABOUT IT!!! The braised beef literally melts in your mouth and the salt and pepper chicken is perhaps the most delicious fried chicken that I have ever tasted! And many chickens have met their fate on my plate over the years! The noodles in oyster sauce are out of this world, served in good sized bowl with vegetables and Chinese sausage! If you are going to visit NYC as a tourist, don't miss this place! If you live in NYC, go there often and try EVERYTHING on the menu. Tell them that Monty sent you!!!

Potluck club had some solid and unique Asian food dishes with there being Asian inspired crispy chicken and waffles with sweet sauce, as well as honey walnut shrimp. I absolutely loved the honey walnut shrimp which had huge pieces of shrimp smothered in sweet mayo sauce and tons of crunchy walnuts. My absolute favorite dish however was the crunchy chicken with sweet Asian inspired sauce and scallion pancake scones! If you are near Chinatown in New York definitely check out PotLuck club!
Overrated and overpriced but I appreciate the overall style and presentation of the atmosphere and food.

Worth the hype. Phenomenal brunch - the Hong Kong French toast was exceptional and unique. The coffee milk tea was wonderful, as was the lychee mimosa. Everything came out quickly - would have liked a slightly slower progression but didn't feel like we were being rushed out. Great vibes, will be back for the dinner menu!

My cousin and I came here for dinner as a walk-in on my recent visit to NY. I had saw this place on a youtube/IG video about this restaurant with such a Cantonese influence and had bookmarked it to try next time i came into town. I didn't make reservations for my visit as I was unsure of time or amount of people or if it was even an option. We had arrived a bit before opening and was the 2nd party to enter after it opened. Luckily we were only a party of 2 so we sat at the counter by the kitchen, which was nice so you could see the inner workings of the open-style kitchen. The inner decor as you walk through the restaurant is as if you're walking through an old cinema with display of upcoming movies. 

JADE SCORPION (Green peppercorn pilsner) - a refreshing light beer, unfortunately from a can. Was a bit skeptical about getting a beer with "green peppercorn" but I don't think I was able to pick up on those flavors (thankfully LOL. i dont have the most refined taste buds for alchy anyway)

TIGER SHRIMP W CANDIED WALNUTS w calabrian chili aioli, romanesco cauliflower

HUGE tiger shrimps with candied walnuts. Simple dish but delicious. I had a random craving for this. I definitely typically don't ever order this anywhere. Nice creamy aioli, different but similar to the usual sauce used for this dish.

XO FRIED RICE w house xo, shrimp, chinese sausage (lop churng), corn

I would call this "sticky fried rice" more than a normal fried rice. The rice they used seemingly has the same texture/chew as sticky rice but not "clumped" together like sticky rice. Topped with a ton of crispy onion bits, big chunks of sausage and shrimp. 

SALT & PEPPER CHICKEN W SCALLION BISCUITS w pickled jalapeno, chili-plum jam

This was probably the favorite of the night between the two of us. SUPER JUICY deep fried chicken with a batter similar to what you'd get from like taiwanese fried chicken, topped with pickled jalapenos that were nicely tart but also not too spicy either. The biscuits are delicious, warm, buttery. Almost like a fusion of like your green-onion pancake flavor in a biscuit, which was interesting. The included chili-plum jam was mainly sweet, but was a nice change from the spiciness, tartness, butteriness, savoriness of the rest of the dish.

Overall, good once over experience. Would've loved to be able to try the brunch items as well. Interesting experience. The food overall was good. Quality was good. Bit pricey but probably matches the quality and technique put into the food. Would recommend for a unique experience !
Food was spectacular, service was ridiculously friendly and speedy, and the ambience was very warm. I'd love to come back when it's less busy :)

First meal of 2024 and the bar has been set extremely high. The menu is limited but still gives you a little bit of everything for any mood. I also loved how reasonably priced the dishes were. Especially considering the portions and quality. It's refreshing to visit a restaurant not price gouging in NYC. The ambiance was amazing, playlist was crazy and the decor ? I was like a kid at museum. Wanting to touch and look at every piece of art. 

I almost skipped the tuna crudo, as I'm very particular where I eat uncooked fish but damnnnnnn that was good! A must order. 

Everything was amazing but the other stand out dish for me was the chicken and biscuits. Amazing! The chicken was crispy, yet juicy. They included something pickled, which I love when eating anything fried. The biscuit???? Obsessed! They should sell sides of them if they don't already. I'd order some to go. 

To top it all off, the service was excellent. My server was sooooo sooo pleasant. He visited the table multiple times. Asked us how we like dishes. Very personable. The food came out so fast, we were on entrees thirty minutes in. I should mention I wouldn't consider it rushed either as we had ample time to sit with each dish and enjoy. We ordered, and apps were on the table 6 mins later. 

I thoroughly enjoyed my visit here. Finally a place worth the hype.

Such a cute spot ! We had a great experience! Service was very pleasant . The menu is not too intense , but just enough to choose from. XO fried rice was on the spread which was so yummy! Crispy drunken chicken was so good ! The chicken was cooked to perfection. Last the tiger shrimp was great as well. Honestly everything was truly delicious. The craft cocktail , lunar was so good. I enjoyed my experience here , def returning.

Starting off 2024 strong with dinner at the potluck club! I liked everything we tried one better than the next. We tried the rice noodle rolls, spicy eggplant, curry tofu, and tiger shrimp. We had a 530 reservation and that is the time the restaurant opened so they came to open the door at 530 and we were seated right away. Our food and drink order were taken as soon as we sat down and our first dishes came out in record time!! I cannot recommend this place enough the cool ambiance and decor would make any date night or friends dinner one to remember.

Modern Cantonese style restaurant. Preparation here is certainly American palate friendly with food leaning towards sweet and savory. Menu is very approachable with a few dishes in each section. I found the dishes to be consistent across the board. 

I started with a Cantonese beer brewed with green peppercorns. Cool to have a beer I haven't seen elsewhere.

Food wise, we started with the spicy eggplant and the tiger shrimp. Eggplant was sautéed with a sweet, spicy, and savory sauce. It was a satisfying dish to eat, but I had a hard time determining where the sweetness and savoriness was coming from. 

The tiger shrimp were big and crispy. They offered up a juicy and flavorful bite. Sauce for the shrimp was super savory with a very mild spiciness to it. Came with candied walnuts and I believe roasted broccoli which all added a good crunch.

Next came out the curry tofu and the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles. The curry tofu was one of the most flavorful items. The mushrooms with rice rolls was probably my favorite item. Great seat on the rice rolls. It was more umami forward with sweetness taking a back seat in this dish. 

The last dish we had was the drunken chicken. Super juicy rotisserie style chicken. It was pricey at $30+ for a quarter chicken. Came with a delicious cilantro sauce and some big shrimp crisps. Haven't seen this type of dish at a Cantonese restaurant before with some significant Peruvian influences. 

Service was friendly and attentive. Pacing of the food was on point. I didn't use the restroom but my friends had some positive things to say about it.

Came here twice, once for dinner and knife for brunch. 

During dinner, we ordered (1) the endive salad, (2) the Tiger shrimp with walnuts, (3) rice rolls with trumpet mushrooms, with steak added, and (4) salt and pepper fried chicken with scallion biscuits.

The fried chicken was a little salty, but the biscuits were divine. The other dishes were also delicious and intensely flavorful. The endive salad was refreshing; the rice rolls had great bite; and the shrimp has delicious sauce.

The night we went, there was also a special dessert, milk tea tiramisu. A great way to end the meal.

For brunch, I highly recommend the Hong Kong French toast. The egg yolk filling is a nice savory contrast to the sweet condensed milk topping. The char siew egg sando is also good; the bun is soft and the egg is fluffy and the pork belly is tender.

Located in chinatown, it is an upper scale restaurant compared to the restaurants surrounding it. 

The ambiance is pretty hip but the food is great - a little overpriced but worth a try.

Got the mushroom rice rolls and fried chicken and biscuit with some hamachi appetizer.


Overall, solid experience , just a little overpriced.

My friend and I ended up trying their infamous "salt & pepper chicken w/ scallion biscuits," "snow pea shoots," and "dole pineapple soft serve." Amazed by every dish. I thoroughly enjoyed the salt & pepper chicken and the pea shoots were cooked to perfection. I would highly recommend you checking out Potluck Club if you have the time although  their hours of operation are quite abnormal. I've definitely have tried better dole, but if you  haven't tried dole before this is a great place to have a taste of dole to start. 

The interior of this restaurant was also amazing. I really liked the vibes of the place and the unique decorations truly made this place memorable.

This was one of those places I waited to try and now I regret that. The interior of the restaurant itself is a vibe so many visually appealing aspects it feels like a lot of thought went into the decor. I can truly appreciate when a restaurant goes above and beyond for the customer experience. Take a few minutes to do a lap around and take everything in it is worth it, even the host stand is not your usual host stand. The service was great, everything came out within reasonable timing and you could see and taste the freshness. I do wish the seating was a little more evenly spread as when being seated at the entrance you feel a little distant from the rest of the seating and are not getting the full experience of the rest of the restaurant. The drinks were delicious and I appreciated the intention behind all of the drinks staying on brand including the non alcoholic drinks! That was definitely a plus. The menu is small however I believe that is intentional to make sure all items are perfectly curated and that works because everything was honestly exceptional. The oyster mushroom noodles were recommended by our server and we were so glad he did so bc they turned out to be our favorite delicious I also love when the veggies are a bit crunchy in this case the asparagus was cooked to perfection. The biscuit from the salt & pepper chicken was also a huge hit as it came out still warm and melts in your mouth. I believe the dessert menu changes nightly or weekly not sure but I also really love when restaurants do this specially when you are a returning customer. Over all I would say it'a worth coming as I have returned several times.

Took my dad and stepmom here for holiday dinner and lets just say Potluck Club did not disappoint at all. Definitely recommend making rsvps wayyy in advance. Theyre like super booked on resy!!!

The whole restaurant decor is such a vibe from the moment to enter! So many nostalgic details! Literally brought back all the memories of growin up as a kid who watched so many comedies with Stephen Chow and Ng Man Tat!
