Our waiter, Justin took great care of us! My stepmom is a full fledged vegan with crazy restrictions and he was able to accommodate it ! (I wouldve gave up the min she said no garlic, no scallions, etc!)

Some of our favorites include:
-endive salad (what a fun twist of fruits/nuts and veggies)
-salt n pepper chicken w scallion biscuits (we loved this! A must try!)
-xo fried rice
-oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (if you like rice rolls you gotta have this! They were made perfect! So soft!)

Ps. Save room for dessert. Cant even describe the dessert we had. Just remember it was a mind blowin mixture of ovaltine, black sesame and milk tea! 

Thank you Potluck Club for a wonderful evening! Definitely need to come back for brunch!

Ever since the NYT article, I feel like it has been harder to get reservations at  Potluck Club. You really have to be on it for an ideal time. Luckily, I was able to get a reservation around 6:30pm. Ended up sitting in a booth. They only have one table with a lazy susan which was a bummer since we had to pass around the dishes. 

For a group of six, we shared two appetizers and three mains, which was more than enough. The Berkshire pork and chive potstickers were good. The skin was thin, and the bottoms were perfectly crispy. Soy sauce was quite spicy. There's only 5 per plate, so they offered to add an additional one for us. The endive salad was good. I loved the sauce. Dragonfruit was a little bland but expected as I have lower expectations for dragonfruit in the States.

Salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits were amazing. The chicken pieces were big and juicy. Make sure to order enough biscuits for everyone at the table. The scallion biscuits were moist and buttery and the chili-plum jam was a good balance between sweet and savory. Not too spicy either. Got the other chicken dish, the crispy drunken chicken with shrimp chips, as well. Not as good as the fried chicken but still tasty. Oyster mushroom rice rolls noodles with added steak was okay. Their version of a dry stir fried beef noodle. Didn't think it was anything special, and the beef could have been more tender. 

Normally, I'm a little bit more skeptical with Chinese-American restaurants because it's hard to do traditional Chinese dishes better, but Potluck Club really rose to the challenge.
Got the eggs with radish cake and a side of fries and coffee. Everything was pretty good. Good service as well. About a 30 minute wait.

Alert! Alert! This is based on the dinner I ate here, as this restaurant is open for brunch on weekends, but is a dinner only location on the weekdays.

This is a restaurant that books up very, very quickly. It is not long after the doors are unlocked that throngs of customers with reservations are thrust onto tables or other seat pairings. Those who do not have reservations are turned away or told to sit at bar. I was one of those who was told to sit at the bar.

Feed me up, before you go go.

A pretty female bartender senses I am not familiar with this cuisine and holds my hand through the entire process. She is thorough and genuine and unlike me, she knows what she is talking about. I do not have the slightest clue, just nodding and agreeing and acting like a schoolboy who never saw stir fried or pan seared before.

She led me into 4 items:

-Yellowfin Tuna appetizer 
-XO Fried rice with tea egg 
-Oyster Mushroom Rice Noodles
-Old Man Chiu Drink

Bear in mind none of this came cheap, so this restaurant is not made for those with shallow pockets. I decided to experiment my trying a bit more than normal, expecting to not like everything I tried.

I was correct.

The tuna appetizer is nice, but small and incomplete. It is just a few sashimi pieces of tuna in a tangy sauce. Maybe I was hungry, but I finished this in two minutes flat.

The drink I got is tasty, but save it for the entrees. It will allow you to enjoy it more. 

The rice noodle dish is super. It is full of flavor, maybe a bit too salty but that is fine. The noodles were great and the asparagus is the right call with the mushrooms. For an extra fee, you can order this with steak. Get the steak. It adds an extra layer of texture and taste that does not ruin the dish.

The fried rice I could barely eat. There is too much onion in it, and breaking the tea egg into the dish only nauseated me. The sausage is too sweet for my liking, and the rice is particularly bland. For me it was the onion that did me in, as I have a long subway ride home and was not about to jeopardize it by eating something I did not enjoy.

Overall the menu items are quite onion heavy. I understand this is a major part of the cuisine, but this is where I have to draw the line and be careful. 

It was an enjoyable meal on the whole, however I have no intention of returning here, media endorsement or not. The onion overlords have asked me to refrain.

The food here was good, but nothing blew my mind. Service was also fast and they were able to remake a dish for us due to shellfish allergies in my group. 

- Endive Salad (4.5/5): the endives had a really nice and refreshing crunch, and was a great palate cleanser. Super light and addicting 

-Jellyfish Salad (4.5/5): As a jellyfish lover, this dish was really flavorful. Was a bit oily but delicious overall

-XO fried rice (3/5): the rice was OK. I wish the texture of the rice had a bit more wok to it but the fried garlic added a nice crunch

-Tiger shrimp (3.5/5): The shrimp were big and juicy, but there was a bit too much batter. Not my favorite shrimp but a solid option. 

-Fried chicken (2/5): this chicken honestly had no flavor without the sauce. Pretty oily but and heavily battered and nothing too special 

-Pea shoots (4/5): tasted like your typical pea shoot, but felt clean to eat vegetables amongst the other dishes 

While I'm glad I tried this place, not too sure if I would come back. They have a vending machine full of fortune cookies though which was a very nice touch!

We ordered the server's recommendations and the food was mid and pricy. The hype was overrated. I hope their brunch menu is better than the dinner we had. This is just another restaurant with gimmicky interior. 

We split the bill and the server was staring at my credit card in his hand while my friend was paying. It was very odd and uncomfortable. Why was he reading my card for so long... 

Overall, it was a disappointment. Great marketing tho

Hmmm. This place was pretty disappointing after all the hype. Started off on the wrong foot with getting super excited about several dishes, only to be told we were looking at the wrong menu....um, if it's wrong, why did you give it to us?

So, things like chicken and biscuits, totally a breakfast item right? WRONG. You can only order that at dinner. Chicken sandwich for breakfast that is impossible to share? Yep, despite the restaurant having lazy susans on the bigger table, they really don't care if you want to share or not. When we expressed disappointment at not being able to order the chicken and biscuits option, we asked if they could split the chicken sandwich for us in the kitchen. I realize this is not a super cool request, but we'd been baited and switched by the alternative so maybe, you know, help us out? Nope. They said they'd bring a knife. 

The milk tea french toast was dry and really disappointing. The coffee milk tea was a 33c bag of milk tea you can buy by the dozen in any grocery store in the neighborhood. The chow mein was fine but not chock full of goodies to hunt for...just a lot of noodle and a little bit of other stuff. Listen, you call it potluck, I'm thinking it's going to be 1. a signature worthy dish (nope) or 2. packed with a kitchen sick level of awesomeness (nope again).

Karaoke fries are the one thing saving this review from 2-stardom. They were excellent.

So, in sum, pretty meh service, very meh brunch offerings (totally not share worthy yet they clearly pump up the instagram feed to suggest otherwise) and WAY less fun than you want it to be. Would not recommend unless they start offering better stuff at the brunch hour. Maybe dinner is superior, but brunch was kinda lame.

4.5 stars here. Certainly passes the vibe check with its decor. Reservations are a must. We came for their late lunch around 1:15pm and I think it was before their closing time so we didn't feel rushed. The food was all fantastic, lost half star because it was a bit on the pricey side and saltier. 
1. Char Siu sandwich had really good flavor and the meat is tender. Bread is was extra buttery. French fries reminded me of crispy McDonald fries. Lots of people were getting the salt and pepper chicken one which looked loaded. Seems like you can't go wrong
2. The chow mein was essentially crispy noodles with beef and scallion. It was a little bit of the drier side but flavor was 10/10 and it came with chili oil on the side
3. HK French toast was perfect - buttery, the salted egg yolk was oozing out like it should. This was a great twist to the classic buns and I'd say a must get! 
4. Their two nonalcoholic signature drinks were really good and refreshing (old man Chiu and the strawberry one), would recommend !

Dinner menu over their lunch menu!

Favorite items from dinner menu 
- XO fried rice 
- spicy eggplant
- Berkshire pork & chive dumplings  
- salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits 

Tiger shrimp with candied walnuts had a too much mayo for me. The shrimp was large though!

Potluck Club is like the hip Asian grandma on the block who makes traditional dishes with a chic twist. Perusing the menu, you'll find creative plays on nostalgic foods such as dumplings and fried chicken. This is a place you should come with 4+ people; you'll want to try a bit of everything family-style.

My favorites: the fried chicken and scallion biscuits (what a filling combo, both for the belly and the heart), eggplant (who doesn't love a classic flavorful veg dish), and jellyfish salad (light and crunchy but bursting with flavor). 

The minute you step into Potluck Club, you know you're about to experience something special. It's one of those establishments in NYC where you actually will remember the dishes you ate.

Being a Canto-American, Potluck Club was a place I had on my list to visit for a while. I was interested in how they would place a modern twist on Hong Kong cuisine, and they did not disappoint (for brunch and dinner). Yes, we went twice to try the full menu. 

DINNER:
We weren't able to get a reservation, so we came right when it opened at 5:30pm on a Friday night and were able to be seated without any wait. We ordered the Jellyfish Tiger Salad, Tiger Shrimp with Candied Walnuts, and Oyster Mushroom and Rice Roll. All were delightful.
Jellyfish Tiger Salad included scallion, cilantro, jellyfish, mixed with a tangy sauce.  I'm usually the type of person who picks out the cilantro in dishes, but I had no problems clearing this plate.
Tiger Shrimp with candied walnuts included 6 jumbo shrimps that were lightly battered, fried, and coated with a spicy mayo sauce. The Romanesco cauliflower heads provided a nice crunch as well, but were a little too salty.
Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll noodles included bouncy chewy tightly rolled rice rolls, umami oyster mushrooms and fresh stir-fried asparagus. This dish balanced very well together, but due to mushrooms naturally absorbing flavor they were a little too salty too.
I like the display of Canto actors on the walls and the postcard they let you keep after getting the bill. It gave a nostalgic feel. The service was swift, and the staff was attentive to our needs.

BRUNCH:
This time, we did get a reservation for 11am on a Saturday, but the restaurant was only around half filled with people who made reservations and walk-ins. We ordered the Taro shrimp fritters, Bolo bao milk toast, Hong Kong French toast, Pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich w/ fries, and Lemon Tea.  
Taro shrimp fritters ($12) were served with cilantro aioli and  half a lemon. This was one of my favorites of what I ordered. The lemon was a great addition to the flavor. However, I agree with another review that said it would be better if it was shrimp filling was covered with shredded taro and then deep fried because I think it lacked the taro flavor. 
Bolo Bao Milk Toast (15) had a fluffy interior and a hard exterior, served with a milk tea butter. I wish the milk tea butter had more of a milk tea flavor. Though the toast was good, there wasn't enough of a twist to make me enjoy it more than the normal bakery bread.
Hong Kong French Toast ($15) has salted egg yolk lava inside, cultured butter on top, topped with condensed milk drizzle. There was a very nice light crisp, caramelized exterior. The salted egg yolk wasn't quite runny, but the savory and sweet combination was lovely. Would recommend this toast if you don't want to order both.
Pork Belly Cha Siu & Egg Sandwich w/ Fries (21) had fatty slice of meat, soft moist scrambled egg, hoisin-garlic aioli, and arugula. Was good.

Overall, I was pleasantly surprised with my experience here. I enjoyed most of the items we ordered and would come back. Food was pretty pricey, but the quality and taste made it worth trying.

For one, food was too good.
For two, that young and hip vibe was more than amazing.
Lastly, people were too nice and caring that you wanna revisit them so much! To be honest i didnt have high expectation because all reviews are all paid to make the vendors stand out. But this spot is 100% organic go-to place

Went to Potluck Club for lunch! Was super excited to hear Cantonese spoken by everyone who worked here!! Absolutely loved the brunch menu - we got the bolo bao toast with the milk tea butter, the beef chow mein (came with chili oil), and the pork belly with egg sandwich (came with fries). Everything was so flavorful but also elevated and a throw back to what I ate as a Cantonese kid growing up in the bay area!! Loved all the little Easter eggs scattered all around the restaurant - what a throw back!!

It's a pretty big space too. There's seating in the front,  a bar area with seating,  and then seating towards the back where you can see the action happening through the glass kitchen. 

For any parents:
High chairs available
Lots of bathrooms
One of the bathrooms had a changing table

If it's your first time, I highly recommend coming with a group of 6! We were able to order all the mains and a few smaller dishes to share. Now we know which dishes were hits and misses for our next time
It's still not the easiest to make a reservation for, but try setting notifications on Resy for last min cancellations
The restaurant itself is pretty small, so they pack a good amount of small tables, which i'm sure they can rearrange if necessary 

-Jellyfish tiger salad: great starter! good flavor, texture, and refreshing
- Salt & pepper chicken w biscuits: This reminded me of popcorn chicken with the tapioca starch crust. Very crunchy and well seasoned! I could've done without the biscuit, mainly because I was so full from everything else. but my husband liked it
- Mushroom rice noodle rolls: If you're going to choose one of the carbs, I'd choose this over the fried rice. It had a nice wok hei flavor
- XO fried rice: I'd pass on this one. It wasn't too memorable
- Shrimp w/ walnut: much crispier version of the one youre probably used to! It had less mayo sauce and the shrimps were huge. It only comes with 6 though, so everyone got 1 piece each
- Crispy drunken chicken: juicy and moist white meat! this was cut in like a soy chicken style with the bone in
- Braised short ribs: super tender, and a little on the saltier side

Overall the dishes were very unique, but some were just bit too salty for me. I dont know any other Chinese restaurant like this, so it would be great place to take visitors

* NOTE THIS IS NOT TRADITIONAL - ITS A FUSION.

I came here for a holiday party of over 12+ people and they were super accommodating and service was amazing. They gave us a lot of time and made sure we were all comfortable along with explaining the drinks and menu items.

After sitting down I noticed the old school theater aesthetic with Jackie Chan movies and reminds me of how my family and I used to watch these old movies together and hit with nostalgia with their display case which happens to be a free vending machine for fortune cookies (don't miss out! You must get one!) and it reminds me of all my childhood from the cough medicine we used to drink to the rubbing oil my mom used to put on my belly when I have a stomach ache, and the pills to stop my digestive problems- it's all very Chinese. Immediately I know this was a fusion because I know traditional places never really place these items on display- and better yet from someone who probably is like me, a first gen us citizen from Chinese immigrant family. 

Now that I recognize this, let's get into what I had:
------
Yellowtail tuna crudo
Absolutely amazing, one of my favorite things on the menu. It was packed with flavor and super juicy. I loved it! Can't go wrong with sashimi.

------
Berkshire Pork and Scallion Potstickers
This one takes the gold plate because it's just like our favorite pan fried dumplings but takes it up a notch about 5x. This made my heart sing and one of the most flavorful dumplings I ever had MUST ORDER.

------
Endive Salad
I am a salad lover so I ate this up so easily there is a fresh fruit flavor along with the red endives which was slightly bitter. I really enjoyed the combination but you can skip this one if you don't like fruits or stuff like red lettuce. It's like another version of Caesar salad which I thought was really neat!

------
X.O fried rice
Super yummy and flavor packed. Reminds me of a Hong Kong diner (Cha Chan tang) but like fancy-fied and American-ized.

------
Salt and pepper chicken with Scallion Biscuits
Amazing take on southern chicken and biscuits! Really felt like I was transported to the south but add some Chinese kick to it! The jam was a really good add because I love a salty jam with my biscuits! Not only for the biscuit but you must add it on the chicken.

------
Braised Short Rib
Reminds me of a French dish! Sometimes when I eat in Chinese restaurant we always have our overcooked steak but I see the inspiration for this through the soft texture and the heavenly bite into this. With Asian flavor and French style cooking it became my sort of heaven! 

------
Spicy Eggplant
I always hated eggplant. I still do. But tons of people in my party were obsessed with this one.

------
Tiger shrimp with Candied Walnuts
Now this one is tricky because I love honey walnut shrimp and I'm a little bit more on the traditional side. I felt like this was way too flavorful and never liked walnuts so I definitely won't like candied ones. However the tiger shrimp was very nicely cooked and was soft and juicy inside which I appreciated.

I honestly love this place as a fusion restaurant. If someone took me here as a regular Chinese place when I was craving something more like Congee Village I would be upset but after knowing and experiencing the place the way it is I'm happy to have come and tried all the dishes and got to experience how fun the menu really was. Thank you potluck club for the fun experience!

* Remember to check out the bathroom peep hole! It's Jackie Chan!

I was here with one of my usual groups a while ago. The atmosphere inside is unique and fun and definitely creative though it reminds me more of a spot you'd find either further into the Lower East Side or something else but sure why not. The service was friendly and the place was quite crowded as it is most nights. The food here is Cantonese-American but I would say that they have a lot more fun here and the dishes are more unique. Most of the dishes worked well but I would say that they were definitely highlights and one dish that was a lowlight that was unfortunately the most expensive thing but overall the food was excellent. I got a glass of the Hwaju for $16 or $70 for the whole bottle which is apparently $40 on most sites. Listed as an unfiltered rice wine, Hana Makgeolli Brookyln/Sayangju organic rice infused with chrysanthemum flowers, this was alright. I knew I likely shouldn't have gotten a glass as usually even bottles of makgeolli cost only around $20 or so in the city. It was a lighter version of this rice wine and I really couldn't taste the chrysanthemum but this is on Hana not the restaurant. I likely would get one of the non-alcoholic specialties or something next time. 

Our first dish that arrived was the Tiger Shrimp With Candied Walnuts with Calabrian chili aioli and Romanesco cauliflower for $32. This was pricey but honestly pretty much worth it as the shrimps were quite large with a good bouncy texture. Normally this is just with a sweet mayo but the chili added a nice kick you normally don't find in this dish and I'm pretty sure the cauliflower was roasted or something similar which was a fun spin on the usual broccoli you find in this dish. 

The next thing that arrived was the Steak With Oyster Mushroom Rice Noodle Rolls with asparagus and garlic chives which is $31 but you can also order it without steak for $23 which would be a sizable tasty entree for someone vegetarian. This was excellent with a nice wok he from the rice rolls/cheung fun as well as them having a good texture and it was probably my second favorite dish. To be honest I think it would be fine without the beef added even though the beef itself was very tender and there was a good amount of it justifying the extra cost.

The third dish that arrived was our favorite and is essentially their signature from when I can tell which is the Salt & Pepper Chicken With Scallion Biscuits with pickled jalapeno and a chili-plum jam for $25 but you can add an extra biscuit for an extra $3. The chicken was moist and tender with a good crunch from the crust and this was a fun almost southern spin on the salt and pepper chicken you find in other Canto spots. The biscuits were good but my favorite thing in the dish was easily the jam. Part sweet and part savory, this also had another unique umami flavor and I'm curious if there's fermented black beans or something else mixed in. I would honestly buy a jar of it and use it for meats and stuff as it was that good.

The final main dish that we ordered was the Braised Short Ribs with creamer potatoes and carrots for $40. This was easily the weakest of the dishes. There was plenty of meat and the carrots were nice and tender along with the potatoes but I found this way too salty. This felt like a dish that really needed white rice to cut down on the saltiness. The meat was tender and the veggies were well cooked but I wouldn't get it again. 

A couple of us because we were here already decided to go with the cheekily named Pineapple Pineapple Soft Serve or Dole pineapple with bolo bao/pineapple bun crumble for $8. Dole pineapple soft serve also known as Dole Whip® has a strong pineapple flavor that has become popular recently in New York with I believe Chikarashi helping to introduce it to the NYC masses. The bolo bao topping was a fun touch with a bit of sweetness and crunch. There was also some fortune cookies in there because why not. This was a fun dessert though I'm not sure if it was worth it but still it was pretty tasty. 

The prices might be high here but the food quality was excellent and the portion sizes were good for the price and overall their modern interpretations of Canto food worked in most cases. I'd go back here again especially to get the chicken or rice rolls or try some other good dish here. Mid 4

This was such an interesting restaurant that plays on traditional Cantonese dishes. It made me very nostalgic walking through the restaurant and seeing pictures of famous HK stars on the wall. We went in with a group of 6 and got to try all the main dishes and an appetizer - the jellyfish one! I'd recommend trying all the main dishes since they were all pretty unique tho a little salty. It looks like they offer brunch too so I'd probably come again to feel sentimental about HK's cha chaan tang.

We saw so many tiktoks about this place so my group and I decided to make a reso and give it a try! Walking in the ambiance was super artsy and gave a nice vibe to the meal. 

We got the landlady, lemon tea, and coffee milk tea to start off. The drinks were refreshing and nostalgic, they were also not too heavy to start the morning off. For food, we got 4 items to share for the table. 

The endive salad had a slight bitterness and mixed with the citrus made the perfect combo, we also added the salt and pepper chicken which complemented the dish well. The eggs with radish cake were good, I enjoyed the texture of the radish cake, it resembled a mochi like consistency. The HK French toast looked exactly like something in your mom & pop HK cafe and it was delicious. I would say this is a must order, the portion size and sweetness of the dish was perfect to share. The  hanger steak chow mein was okay, I felt like it was a tad oily and salty in my opinion. The meat was tender and I loved the pickled onions that brought acidity to the dish. It was nice that they also provide chili oil to add to our food. 

Our server was nice and quick with service, the timing was just right. They gave out Asian gummies and a postcard with your check which I found was a nice send off! The hype is definitely there and I'd revisit to try their dinner menu!

Potluck is a modern take on Asian cuisine. It was totally worth waiting for a table. You cannot go in with a mindset of trying to find the authentic asian food flavors here. If you change the mindset, this place will be one of your favorites. I love the options they had and their roll noodles were the best I have ever eaten. Highly recommend this place!!!!!!!!!!!!

There's a lot here that reminds me of Thai Diner: an Asian cuisine served faithfully, but in a brunch-friendly format. The right blend of clever brunchy crossovers and authenticity, wrapped in a trendy, instagrammable setting. 
Like Thai Diner, Potluck Club is speedy and convenient. My party walked in at noon and got three counter seats in less than ten minutes, and our food came out extremely quickly. 
French toast: delicious and decadent. My standout and my rec if you go. This dish in particular is what inspired the Thai Diner comparison mentally for me. 
Milk tea: fine. I had two, but it was just milky tea in a paper cup, not the second coming of Christ as other Yelpers would have you believe. 
Sunny side eggs and radish hash: OK. I always dither and then go savory at brunch, but this was just eggs and arugula, punctuated by roast-potato-like cubes of Chinese radish and shishitos. 
Heard good things about the sandwiches. 
A worthy brunch option, albeit with a small menu, but why not go all the way since you're in the area and do Dim Sum?

Me and my group found this place through tik tok. We were excited to try the place for the first time but we did make one mistake and didn't place a reservation. The place is super friendly yet upscale, if you do decide to dine here be sure to reserve ahead of time so you don't have to wait. 

Let me just start off from the beginning:
As you walk in the dynamic of the restaurant really brought you back to China, kind of similar to like a Chinese brunch/ diner vibes. Super Aesthetic!!!
The host greeted us very casually, as we got seated the menu is quite small so everything is already there labeled for you. We ordered the jellyfish tiger salad and the pork and chive dumplings in chili sauce as our starters. The jelly fish was super refreshing and I was quite skeptical about it at first but it has a nice crunch to it. Dumplings aren't your regular dumplings that you normally see, I would have preferred if the skin of the dumpling was a little thicker but that is just my own preference. As for the drinks I order the yuzu sake with herbal tea ( forgot what it was called ) it was super refreshing, yuzu taste was definitely there and you wouldn't even know that it has alcohol! Moving onto the mains we got the Drunken Chicken, XO Fried Rice, Spicy Eggplant, and the salt n pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. You're able to add more biscuits if you would like at extra cost. The dishes are super vibrant, the vibes were immaculate, our waitress (forgot her name but she has a nose ring) was super friendly and very welcoming. Place is very fast paced so if you're looking for a place that is more quiet, this may not be your cup of tea. Only key thing to note is I would've loved it if they had a liquor license def would bring the vibes up a bit more. Overall experience I give it a solid 8/10. Def would be back here with a date.

I was so happy to get reservations on a Saturday for dinner. It was our first time here, and it won't be our last.  Here's what we ordered and shared.
Endive Salad: Bitter & Sweet order it, you won't regret it. 
Pork & Chive potstickers: nice thin dough, juicy, and packed with flavor.
Oyster mushroom rice roll: Add the steak it's cooked all together, and every bite is flavorful.
Salt & Pepper Chicken: super crispy chicken,  scallion biscuits were soft and tasty, and the chili plum jam paired nicely. Chef's kiss!
On top of the delicious food, the service was super friendly. We can't wait to come back to try the bruch.

Arrived for our 7:30pm reservation and we were promptly greeted and seated. Despite the bustling atmosphere of a full seating area, my family and I felt well taken care of- not a single water glass left empty,  great drink recommendations,  and unrivaled attention to detail with our order as my younger daughter has an egg & nut allergy. 

We started with the mushroom potstickers which were delightfully crispy and savory. I'm normally a basic pork dumpling kind of girl, but this dish definitely hit the spot and I didn't miss the meat at all!

Bursting with brightness and tiny kick of heat came the tuna crudo. I inhaled this plate on the spot.

The rest of the dishes were family style.  Snow pea shoots were perfectly cooked and elevated by the creamy roasted garlic.  XO fried rice had my 4 year old clamoring for more.  Salt &pepper chicken was crispy and juicy and paired perfectly with the chili-plum jam (and this is a lot coming from someone who's not into sauces, let alone fruit). My 6 year old loved the scallion biscuits so much, she asked to save one for home. Mushroom rice roll noodles were a meal in and of themselves with the addition of the tender morsels of steak. I was so full, I only managed two bites of the curry tofu but it was divine (and reheated well over rice the next day). And last, but certainly not least,  as a twist on my husband's favorite traditional honey walnut shrimp in white sauce, came the tiger shrimp with candied walnuts and chili aioli- 10 out 10, would recommend, will definitely order two next time because my husband ate most of it and it was a crowd pleaser!

TLDR: You will not regret eating at Potluck Club. If you're a glutton like me,  you will regret not having enough space in your stomach to fit all the delicious food in one go. Reservations recommended for dinner as they were quite busy on a Friday evening. 

Shoutout to my kids' new friends- Auntie Alex and Uncle Cory. Will definitely see you again soon!
The food was delicious! The staff were friendly! The decor was so cute! Would highly recommend.

My friend said this was her favorite place for food in all of New York, so I had to try it out. Still trying to figure out what Cantonese food means, but anyways. We didn't have a reservation so we just showed up early in the morning before the restaurant opened, hoping to snag a seat. Was surprised that there was already quite a line out the door, but was able to still get a seat immediately! During late lunch, it didn't seem like the place was as busy and you could walk in just fine.

- Salt & Pepper Chicken Sandwich and French Fries - My friend said that this is the best chicken she ever had in her life, which is an insane statement. I don't know if I agree with that exactly, but the chicken was really good as it was fried to perfection and I loved the breading which was incredibly flavorful on the outside. I didn't care much for the rest of the dish as I thought the french fries were just okay, not a lot of flavor. I did appreciate the portion sizes though as it was all huge.
- Hong Kong French Toast - This was not my favorite thing. I didn't taste the salted egg yolk flavor. Also, I thought the whole thing was a bit too sweet for me as the condensed milk was extremely overpowering.

Overall, I would give 5 stars to just the chicken and 3 stars to all the rest of the food. I might come back to try the chicken in the scallion biscuit. I do have to say that when we ordered this for 2 people, I was a bit worried that it would not be enough food but it was more than enough as the portion size is pretty big.

IG: @mrtravelfoodie

After seeing so many posts about Potluck club over this past year, I've been dying to dine here for quite some time, but I could never get a reservation for prime times when I was available. I was finally able to visit on a Saturday for Brunch after over a year of waiting and this was well WORTH the wait!

Appetizers
- Karaoke Fries 
- Taro Shrimp Fritters 
Toast
- Bolo Bao Milk Toast 
- Hong Kong French Toast 
Mains
- Sunny Side Eggs over Radish cake hash 
- Potluck chow mein 
Drinks
- Coffee milk tea 

Yes, I starred every dish that we ordered because everything was amazing! From the INCREDIBLE service when you walk in, where they treat you like family, to the delicious food, I was blown away by how amazing this experience was! I know that people think once you get hyped up or blasted all over social media, restaurant's lose the foundation of what made them popular. However, I'm here to say that Potluck Club lives up to every expectation you may have and more! They strive to keep Chinatown alive for the future generation with a twist on being Asian American, which is how so many of us feel!

I would highly suggest making a reservation asap and visit Potluck Club to enjoy one of my favorite dining experiences in NYC! For more great eats, locally and abroad, follow to stay updated on my next food adventures! 

Rating 9.7/10

Such a hearty, authentic meal! Trendy interior but still had that family style feel. Oyster mushroom potstickers were spicy but flavorful with a satisfying crisp. XO fried rice was so comforting, topped with corn chunks and Chinese sausage. The salt and pepper chicken was definitely the star of the show - deceptively juicy paired with a rich plum jam. Fun drinks menu with Asian beers.

Make a reservation on resy! It takes about 1-2 weeks for reservation. We didn't try walk in.

We were served right on our reservation dot, also left right on the dot for time as well. Depending on your party size, there is a time limit.

The food was great! We ordered yellowtail which was really good. The oyster rice noodle was mainly rice noodle. The XO fried rice was good, my friend really liked it. The shrimp with walnut was really good, reminds me of chinese wedding food.

Ordered a variety of items from the brunch menu. To start, the coffee milk tea is amazing! I mean, what a brilliant idea mixing two great drinks - milk tea and coffee..

The bolo Bao French toast was my favorite thing we ordered. Basically a thick crispy piece of toast filled with sweet custardy goodness. So decadent and rich, thank goodness we shared it amongst 3 people!

The karaoke fries were just okay (which I found surprising because I love fries in general). I thought these had way too much sauce on them (although the sauce did taste quite good - kind of like a red curry sauce) - but the amount of sauce just made the whole thing come together as a soup rather than crispy fries. 

The shrimp fritters were pretty good - crispy, packed with shrimp, and went quite well with the cilantro aioli. I didnt love the Hong Kong French toast. The texture of the bread was almost too chewy/sticky, just too rich overall and not my favorite. 

The pork belly sandwich was also pretty good. Not much more than egg and pork belly - could've used something more to give it a little bit of crunch but at least the pork belly was well cooked and flavored.

Overall a great place to try for some unique twists and tastes.

Chinese inspired brunch! That salted egg yolk toast should be crown the Golden Toast 

The food came out so quickly, service was on point and the decor was so cute. Worth checking this out!
A wonderful experience, the food, service and ambiance all awesome. Highly recommended!

This was such a fun brunch experience. It is a tight menu full of stars. We really loved the chow mein -- which we also saw every other table order. We also shared the hong kong french toast and the pork sandwhich. It was probably a bit too much food for two people but we just wanted to try so many things! 

We also loved the decor. It felt hip and young, but also rooted in chinese culture. My boyfriend kept talking about how the fake vending machine items reminded him of his childhood.

Looking forward to coming back!

Came here for dinner on a weekday evening and it was quite busy. The restaurant has quite large serving sizes, which is nice, but is on the more expensive side for Chinese fusion. We ordered the: 

- Oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (9/10) - Chewy with a great flavor

- Tiger shrimp w/ candied walnuts (9/10) - Absolutely loved the crisp that the walnuts gave and the shrimp was breaded well without being soggy 

- Crispy drunken chicken w/ shrimp chips (6/10) - Not sure what part was crisp here since it seemed more like poached chicken with shallots. I really liked the shrimp chips portion of this dish though. 

I really liked the decor of the restaurant, as you can tell that they put in a lot of effort with the movie signs, entrance hut, and the vending machine with the fortune cookies at the bottom. They have a separate brunch menu that is offered only on weekends.

Such a delicious restaurant with decor wildly reminiscent of my childhood favorites. You'll find 90s themed Asian inspiration spread throughout the restaurant. At the very back of the restaurant, it'll also be hard to not notice the chefs woking them woks #fire.

The menu was pricy, but definitely worth trying IMO. I had the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles with steak and the wok hei on the rice noodles was impressive. There was a nice amount of char and a generous amount of steak. I always love ordering rice noodle dishes because it's hard to not get it to stick when you're cooking it at home haha. 

We also ordered salt and pepper chicken with biscuits, the pork + chive as well as the woodear potstickers and braised short ribs. The dumplings were good, but hard to beat nearby competition in chinatown. The biscuits were not too dense, buttery, and an absolute must try with the jam. 

There is an innovative beer selection that covers unique asian flavors (tentatively expanding). Although the dishes are not extraordinarily unique, the flair and execution makes coming here a nice treat.

Better than expected. To me it was Chinese food with American fusion. The oyster mushroom noodle with beef was most memorable. The fried chicken was OK, I think Popeyes is tastier, not much Asian about it. Nice ambiance, 1989s with Bruce Lee. Portions could be larger. Service was friendly with a smile. Hip place with above average food.

I walked in without a reservation. I sat by the chef's table, basically looking into the kitchen, and it was fun to watch the chef preparing the food.
everything I ordered was good. My favorite is fried chicken. I see why everybody hype about it. 
The service was very good. They constantly come over asked if we need anything.

We had a dinner reservation on a weekday evening - this place gets pretty busy so definitely try to snag a reservation, but they do have bar seating for walk-ins. As other reviews have mentioned, they outdid themselves with the decor, and I especially liked the movie wall by the entrance.

We ordered the braised short ribs and eggplant. They were both good and the ribs were tender, but I almost found them to be too salty/savory, though it may just be because I've gotten too used to Korean braised ribs, which are usually sweet (my friend was a huge fan of both dishes!). I wish we tried one of their chicken dishes, but the ribs and eggplant were just the right amount of food for two people! As an aside, their white rice was also weirdly really good - I'm not a rice connoisseur by any means but for some reason I was a huge fan.

Overall this place is good and worth checking out, but it's not mind-blowing and it's definitely on the pricer side.
Came here expecting really great food based on reviews and I was super disappointed. Everything was pretty bland and nothing special about the place. Service was decent. Wouldn't come back here

Service very friendly!! Very nice for a small party. Bathroom is unisex be careful going into them. Must knock on the doors beforehand. Otherwise very nice. The food is delicious fried chicken and special made salads is sweet and savory to the taste.

The menu at Cantonese-American restaurant Potluck Club is small, but don't let it fool ya - there's umami in every dish!
- While the menu is inspired by NYC's Chinatown, there's twists on the classics.
- Their brunch and dinner menus are pretty different (we got dinner!), so you gotta go at least twice! 
- Starters are ~$17, mains are ~$25-35, and veggies are ~$19. We ordered 12 dishes for 6 people and had ab one dish's worth of leftovers.
- service was attentive & helpful, and I loved the laid-back easter egg vibes of the restaurant

Here's what we got! (I normally rank dishes, but every. single. dish. here was good!!!)
- endive salad - super fresh & great light contrast to the other dishes, especially with the dragonfruit and orange
- oyster mushroom rice roll noodles (steak added) - SO BANGER. Umami AF & I actually yenainhaled this
- crispy drunken chicken w/ shrimp chips - love the contrasts in textures, and we wanted to drink the ginger scallion sauce fr
- braised short ribs - suuuuuper melt in your mouth beef 
- drinksies: the landlady (added alc but probs better without alc), old man chiu, ribena spritz, arnie wong (tasted like herbal tea in the BEST WAY!
- & the other dishes we got that were also great: yellowfin tuna crudo, jellyfish tiger salad, berkshire pork & chive potstickers, woodear & oyster mushroom potstickers, xo fried rice, tiger shrimp w/ candied walnuts, spicy eggplant, curry tofu

Absolute smash. One of the best potstickers I've had in my life. Overall the food was incredible & the restaurant had a great vibe. Highly recommend if you're in LES. We walked in without a reservation at 6pm on a Thursday and were seated by 7pm

Very good food and relaxing ambiance. The fried rice is super delicious and highly recommended. It is a must try. The service excellent and really enjoyed having a dinner with friends and family. If you don't have reservation, it might be a wait. Enjoy.

We came here for my sister's birthday and I already love the vibes! It's very 80s hong kong with old movies on the walls and giant posters and they even give you a postcard with some hong kong celebrities when they were younger like Jackie Chan and Jet Li! 

The drinks were delicious however they weren't strong - we got the arnie wong and the ribena spritz - while tasty, do not expect to get tipsy on them 

My favorite dishes were the short ribs , perfectly tender and flavorful and the tiger shrimp was very flavorful as well with a nice kick to it! 

I didn't get a picture of it but we also ordered the XO fried rice which is also one of my favorites as well!

I'd highly recommend this spot! I am looking forward to trying their brunch next time!

Wow. The pork potstickers are perfectly pan-fried and the chili oil is unparalleled in terms of the balance of chili flavor, MSG, and more subtle  flavors. The scallion biscuits are light and savory, and the salt and pepper chicken is ultra crispy and juicy, and tastes perfect smothered in leftover chili oil from the dumplings. Their XO fried rice was a delicious version of the classic shrimp and lap cheong fried rice, with the perfect saltiness from the sauce and a lovely sweetness from the sausage and corn. The drunken chicken has pleasantly crisp skin and a deliciously floral, aromatic, herbaceous dip. Top to bottom, an amazing meal, with fantastic selection of East Asian beers to top it all off.

The ambiance here is unreal! The restaurant is so nicely decorated and with old school movies and cartoons. I loved the bolo bao toast and the milk tea butter. We also got the turnip cake hash and I personally love turnip cake and this one was crispy and thick. The pork belly egg sandwich was ok - the pork belly was flavorful and not too heavy. For my drink, I got the coffee and tea mixed drink and it comes in the cutest to go cup with the cartoons on it. I am definitely coming back to try some of their other brunch items!

** BRUNCH REVIEW ONLY ** 

Came here for brunch and overall it was a solid, but not amazing experience. Potluck Club has been on my "must try" list for a while now and as a Cantonese-American I've been so curious at where Cantonese dishes could go. Walked in with a resy at 11am and was seated promptly. Was packed by the time we left.

At any rate, we basically ordered all the items on the brunch menu EXCEPT for the fried chicken sandwich. We did opt to add the same fried chicken to the salad.

Anyways, to go down the list of food items:

Endive Salad - Pretty refreshing/nice, albeit maybe a lil overly dressed salad. My wife really enjoy it. The fried chicken was good lol.

Taro shrimp fritters - My fav savory item on the menu! Really crispy. Like the sauce. Like how compact they make the paste they deep fry it in.

Karaoke fries - I do like HK curry, but I actually think the fries they use for this gets soggy wayyyy too quickly. Felt kinda like I was eating mush after only a few minutes. Maybe should've asked the sauce on the side if possible, idk. A miss for me and the other people I ate with.

Bolo Bao Milk Toast & Hong Kong French Toast - Both were really tasty and probably my fav dishes from the brunch menu. The bolo bao is for the "not too sweet" people and the Hong Style French toast are for the sweet tooths. Do I think it's way better than other HK style toast (or any Asian toast)? Probably not too much, but I do like this one!

Pork Belly cha siu sandwich - This was solid. I do just like eating cha siu with rice, but this was yummy although a lil boring for me.

Radish cake hash - This was just... reallyyy basic and felt a bit uninspiring. There were maybe only 4 or 5 pieces of radish cake too which seemed pretty sparse. Closest thing to me just saying "you can REALLY easily something similar to this at home." Would not order.

Chow mein - I liked this. Pretty typical though I feel although their chili oil was good. Rest of my group thought it was a bit too salty. I enjoyed it but I'm a salt fiend.

Service was fine although they did forget an order until we asked them near the end of the meal. Overall I have really mixed feelings because I was really hyped up for this and although some items were good, no dish is making me want to come back. There are a few items I still want to try for the dinner menu so I plan on giving it another shot, but for now I feel like Potluck Club is "just okay."

No. Just a straight no for the terrible appetizers.  

The jellyfish tasted so salty like our marinated salty white radish.  It reminded me of the first time I had a really salty Nathan's hot dog on a hot summer day in Coney Island.  Who would have thought bad food can bring out bad food memories?  They added soy sauce on top of the already salted jelly fish to accompany it. I can't!! Also, no Cantonese/HK dish has tuna on runny eggs. It tasted ok but...meh! 

This was my birthday dinner.  I was so appalled.  We told the waitress and she brought it back to the kitchen, and then brought out the same dish that tasted as salty as the last. It was bad.  I wonder if the chef even tastes the dish himself?  The other food also tastes average. 

This place seems to be created for white people. It's got the nice decoration and vibe (and you can see through a hole in front of the bathroom a picture of Jackie Chen - the place is definitely decorated with care).  There are certainly a great element of the Cantonese cultural showcases.  But the food? I can't approve. 

It's pricey and it tastes...below average for the portion.  You are really paying for a nice sit down but to a Chinese born Cantonese, I am so disappointed on the food.

Tempted by its nostalgic HK style decors, I finally made a resy to Potluck Club. The restaurant was packed with big groups on a Saturday night. It got really noisy and I had to yell to be heard

BTW don't skip out on the cute vending machine, where you can grab some free fortune cookies before you leave!

＊Salt & Pepper Chicken w. Scallion Biscuits
I like savory pastries, so I was excited to spot scallion biscuits on their menu. Unpopular opinion: I wished they served more scallion biscuits and fewer fried chicken. 

It was basically an Asian-fusionized chicken waffles. The salt and pepper seasoning was invisible. It tasted straight up like a regular fried chicken to me. The chili-plum jam was an interesting pairing with either the chicken or the biscuit. 

＊Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles
It was delicious, but was it mind-blowingly deliciously? No. The asparagus was a great veggie accompaniment to the dish, and I liked the bounciness of the oyster mushroom. Yet I found the rice roll noodles a bit salty after few more bites. It also lacked the wok hei I expected.

HOWEVER, despite my slight disappointment on their food, I might still come back. I watched interviews of their owners and I admire wholeheartedly their concepts and missions to promote Cantonese food. The restaurant is more than just for Instagram.

Potluck Club NYC offers delightful vibes and decor, such as a vending machine with asian-themed goodies, that set the stage for a memorable dining experience. However, the excitement was overshadowed by overly salty dishes. The XO fried rice and oyster mushroom rice roll noodles, while promising, suffered from excessive saltiness. On a positive note, the themed bathroom added charm. Service was friendly. Potluck Club is otherwise a very trendy asian-american establishment that shines.

2/5 for food but 4/5 for ambiance. Overall cute spot for a date or friends but don't expect to be wowed by the food. The food was unfortunately so, so salty & incredibly lackluster, with the major flavor profiles just being overpowering saltiness. The ambiance really made up for an otherwise pretty bad meal. They played R&B music (which I enjoyed) and had an old school parlor theme. The service was nice. I really wanted to try the brunch menu as well, but after the food experience I wouldn't return.

-Jellyfish salad (5/10); I thought it was really good for the first bite. Definitely the most unique jellyfish salad I had & it was well seasoned. However, the more you ate it, the saltier it got. By the end it was making our tongues sore because of how salty it was. 

-yellowfin tuna crudo (3/10); I think a lot of people enjoy the crudo sauce, but this was not for me and my boyfriend's taste. We thought it was lackluster and missed the mark in terms of what flavor profile they were going for (zesty, creamy, salty?). Also it was $17 (I think?) for 6 small pieces so definitely expensive for what you got. 

-salt & pepper fried chicken w/ scallion biscuit (7/10); I wish they gave more biscuits for the amount of chicken there was. the biscuits were really good, they looked really dry but were really moist and buttery when you bit into it. The chicken was also good, but when you run out of biscuit to pair with the chicken it ultimately ends up very salty (even with the plum sauce to try to balance it out). 

-XO fried rice (7/10); this was better than your average fried rice. the grain of rice was really nice (it had a good bite to it). the portion was generous and the fried onion/garlic crisps and Chinese sausage complimented each other. I think this was also the only dish that we didn't think was extremely salty by the end of it. 

My boyfriend also got one of the $8 drinks with strawberry, salted plum and sprite. he didn't think it was worth the price

10/10 traditional Chinese dishes with an elevated twist 

Great spot for dinner with your friends and family or even a fun date spot. The interior is well done with an intentional Asian aesthetic. The wait is about 30 mins normally if you don't have a res. 

The menu is limited but thoughtful and everything is delicious. (Pro tip, ask for the house made chili sauce)
- the squid salad is a must appetizer, the sauce is kicking with flavor and the texture is like a hard solid jello
- For mains you can't go wrong... unless you don't get the fried chicken and biscuits. This is a must get dish and is what they're known for. Although not a traditional Chinese dish per se, it slapped so good. The sauce was a little sweet and the biscuits were so buttery flakey. This dish is pretty large 
- Another must try is the mushroom rice rolls. The texture of the rice rolls is soooo good and a little chewy. The mushroom were thinly sliced and pretty chewy 
- The short ribs was mad tender. It was so yummy and the carrots were delicious covered in the sauce 
- For the veggies we got peapod stems which you can never go wrong with. These were not the best I've had tbh I normally like them more garically. I think you could skip it though
kind of small but decent food very young crowd the short ribs were tasty and the portions were good

I went here for their brunch and was surprised at how long the line is.  It was super crowded by the door and we were told to wait 30-45 minutes.  The menu was small and we opted for the toast and drinks. For a $15 toast it was quite pricy and not much different from other Cha Chan Tangs in the area. I don't think I will be back for lunch but might try their dinner menu.

Serving up Cantonese-American food in a hip space Potluck Club is a very good restaurant in Chinatown.

The restaurant itself is very cool with various murals on the wall and a video wall of some of the best Hong Kong movies playing on repeat. The space is broken up with tables for two up front, a bar area in the middle, and larger party tables in the back.

Food wise everything we had was very good. Appetizers are easily shareable and main dishes will easily fill you up. On our visit we had;

Yellowfin Tuna Crudo - I'm not big on tuna crudo but my partner really enjoyed it.

Berkshire Pork & Chive Potstickers - excellent, favorite dish of the meal.

Braised Short Ribs - the short ribs were tender and juicy, very good.

Oyster Mushroom Rice Roll Noodles - I've never had noodles rolled up in this style and I loved them. I added steak as well, which was a nice portion of cut up hanger steak that paired with the noodles well.

Service was casual yet on point and pro. If you're in Chinatown this is a spot to hit.

Went here this past month-- Had the chicken with scallion biscuits and the xo fried rice. I would say food is solid, nothing mindblowing but the portions for price are very decent for new york. 

Main selling point is the ambiance! The decorations are so cute and they even have a vending machine with secret fortune cookies to take on your way out along with nostalgic japanese fruit gummies when you get the check. The staff were such gems, super sweet and quick with taking our orders + getting food to us even on a Friday night. 

Would definitely say it's a great place to go with a group of friends to try and share dishes. The ambiance + good company make the dining experience :)

Potluck foods are very flavorful, at one point it's quite salty for some of them. When the Oyster Mushroom rice roll noodles served on our table, we couldn't help but rave about how amazing they smell! The rice roll was packed in flavor and had a soft, firm texture. Some bites from the endive salad was good assuming the blood orange to be sour but it's sweet (found out it's different type of orange), this type of salad or other fancy salad always have a slight bitter aftertaste. The eggplant we had is the savory type comparing to the regular fish sauce eggplant. All the drinks are awesome!

(Overall: D) - While the service was good, and the staff are knowledgable and attentive, with a cozy atmosphere and contemporary decorations, I felt that the food was just poorly executed from a multitude of views. When the menu is countably small, you would think that each dish would be prepared flawlessly. However, each of them each have technical errors that are problematic and does not pay the underlying representation of Cantonese food with respect.

(Rice Noodle Rolls: F) - While I was drawn to the restaurant by this intriguing dish, unfortunately almost every single component of this dish has some technical flaw. First, as a person who enjoys saline forward food, I found this dish to be incredibly oversalted in a beyond unpleasant way -- this issue is further exacesterbated by the mushrooms absorbing the sauce to its entirety. The steak is also borderline overcooked as the wok hay was not present so the steak was not cooked fast enough to be tender and tastes boiled. Finally, asparagus was a poor substitute for a more traditional chinese broccoli as its delicateness does not allow to give any reprieve from the salt overload.

(Snow Pea Shoots: D) - This is a traditional take on pea shoots, with the addition of oyster sauce, which unfortuately I felt added to the saline foreward profile of this restaurant's entire menu. 


(Old Man Chiu Cocktail: C) - This is a pleasant yuzu soda spiked with yuzu soda. The drink is on the sweet side and the the presentation is on the simple side, but I wish I could taste the sake a bit more as it was undetectable.

(Tiger Shrimp: F) - Unfortunately, this dish felt overpriced and not cohesive. At $31, I was expecting more than 6 shrimp, a few pieces of candied walnut that was surprisingly bland, and roasted romanesco. The biggest issue of this dish is that it felt like the components were prepared separately and not combined together in any way and the flavors dont necessarily build off of each other so it is just poorly executed.

--
