Presentation: E
Price: -1
Atmosphere: +1
Service: +1
Menu: -1
Overall: -1 D

Insta/Beli: @amei_eats

I had finished a mid-day trip to the MET with some coworkers and three of us were headed down to Chinatown for some post-museum boba. One of my coworkers suggested we grab food as well and since it was so early, we decided to try our luck at Potluck Club. It was about 5:48pm, so about 18 minutes since their opening and we managed to snag three seats at the chef's bar. Score. 

We ordered a few items to share: 
- XO Fried Rice with house xo, shrimp, chinese sausage, and corn 
- Tiger shrimp with candied walnuts - calabrian chili aioli 
- Salt & Pepper Chicken with scallion biscuits and chili-plum jam 
- Spicy Eggplant with garlic, oyster sauce 

All the food was really good, but I absolutely loved the tiger shrimp with the calabrian chili aioli. It gave the shrimp a bit of a kick, instead of the standard sweetness of the walnut shrimp you get at Cantonese restaurants. The spicy eggplant wasn't super spicy and was so flavorful and unami. 

I had a Ribena Spritz, which has yuzu sake, ribena, and seltzer. It was so yummy and I would gladly drink this again. 

Service was attentive and friendly. I know some people don't love that it's essentially expensive Cantonese food, but I love the idea of an elevated, creative twist version of my people's food.

By far my favorite restaurant for brunch and dinner ! I highly recommend this spot and coming with a group of friends so you can order a bunch of things from the menu or order everything from their menu like I did! The staff is so attentive and friendly towards their customers! I enjoy everything on their menu and will continue to be coming back for brunch and dinner!

Great atmosphere and service. Really enjoyed the Berkshire pork potstickers. The Berkshire pork added a really memorable flavour I have never had before. The oyster mushroom rice rolls with steak had great wok-hei, textures and taste. The salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits were good as well but I enjoyed the other two items more.

Hidden on a busy street in Chinatown, Potluck Club doesn't look like much on the outside, but once you walk in, it transforms. Potluck Club becomes modern and sleek and features films and Chinese designs throughout. My friend and I shared the Hong Kong French Toast and Pork Belly Cha Siu & Egg Sandwich. Although the toast wasn't too special, the sandwich tasted great and was balanced. These were part of their brunch menu, but I do want to come back to try their other items!

This is a trendy spot in Chinatown, so I would definitely get a reservation beforehand or you'd be unlikely to get a seat. The inside is so cool, they did a great job with the decor and all the themed props.

We tried the jellyfish salad, the salt and pepper chicken, the shrimp and walnuts, and the greens. The jellyfish salad was good, but it didn't really stand out to me. It came as an appetizer and it was good size for sharing. The shrimp and walnuts were good, but felt very overpriced for what you get. There were maybe 6 shrimps, so everyone could only get one basically. For a family style establishment, I would expect the portion sizes to lean a bit on the larger size, so I was surprised to see how small this plate was. For almost $30, I would not order it again. 

The salt and pepper chicken was amazing though. It came in a few large pieces and was super crispy and seasoned. The biscuits were also delicious, especially with their homemade chilli jam. It was such a unique flavor combination, but worked so well together. 

The side dishes, the veggies and the rice roll noodles were also solid and helped fill us up. 

The service was amazing and very attentive. We tried to order our own individual dishes at first, but our waitress heavily recommended us to do family style and it was definitely the right choice. 

Overall, I would come back for the salt and pepper chicken. It is in the pricey side, but the trendy atmosphere makes it a cool place to hang out.

Thought this was going to be an ordinary Asian restaurant but it exceeded my expectations! We try walk in right when they opened on a Saturday and thankfully they had spots. We were seated in the tall top seats towards the back of the restaurant where you get to watch the chefs cook. 

What we ordered: 
-jellyfish tiger salad: this has to be my favorite jellyfish dish! I love the aroma of the cilantro and how refreshing the whole dish is. Also I've only had jellyfish in small pieces but they have the jellyfish in the form of noodles and it was really fun to eat
-oyster mushroom rice roll noodles: I've only had rice rolls from the food carts that are in plain form and they add some sort of sauce to it. But this stored fried rice roll dish is so good! The rice rolls are perfectly textured and taste so good with the mushroom and other veggies 
-salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits: this plate is huge! Chicken pieces were perfectly fried, juicy, and tender. Biscuits tasted like regular biscuits. Definitely a very filling dish 
-jade scorpion beer: "green peppercorn Pilsner"  and you really do taste the peppercorn which is so interesting

Highly recommend everyone to check this place out! Amazing food, great service, and insane interior design.

I was excited to try Potluck Club after seeing the hype on social media but was left disappointed.

I felt that all of the dishes lacked depth in flavor and tried to compensate with salt. 
Rice noodles: especially salty that I had trouble eating more than a few bites. 
Braised short rib: the meat was tender but again, lots of soy sauce but no other flavor 
Fried chicken with biscuits: chicken was juicy with some hints of five spice, biscuits were just ok
The plain white rice was also on the mushier side. 

Overall the presentation and decor is nice but the meal was not anything remarkable.
Delicious food, good, efficient, friendly service. We had some kind of noodle dish with Mushrooms and added steak pieces, can recommend this one.

I absolutely love this place! Came here with my sister and cousin about 6 months ago and ordered practically everything on the menu. The staff were super friendly and gave their recommendations. There was no wrong choice. It's on the pricier end, but I think it's worth it for the ambiance and experience. Stepping into the place definitely gave me big Hong Kong vibes.

I came here with my parents early Sunday afternoon, and we just walked in with no wait. The inside is really well-decored and nicely themed! Service is also super friendly; they were super happy to answer any questions, quick with the water refills, and generally made the experience great. 

We started with the endive salad, which was actually great. Super crisp, not overly bitter, and the dressing they use is nice and vinegary, which really excited the palette. The potluck chow mein was just ok. The chow mein was a bit too crumbly for me and definitely too salty. The steak pieces were tender and good though! We also got the radish cake hash, which was a unique take on the traditional radish cake. It was nice and crispy, but I honestly didn't like it as much as the pre-packaged radish cakes that you can get from the grocery store.

Overall, a vibey spot that is fun to check out with friends, but wouldn't go out of the way for the food!

I was excited to try potluck club but completely blown away by the whole experience. The oyster mushroom rice roll noodles ( add steak) were amazing 

We loved the chili oil so much that we bought a jar to take home! can't wait to go back
Support your locals and also order everything on the menu. Potluck has efreshing salads with vibrant flavor. The salt and pepper chicken and biscuits are phenomenal. Stop in and see for yourself!

Hard to get a reservation but we went right when they opened and were able to get a spot later that night at 7pm for 7 people. Such a great modernized approach to Cantonese cuisine. Probably most ideal for small groups up to 5-6 , gives a chance to try range of dishes. The sauce on the oyster mushroom rice noodle rolls was particularly divine and short rib was also lovely.

The service was great. My party sat near the bar and the bartender was nice and took pictures for us. The food was delicious, but be warned, this is a fusion restaurant. The ambiance was casual. My party was there to celebrate a birthday while I saw other parties on dinner dates. The price was a little high for me, but I do understand if you eat in Manhattan, you will pay more. The drink menu was interesting as I ordered green peppercorn pilsner. I really loved the pork dumpling, especially the spicy sauce it came with. $14 was a little pricey for 5 pieces but tasted good. $5 for a bowl of white rice. Wasn't a fan of the scallion biscuits, but the chicken was great. I say, head out to this trendy spot and enjoy the drink menu.

This is my second time here and I wasn't blown away the first time but this time around I thought every dish was amazing. 
Highly recommend the oyster mushroom rice rolls and the chicken and biscuits.

A friend took us here for dinner and it did not disappoint! The food was so flavorful and tasted authentic. Our favorites were the Tiger Prawns with Walnuts and the Pork Dumplings but wverything we got was honestly superb. I also loved the beer I got (Jade Scorpion), it was a Green Peppercorn Pilsner which I've never had before and it brought out the flavors in the dishes. Can't wait to come back and try the other dishes!

I really enjoyed the atmosphere and the 90s Hong Kong cinema vibes that was all around the restaurant.  I think it would've been even better if they played 90s Hong Kong music, but the crowd that they are trying to attract may not know anything about that so probably couldn't relate.  The service was great, I have no complaints. They were all polite and very professional. 
The food was a bit salty for our family. The menu wasn't very extensive and we had 6 people in our party so we were able to try quite a bit of the dishes.  This is the first time we've ever had Cantonese style with American twist and honestly while I think it's very creative, it really wasn't for us.  The popular Cantonese dishes that they took to make the twist were already very tasty and really didn't need any change.  I'll just name one dish and that was the beef chow fun using rolls of noodles and mushrooms, we also add the beef but we really liked how beef chow fun is traditionally made. Noodles were too thick and the dish lacked the "wok hay" in our opinion. Original is best.  The salt and pepper chicken was pretty good but the drunkin chicken was too dry.  For the price, both of the chicken dishes gave a decent portion so that was a plus! We were happy to stop by since we didn't know what to expect but since we are out of towners, most likely won't be back. Everything else was great!

Did walk in for brunch and had no wait. It is a limited menu and not same as dinner menu. The endive salad was the best thing with the dragonfruit and Cara Cara oranges. Taro shrimp croquettes were crispy and yummy. The portions are large so we regret ordering so much. We also had beef chow mein, pork "Bao" sandwich (regular burger buns) and the milk French toast. The French toast was just ok. Would not get that again. Beef chow mein was good and large. Definitely shareable

The interior of this place is so cute! We had a reservation so were seated immediately. There were lots of people waiting so I do recommend booking a reservation if you can. The endive salad was one of my favorite dishes, it was so light and refreshing. The flavors of the different ingredients all went together so well and it was the perfect starter. We also got the pork potstickers which were also delicious, and I loved the chili oil. The salt and pepper chicken was AMAZING--the chicken was so tender and juicy and the skin was crispy. It was seasoned perfectly. The scallion biscuits came with a chili jam and that was a heavenly combination. At the end, they give you fruit gummy candies! And there's an aesthetic vending machine in the wall that you can get fortune cookies from. Overall a fun restaurant with delicious food!

Sorry, grandma, but next time I need fried chicken Pot luck Club is where I am going. 

It was jumping, it was bustling, and the open kitchen was churning out heat under the pressure. A beautiful space with memorable eats.

I started with some veggie potstickers. Amazing. Simple as that. Coated with some chili oil and the edges crisped to perfection. The inside stuffed full of mushroom and veggies sending waves of umami packed flavor to your taste buds. I was solo and ate every single one. I would do it again, too. 

Now, the chicken, biscuit, and sauce. Sometimes you just look at a piece of fried chicken and know it is special. This salt and pepper chicken aces the eye test. It is beautiful. Stunning. But, it gets even better' you can eat it, too! Let me tell you, remember that first crunch when you bite it. Savor it. It is euphoric. The crunch from the skin could be heard by the deaf. The flavor is so rich. Salty, peppery, and the chicken is not dry. Add a little bit of that sweet and savory jam... boom, magic. And the biscuits are the perfect accompaniment. Flaky, salty, and the scallion is so amazing. 

Let me tell you, go to pot luck club. Eat the chicken. Do not stop. Enjoy it. Savor every bite of that salty skin. Scoop every drip of that jam onto your biscuit or chicken. Order an extra biscuit. Enjoy your company. This place is ELITE. Like, real deal.

I came again here last night for dinner and the food is still delicious. It is always great when you return to a place and it is consistent. We ordered different items but it was still delicious so I am glad we went back. We ordered the potstickers both pork and the mushrooms. These dumplings were delicious and the filling was great. The sauce the dumplings were in was so good; the right balance of spicy and flavor. I wish they sold the sauce the dumplings were in because I would gladly buy it. We ordered the short rib and the noodles. The short rib was very flavorful and soft. The portion was enough for both of us.I have never had rice roll noodles but it was delicious and the texture was perfect. I was concerned with that type of noodle it would be too doughy but it was cooked perfectly. The food was flavorful and hot. The employees ate really nice and helpful. I do want to come back for brunch. This place is amazing and I'm glad we waited for them to open. The place is great for all occasions and ages.

Vibe: 8/10
Service: 6.5/10
Value: 4.5/10

potluck chow mein: 9/10
pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich w. french fries: 8/10

Overall: 7.2/10 (3.6/5)

[To clarify our review system: 
10 = we'll never have anything else as good as this in our lives (we use 10 very sparingly!) 
9 = extraordinary
8 = great
7 = above average
6 = average 
Anything below 6 is being critical]

My husband and I grew up in LA and SF Chinatown, so we were excited to check out Potluck Club. We ordered their milk tea, bolo bao toast, fried chicken sandwich with fries, and chow mein with hanger steak. 

Bolo bao toast: 3.8 out of 5. We thoroughly enjoyed the crust and the paste inside it but not something we would pay $15 for in the future. 

Fried chicken sandwich: 4.5 out of 5. The chicken was divine. All the flavors came together. The fries also tasted like McDonalds, haha! A must get! 

Chow mein with hanger steak: 4 out of 5. The hanger steak and flavor of the chow mein was delicious. It was an elevated dish that still kept Cantonese roots. 

Milk tea: 2 out of 5. Just go to a mom and pop shop in Chinatown instead. We didn't taste the condense milk that milk tea traditionally has.

I came back to dinner and my review still holds but had to update anyway. Usually, Americanized/modernized Asian food gets a bad rep but Potluck club does it SO well. 

We came with a big group so I think we tried 90% of the entire dinner menu. My favorite dishes for dinner were the pork potstickers, spicy eggplant, salt & pepper chicken and the rice rolls with mushrooms and add the steak. 

Their service is also great, the servers are so friendly and chill. 

So worth the hype, highly recommend trying both dinner & weekend brunch!!!

Zed says really really nice host/bus boy waiter Cory and really good food. Our kids loved the endive salad with dragonfruit and pistachios as well as the fried chicken. The noodles are very unique - rolled up like delicious pillows of dough that melt in your mouth! Unique, subtle flavors that please kids and adults!

I love the design and decorations here! We came for brunch with a large group so I got to try several items. 

The Hong Kong French test with salted egg was excellent - id recommend this as a shared plate as it may be too sweet for one person to eat. A few bites are perfect though! 

Get the taro shrimp fritters!! They are fried perfectly crisp and the taro is subtle yet unmistakeable. The aioli was a refreshing sauce to balance out the fritter. 

The endive salad was fresh but did not particularly stand out to me. Still, it was a light, refreshing shareable. 

I ordered the salt and pepper fried chicken sandwich. My only gripe was that I wish there was more sauce!! 

Overall had a lovely brunch with excellent service, and I am intrigued to try their dinner menu!
Overall food was flavorful, but extremely salty and over seasoned. I loved the decor of the place. Bathrooms were very clean. Service was great. Drinks were great.

Good throwback interior with amazing service. Portion sizes are huge, but I HIGHLY recommend the Oyster Mushroom Rice Rolls as the marinate & texture = perfect and the Berkshire Pork & Chive Potstickers. 

The Salt & Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits is also huge portion size but make sure to use the sauce with it as that's what makes the huge difference!

The curry tofu was good but I didn't find anything too special about this. Once again, huge portion size. 

I recommend getting couple dishes and sharing with your table! 

I will definitely come back for the oyster mushroom rice rolls.

Love the indoor decoration of this place. Brings you lots of HK-ese memories. The menu is very simple, bringing the most common Cantonese foods. The milk iced tea and coffee milk iced tea were a bit bland, not much milk taste to it. I would suggest they use stronger tea to make it. It's definitely a nice experience but I also won't come back for it, since I thought the food was meh, at least compared to the Chinatown ones. Customer service is good.
I was finally able to get a reservation at Potluck Club! Everything was yummy - the Endive Salad and Fried Chicken were my favorite items.

I came here for dinner on a Wednesday night. It can be tough to get a reservation as they only open a limited number of tables and only offer dates two weeks in advance. 

The restaurant has distinctive decor. It's a mix between a traditional dim sum restaurant, a diner, and a trendy hot spot. 

To drink, I had the ribena spritz. It arrived beautifully at the table with a warm pink color melting into deep purple. It was fruity, fizzy, and perfectly sweet. 

To start, we shared the woodear and oyster mushroom potstickers. These were delicious. A crunchy shell was topped with a savory chili crisp. It was quite flavorful, especially with the scallions and sweet soy sauce. 

For my main, I had the vegetarian xo fried rice. This was tasty and a generous portion size, but not particularly noteworthy. 

I also tried the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles. I loved the tender, savory mushrooms. The rice rolls were decently firm, but could've had a bit more flavor. 

The scallion biscuits and chili plum jam that accompanied the salt and pepper chicken were an unexpected treat. The jam was rich and thick, and paired well with all of the dishes. 

Service was fast and even though the restaurant was crowded, it was easy to carry a conversation.

Came here with three friends on a Thursday night. A+ service and ambiance. The waitress was so kind and friendly and very proactive in getting us drinks and providing us recommendations and tips for ordering. You can just tell by the photos that the food was extremely tasty. I think the table rated the Salt & Pepper Fried Chicken and the Pork & Chive Potstickers as our top picks. Really fun and welcoming ambiance - definitely worth checking out.

This place was amazing. The food is so cool and yummy. Our server was amazing and so kind. They did an amazing job creating such a cool ambiance at the Potluck Club. Definitely want to come back next time and try the lunch. Very impressed with this place!
Great food, great drinks, great vibes! Highly recommended if you're down in LES. Can get busy so book ahead.

A modern take on Chinese food. You have to order the salt and pepper fried chicken and the oyster mushroom rice noodle. 

It has a hip vibe, service was good as well. Nothing bad to say only wish the menu was a little bigger, but that's it!
Ordered a toast, cha siu burger and shrimp fritter. The fritter, toast and fries that came with the burger were over fried and unpleasant to consume.

Applause to Cory and team!

What a great place to come and hang out, eat some abc fusion food, and be a part of the evolving culture that the team behind Potluck Club is creating.

The food was nothing short of spectacular. My party that came to dine with me has been in the restaurant business for a while and they were overly joyed with the food. Their favorite was the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. The chili plum jam was phenomenal! Everything here maybe on your typical canto menu but nothing is typical about the new modern flavor combinations.

Highly recommend being part of Chinatown history!
This places ambiance and food were amazing!! Our waitress was so nice too!! Definitely would come back to try even more dishes!

Friend took me here for brunch- the place opens at 11am, and there were already 5 groups anxiously waiting to get in.

Cute decor- step in and the first thing you'll see is the host stand that looks like a telephone booth. Check out the interior, I really loved all the playful details. The decor includes a lot of references to classic kungfu movies, so lots of fun things to look at.

Brunch menu was fascinating- classic brunch dishes but with an Asian twist. For example, the Hong Kong French Toast that my friend and I shared was made with thick milk toast and featured a salted egg yolk lava, with condensed milk. The sweet/salty flavor was so delicious!

We each decided to get breakfast sandwiches- salt and pepper chicken for my friend, and pork belly char shiu for me. Both came with a generous portion of fries. 

Pretty good brunch, but I'm laser focused on trying out dinner!
Been here twice; both times the food was bursting with flavor and personality and the aesthetic/ambiance was hip throwback.
Amazing brunch experience. Salt and pepper chicken sandwich, hanger steak chow mein, Hong Kong French toast, and coffee milk tea were all great. Staff are extremely friendly and helpful

I am typically not a person to eat this type of cuisine but boy was I shocked and in a pleasant way. I throughly enjoyed this meal. The tiger shrimp and candied walnuts were so good, I wanted to order a second round. The potstickers were delicious, their chili crisp added the perfect kick, but I really liked that it was easily removable for when the spice became too much.

I had a great experience. Partially bc the staff was so nice and helpful. It's a shared plates kind of place. I think it was the perfect amount of food for a greedy party of 3. We ordered 4 main items and two appetizers. We spent about $70 a piece after tip. And there was some food left to take home. 

We tried the fried chicken with biscuits, potstickers, endive salad, walnut shrimp, oyster mushroom noodles, & xo fried rice. I enjoyed everything. The potstickers were one of my favorites. The endive salad was also really delicious and refreshing. Some of the main dishes lacked in flavor to ME but I still enjoyed my meal. 

It's a great place to go with a group and try a bunch of different things.

Delicious food! Highly recommend for a date night or night out with friends! The yellowfin tuna crudo is my favorite, Woodear potstickers are also so good! My favorite entree is the oyster mushroom noodles with the steak.

Love this place!

First of all, the food is so darn good! As someone who grew up eating Cantonese food, I was pretty skeptical of this modernized take on HK food, but it was great! It was a good mix of nostalgia with a glimmer of growing up Asian American. 

Secondly, the interior is so cute! It had a lot of TVB shows and a fake vending machine of common Cantonese household goods like Tiger Balm. Don't forget to grab the fortune cookies from the slot! 

Highly recommend this place and would definitely go back again!!
Food is American canto, best thing is the noodles, apps were fine and drinks were fine. Service is fast and ambiance is casual. Good amount of bdays here

This place is absolutely worth the hype. It's pretty busy so definitely make a reservation in advance. I came for brunch because of the famous toasts. The lychee mimosa and ribena spritz ($15 each) were both refreshing and sweet. For food, we had the Hong Kong French toast ($15), salt & pepper chicken sandwich ($21), and pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich ($21), and everything was absolutely phenomenal. The chicken was perfectly fried and crispy and the cha siu was juicy and tender.

Cute dinner and brunch spot very a cool vibe! They serve modern Cantonese food and it's reflected in the retro decor. It's perfect! The food is also amazing.

It's very easy to make a reservation online too, so would definitely recommend for brunch or popular dinner times.

For the brunch we got the karaoke fries, Hong Kong French toast, the radish hash cake with sunny side up eggs. Everything was delicious! The fries came with fish balls and a flavorful thick curry sauce. The French toast was covered in condensed milk and had a salted egg yolk lava inside, it was the perfect sweet breakfast dish. The radish cake was nice and crispy and went well with the runny eggs. 

For drinks we got the landlady, a non alcoholic drink with fresh strawberries, salted plum and sprite. Really enjoyed it, it was refreshing and not overly sweet. 

Everything was a 10/10! Would come back for brunch again or to check out dinner

The only problem I have with this restaurant is that it is not open Mondays or Tuesdays. I wish I could have this for dinner every night. 
We visited this restaurant for a late night dinner and it did not disappoint. The aesthetic is exceptional and that is nothing compared to the taste and presentation of the food. 
We enjoyed the XO Fried Rice (necessary to add the tea egg), Berkshire pork and chive potstickers, salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits and the endive salad. 
The winner was the endive salad. Each ingredient on its own was good but the combination is a salad I would never think would taste as good as it did. GET THE SALAD!

This is a place I've always wanted to try and I'm glad I did but I can't say I'll be back. Think Hong Kong diner meets American diner but with a more expensive menu. My tastebuds weren't wowed and neither was my wallet.

Potluck club is a new hip Canto restaurant that seemed to be small tapas style dishes. 

We got, for appetizers, the endive salad and the pork and chive dumplings. And for mains, the tiger shrimp, salt and pepper chicken with biscuits, oyster mushroom rice roll noodles, and eggplant with 1 white rice. This was just enough food for 6 people with low/moderate appetite.

The highlights for me were the dumplings and the eggplant. The dumplings were super thick and had a respectable portion of meat. The chili sauce it came with was also so good, not too spicy, savory and a little sweet. The eggplant was also very flavorful and a good amount.

The downsides I will say, for some of the prices, the portions were pretty small, especially the tiger shrimp (6 pieces) for $32. The chicken was likewise, with 6 pieces and 3 biscuits, half per person. Additionally, the biscuits themselves were undercooked--a bit doughy. Aside from that, the food was pretty tasty overall.

Would definitely recommend if you're looking for a fancier small-dish hip place that serves quality food with quality service! But if you're looking for value, I'd suggest going elsewhere.

Service: 5/5, our server was very attentive. Timely asked us for drink orders and food. Quickly refilled our water once it was finished. 

Had an odd run in with the host. He asked if we wanted to sit in the back or front. I saw that the only table left in the front was by the host check in station, so I said back. And then he goes "actually we have one table left and it's reserved for friends of the owners". I thought this was an odd statement to make. Also, why ask me if I want to sit in the back if there was no space? I saw a bar and chefs counter top, so I asked about those spots and he said that was available so we were able to sit there. 

The food: 
Tuna crudo - 5/5, This was an amazing way to start off the meal. Great bite. I loved the spice, fish was fresh, combo with the citrus vinaigrette was perfect. $17

Pork and chive Dumplings - 5/5, loved the spice and the amount of sauce/green onion. Perfect level of crispiness. $14

Xo fried rice - 3.5/5, love the addition of corn which is not common for canto food. Loved that spin. But where was the Xo flavor and spice? It was very bland. $25

Crispy drunken chicken - 2/5, the flavors were good, ginger scallion sauce was good, the chicken itself was so dry. It was just chicken breast that was extremely overcooked. And there was no crisp factor. The skin was soft and the onions on top lost its crisp from the sauce. $30

I saw some reviews about the price. I thought the prices and portions were acceptable. Although it's pricier than a typical canto place, I think the vibes of the place and inflation justify the prices.

Although the chicken was dry. And I was slightly disappointed at the end of my meal. I think it was just an off day probably. 

Learning about what this restaurant does for the community would make me go back again. I appreciate when people recognize their history. Hopefully round 2 chicken will be better!

Cool restaurant, feels like something you can only have in NYC. Food was amazing (pictures definitely don't do it justice), very flavorful, great texture, fresh, interesting combinations,... good price as well and friendly staff, even so they were really busy. Must go there again when I am in town!

The food is definitely good with uncomplicated yet familiar flavors. The fried rice reminds me of my grandma and mom's cooking, but I can make that now as well. I like to add lop yook, lop Cheurg and spam to mine, and the flavors come out very similar to the xo fried rice. I like the offering of non alcoholic drinks, we ordered the land lady. I think it could have used a bit of fizz to make it perfect. We also got the pot stickers and they were good for sure, with Berkshire pork being a premium pork, it can warrant the price. The flavor is similar to lo gan ma chili oil but a tad spicier. It was good nonetheless but also felt uncomplicated. The snow pea shoots are a classic and this was great as well. The fried chicken at this point u was too full to properly taste this, but the next day it was still tasty. It was overall a good experience but we felt a bit rushed. We had a reservation at 5:30pm on Wednesday for two people and by 6:40 we were told that our table is reserved and so we were asked to move to another table. It's a bit weird that they didn't just seat us at that empty table to begin with so we wouldn't need to move. This would have been fine but then by about 7pm or so we were actually being rushed out of there. 

So this place is good however with uncomplicated flavors like I said, but ultimately we felt rushed and couldn't properly enjoy our time there. We ordered quite a bit of food with two people as well, so we obviously wanted to fully experience this place. 

Nonetheless I will still try their other venture Phoenix palace when I get a chance. The food was ultimately good and the aesthetic was cute.

Very funky and lively vibe 
I love the vintage movie posters decor they have
The brunch menu wasn't my favorite ~ left feeling very heavy 
I heard the dinner menu is better so I'll have to go back for that

Food is yummy and ambience is so nice! Everyone was so attentive - they sat us at the bar since we walked in without a reservation, but it was still a fun dinner with friends. It was cool to see the bartender make drinks. 

Next time we come we will try some drinks! They looked really good.

absolutely amazing service and every detailed piece in the decorations had so much thought to it. the atmosphere and ambiance was such a vibe! the food was also soooooooo good and the asian fusion menus were very unique.

I went for brunch with friends and we loved this place. Every time we took a bite of food, we'd immediately stop talking and lose our trains of thought to express "oh shit this is good". 
Favorites:
- bolo bao milk toast (with milk tea butter) - crunchy top, chewy, soft, not too sweet, soo yummy
- potluck chow mein - the steak was tender and yummy and the pan-fried noodles were the perfect mix of crispy and chewy

We split 3 mains and a toast between 4 people and we all left full. The salt and pepper chicken sandwich + pork belly cha siu sandwich were also a delight. The coffee milk tea was ok - more watery than I'd like. Service was fast and our waiter was super attentive and nice!
Run to Potluck club. What a place !!! Incredible food and fun vibe. Chicken with scallion biscuit was WOW WOW. Friends who grew up in Chinatown opened.

We had a great date night here. 

The interior is so cute. I love all the decorations and felt they really added to the experience. 

We ordered the pork and chive potstickers, the XO fried rice, and the chicken with scallion biscuits. 

The pot stickers had very crispy wrappers with a juicy pork filling. The order came with 5 which is always annoying for sharing. 

If you get the fried rice, I would highly recommend getting the egg on top. The egg was cooked perfectly with a beautiful jammy center and the marinade penetrated all the way through to the yolk. The rice itself was very fun to eat with a variety of textures in every bite- bouncy bites of shrimp, soft rice, crispy fried shallots and sweet pops of corn. It was balanced and flavorful. 

The chicken was very crispy and the biscuits had a beautiful soft interior. The chili jam is quite sweet but a great addition to the dish, adding a huge amount of flavor to the already texturally interesting food. 

The portions are quite large, and for two people we ended up taking some leftovers home. All of the staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable about the menu. I recommend making a reservation but it seems that it is very possible to get in on a walk in, especially on a weeknight.

Wow wow wow! I was easily able to make a Sunday brunch reservation a couple days in advance and we came at 11 AM, right when they open. The brunch menu is a little more limited, but it gives you the opportunity to try one of everything if you have enough people! Here's what we ordered: 

- Endive salad with salt and pepper chicken: I've never had endives before so wasn't quite sure what to expect, but this was probably the best salad I've had. Seems a little strange to come to a Chinese restaurant and order a salad, but please trust me and just do it. Definitely splurge on the salt and pepper chicken!
- Pork belly cha siu and egg sandwich with french fries: The sandwich is served on a super soft sesame bun and the pork belly had the perfect ratio of meat to fat. There were a little too many fries for my liking, but overall very solid sandwich. 
- Bolo bao milk toast with milk tea butter: Not super sweet, and a nice dessert to share with the table! The milk tea butter has a surprising amount of milk tea flavor to it. Bolo bao is a childhood favorite, so I loved this fusion!

This was one of the best meals I've had since moving and I definitely want to come back for dinner to try some of their other dishes (eying that salt and pepper chicken). The down-to-earth customer service was just the cherry on top. Already looking forward to my next visit!

Cantonese meets American in a great space. 

The ambience was really impressive. The space is very nicely decorated. It gives you European or Hong Kong vibes. Beautiful. 

The service was very professional and friendly. Much needed dish explanations were given in a very respectful and warm manner. 

The food was exactly what they advertise. Cantonese meets American. 
Taro shrimp fritters where a bit too solid for my liking. But if you think about it they align w American cuisine - something like fish croquettes. 
The pork belly needed bao bun and not brioche bread. Fries were classic American I guess hmmm. 
Cho mein with steak: interesting combo. Steak well prepared. Cho mein traditional. We liked the chili sauce bc it was mild! 

Overall great vibes and service. I would choose this place for the overall experience and not the food only. 

Bonus that the menu was small. Lazy menu reader here
Amazing food! We went on Sunday where they only offered the brunch menu.  We tried different items and they were all excellent! I would be back to try their regular menu.

I'm usually highly suspicious of hype but this spot is worth it! Not too overpriced for upscale Chinese and as a big mala fan I really enjoyed the mala-flavored drinks (although the flavor didn't come through super strong, it's a nice pitch). No trouble getting seats on a Wednesday for two without a reservation (we snagged a table but the bar was open as well) and service was speedy and great. Note, this is NOT the same as Joy Love Club on the west side of Manhattan, where I nearly accidentally dragged us.

Every dish was too salty. Even acknowledging that the dishes were meant to be paired with beer / drinks, some were way too salty to finish (I had potstickers, oyster mushroom rice roll noodles, and crispy drunken chicken). 

Very cool ambiance, but the food was very disappointing given great reviews here.

Most everything we had was incredible. I almost worried my friend and I were too zealous and ordered too much for 2 people but I'm glad we tried the dishes we did. Potluck Club's spin on Cantonese classics is done exceptionally well. I ranked my favorites below but I consider dishes 1-3 to be really close in standings, and I would def order them again next time.

1) Favorite dish as a whole has to be the braised short rib. Extremely tender and fall off the bone. The sauce was mouthwatering; tangy and paired well with the ribs. 

2) Close behind is the Chicken with scallion biscuits, because the chili oil jam was so unique - the smoky spicy flavor from the chili oil tempers the sweetness from the jam well. That chili jam was hands down my favorite thing I ate the whole meal. If they sold this in bulk I would buy 5 jars, no kidding lol. The chicken was crisp and juicy. The scallion biscuits were okay - they were fluffy but when I ate them together with the chicken it left my mouth feeling a little parched for sauce or water

3) Next would be the oyster mushroom rice rolls. The rice noodles had great chew and the mushrooms were super flavorful. Dish as a whole had that great wok char flavor we all know and love.

4) We also ordered the shrimp with candied walnuts. The walnuts were sweet, smoky and addicting. Shrimp was a little heavy on the mayo-based sauce. Dish as a whole was decent but compared to the other dishes, my friend and I probably could have skipped this one as we were bursting at the seams and in pain by the end of dinner. #noragrets but probably won't get this next time 

--

Decor was a lot of fun to explore, the Asian cinema theme really transports you back in time. Stick your hand in the vending machine for a secret stash of fortune cookies!
Worth the hype! Seriously amazing modern take on Cantonese classics. The fried chicken and walnut shrimp are a must get! I'll definitely be back to try brunch.

Such a great experience, we made a reservation for 7 and ordered everything on the menu except for the bolo bao so the waiter gave it to us for free just to try. Our favorite was definitely the karaoke fries, the chow mein was also perfectly crispy. I also really liked the chicken sandwich, the bread was chewy and the chicken was juicy. The bolo bao was pretty dry but the taro butter was a good pairing. Everything was also very fairly priced. We wouldn't get the radish cake again because the portion was small but we also liked the pork belly sandwich (chicken was better) and shrimp fritters.

We had a fabulous experience here and happy to find the food was worth the hype! We came on a Sunday as walk ins. I would recommend coming right when they open. The service was great and they gave solid recommendations. Our absolute favorites were the pork and chive potstickers and endive salad. They were so well executed and I would come back just for these two dishes. We also ordered the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, oyster mushroom rice rolls + add on steak, tiger shrimp, and spicy eggplant. All were excellent. 

It's super viby and a good place to go with friends or a date. I'm excited to come back again and happy to support an Asian owned modern Cantonese restaurant.

Damn! This place is good! Food is good, flavor is so good! Sauce is good! Service is very attentive. Nice and clean inside. Sometimes there could be a line, but if you get there early enough, you'll be good to go to get a seat. Reserve if you have a bigger party.

Food was SOOOO good. Just look at my pics I took! I will come back 100%!

Loved the old hk setting/ambiance in the restaurant!! It really set the mood, and I love when restaurants have unique setups. The food was phenomenal and very well portioned. The beef rice rolls were a unique dish that I really enjoyed, and the eggplant was flavourful as well. My friend who doesn't like eggplant said she liked this dish a lot! The chicken was my favourite dish, as it was super well seasoned and the sauce that came with it was great. The scallion biscuits were so good and fluffy, such a unique taste on biscuits and chicken.

Overall the restaurant has a cool vibe. Very nostalgic. They have old movie posters around and snacks for display. The service was good. Food was okay I wasn't blown away by anything really. We had the pan fried law bac go with bacon, salad and eggs, the pork burger with egg and the lava toast. Everything had good flavor but like I said I wasn't blown away by it, I felt it was overhyped for what it was.

I was finally able to visit Potluck Club after hearing so much about them for 2 years now. We ate here for brunch this past weekend and had a fun time.

The VIBES are excellent. I actually deeply adore the old HK cinema theme and their dedication to Shaolin Popey in particular, one of my old comfort movies that you can see featured on the entirety of one of the walls and on their postcards. The marquee lighting, the posters, the little ticket booth all really add to the vibes, 10/10.
+ I liked the cheeky nods to memes on the marquee sign. During our visit, it read "In the clurb, we all fam"  
- I will say the music is a little loud, so it may not be the best place for intimate conversation, at least during brunch.

Our FOOD was mostly really good!
+ Endive salad with dragonfruit was refreshing and novel while still tasting familiar, it's not as big of a leap outside of your comfort zone as you might think! We got ours with the salt + pepper chicken, which was solid
+ Hong Kong French toast was smaller than I wished but was also solid, there was the fun salted egg yolk lava oozing out when you cut into it
+ Pork belly cha siu & egg sandwich was fine, I think the pork belly was really good but it didn't quite feel right in a sandwich, something about the texture and flavor with the bread didn't feel quite balanced, even though it all tasted good
- Chow mein was good but I did find the pieces of steak to be oddly gamey tasting and a bit tough, it was pretty weird and by the end of the meal we had several pieces of steak left behind on the plate despite there not being a super generous amount to begin with
+ I also got The Landlady mocktail, which was SUPER tasty, as I think the salted plum really and Sprite really heightened the naturally punchy flavors of strawberry, this was super delicious.

Our service was also great, we were well taken care of, they provided my baby with a high chair and offered to bring her a plate (we declined because I didn't want any shattered plates haha) but she had a great time minus the loud music.

All in all, I think this is a really fun spot for a meal. The menu is fairly short, which makes deliberating a fairly painless process, but the atmosphere and the takes on the menu items really are a lot of fun.

So happy I finally got to try their brunch menu. It was worth the trip out from Brooklyn on a Saturday afternoon. The service is excellent, the food is delicious, and the decor is amazing. I will be back for more!!

I've been here for brunch and dinner and def preferred dinner over brunch. I think the food is good but very expensive.

Dinner dishes:
Salt & pepper chicken w scallion biscuit: I thought this was really good. Chicken was not dry and skin was nice and crispy. It tasted more like regular fried chicken, the classic Chinese salt and pepper flavor was not that strong. I also liked the biscuit, it was very soft, more soft than fluffy, but my friend did not seem to care for it. What really set it off for me was the chili jam - a mix of sweet and spicy. I spread that sh*t on everything lol

Oyster mushroom rice roll: this was definitely everyone's favorite. I wished there was more mushroom in the dish. I usually love the flat rice noodle stir fry and this was very similar, and you could taste the "wok hay". We didn't add the steak but I'm sure that would be really good too.

Snow pea leaves: obviously overcooked, and also seemed to have an added flavor, not sure what it was, so it's not quite the same as classic snow pea leaves. Thought this was the worst

Braised short rib: wasn't as soft/"fall off the bone" as I was expecting. It was good, but it was not amazing by any means, and def not worth the price. I also didn't like the potatoes at all. 

When I came for brunch, I remember not liking any of the dishes aside from the endive salad, and I'm pretty sure we ordered everything on the brunch menu that day. The salad was delicious and refreshing. It's also available for dinner so I'd recommend that. The other dishes were either disappointing, or way too salty (the noodle dish).

Service was pretty good and very attentive during dinner. Our waters were never empty. After my previous disappointing brunch experience, I'm glad I came back to try the dinner, but I don't think I'd come back unless someone visiting really wanted to try it.

nice ambiance and friendly staff! the food was super yummy and as the name suggests, to be enjoyed potluck style. a flavorful and filling meal, would recommend for a big group of friends so that you can try more of the foods!

The fried chicken and scallion biscuits are the star for sure. The chicken tastes a bit like the best karaage you'll ever have, with nice light breading and moist, flavorful dark meat inside. The biscuits are buttery and flaky. 

We also tried the pork and chive dumplings which were good but not extraordinary. 

I am curious about their brunch menu as well as the mushroom rice rolls, so a return visit is in order. Reservations are recommended, but were easy to make online.

We love coming to the Potluck Club. The whole places looks like a fun place to be. We enjoy the secret peephole with a picture of Jackie Chan as well as the postcards and the fortune cookie dispenser. We always get the chicken dish!

This place is super cute! Great ambiance, fast and nice waiters. We ordered a variety of dishes to try, and one thing to note the more you order, the probably better considering some of the dishes are quite small. We ordered drinks, I believe it was lunar, and it was super tasty and added to the meal. 
We ordered: 
- braised short rib (pricey and took longer to come out, but pretty good!)
- Jellyfish tiger salad (I love jellyfish and especially when served canto style, but this was disappointing. super small and lacked jellyfish, for the price point I was expecting more) 
- spicy eggplant (pretty good as well, nice twist to canto dishes, would order again) 
- rice rolls (for this being a staple in cantonese food, these were average and honestly could of lived without). 
The food overall had great taste, but given the price point and sizes, some weren't doing it for me. I hope to visit again one day and try out other things from their menu.

I was able to get a reservation for an early dinner on Friday. When I arrived the restaurant wasn't that busy, but it got busier as the night went on. The restaurant is spacious. The service was friendly and the food came quickly. We ordered the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, braised short ribs, snow pea shoots, and the oyster mushroom rice roll noodles. I enjoyed the chicken, short ribs, and the rice roll noodles. The flavor on those 3 items were great, but the portion size is definitely small. The snow pea shoots had a unique flavor to them that I did not love.

Visited on Saturday for brunch with reservations. We were quickly seated and were able to order fast. We got booth seats which were very cozy. Even their bathrooms were super interested, they're like pods lol. We got one of everything on the brunch menu and almost everything was great. 

The service was great. The owners/co-owners were very friendly and the service was great. We had 7 people, and the shrimp fritter was 3 per order and they were kind enough to give us 4 in one of them. Super kind and amazing service!

My favorite was definitely  the karaoke fries. I believe it was curry and gravy fries. Which was really good. The radish cake hash was kind of bland. I kind of expected it to taste like what we would get from radish cake at dimsum. I was also not a huge fan of the eggplant (endive salad). But to each their own. You might like it if you're a huge eggplant fan. But other than that everything else from the bolo bao milk toast to the pork belly cha siu Sandi was delicious! 


TLDR - great service, amazing karaoke fries, cozy atmosphere.

I'm sorry, I don't get the hype. Maybe it's because I grew up eating these dishes, but I had some beef with these dishes.
The tuna crudo came with tiny slices of tuna that were overpowered by the sauce, which just tasted like vinegar. The rice roll noodles were rolled up (?) and rubbery, which is how they taste when I buy them prepackaged from an Asian grocery. For nice, tender, and thin rice roll noodles, go to West Rice Roll King in Chinatown or Joe's Steamed Rice Rolls on the UWS. Thankfully, the mushrooms in this dish were well seasoned and the sauce was pretty good.
Spicy eggplant was good, nothing to complain about but also nothing to write home about. Fried rice was also pretty decent, could have been more flavorful.
Our servers were super attentive and we didn't feel rushed even towards the end of service. The interior was decorated like a vintage Chinese movie theater, which was super cute.

I love *everything* about Potluck Club. I have yet to have a bad or disappointing meal here - and every time I go, I'm already looking forward to coming back. I've been here for brunch and dinner, and both are excellent (although I'm a bit biased towards dinner).

For brunch, don't miss out on the bolo bao milk toast. And if you haven't experienced their salt & pepper chicken for dinner, get the sandwich. 

For dinner, honestly...everything is *chef's kiss*. Must gets for me are their salt & pepper chicken w/ scallion biscuit, xo fried rice, and pork & chive potstickers. But you really can't go wrong here - and you'll find yourself coming back anyway to order what you missed out on!

Great vibes as well and super friendly service. It's a pretty big place but their tables book up fast, so snag a reservation if you can!

This place is so amazing. The interior blew me away. Super trendy, giving retro china vibes throughout the restaurant. We came around little earlier around 5:30 and it was pretty empty but filled up as the night went on.

We got the endive salad, salt and pepper chicken, pork and chive potstickers and jellyfish salad. I did not know I could love a salad as much as I did this. Super flavorful and well balanced and it had such a satisfying crisp to it. The highlight for me was the potstickers. If you open the biscuit in half, spread the jam and create a sandwich with the chicken you get the perfect bite. The jam was sweet which paired well with the saltiness from the chicken. 

TIP: there's a secret peep hole by the bathroom on the opposite side of the stalls..fun little Easter egg they put In there

gosh here i am again! 5 months ago, we came for brunch and this week we came back for dinner. still one of my favorite spots to come to. we had the salt and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits, the potstickers, and the rice roll noodles. we stuck to the same drinks we got last time because we can't find it anywhere else and it was the perfect beverage to go with our meal. blown away by the friendly service and vibey music. both of those truly elevate the enjoyment of eating here with your friends. everyone feels happy to be there. if you asked me if i prefer the brunch or dinner menu, i do think i prefer the brunch menu because of the noodles.
Excellent Food and incredible service.  We have had Sunday brunch here several times and it is always fantastic!!!!
Service and ambiance is great. But food is mid. Rice roll dish was too salty. Food not worth the price.

Initially excited given the positive reviews on yelp and on instagram. Unfortunately, food is salty. Aside from salty food, pea shoots are too old so they end up being chewy. Not sure if that is on purpose. Don't expect Chinese food in this restaurant.

Once you walk into Potluck Club, you're taken back in time. The aesthetic is so unique and beautiful and the layout is comfortable. I ordered the Landlady (mocktail version) and loved it! The sour plum taste shone through and I was a huge fan. We also ordered the endive salad and Salt + pepper chicken w scallion biscuits to share between the two of us and it was more than enough food.
- Endive salad: 7/10. I loved the refreshing aspect of the ingredients but thought it was too small for the price and also found it to be too sour
- salt + pepper chicken w scallion biscuits: 10/10. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the breading was delicious and crispy. The scallion biscuits blew me away with how soft and savory they were without being too salty. And the chili jam that came with it was chef's kiss. A little spicy but not overwhelming 

Would recommend!

P.S. Their bathrooms are gorgeous too

Decor is super cute and fun. Service was good.

This place is a place that has a small twist to a lot of traditional dishes. I personally didn't quite enjoy the twist as much as the original. 

- salt and pepper chicken was actually really good. felt like karaage, but I would eat this again. I don't like biscuits, so I didn't like the scallion biscuits.
- tiger shrimp with candied walnuts were almost there, but didn't quite hit it. Not too bad.
- snow pea shoots also weren't bad, but not quite as good as the regular ones.

Fun fusion brunch! The decor had a cool concept of popular movies and the food was certainly yum. Lowkey, these French fries were PERFECT as well. The reinvented pork belly breakfast sandwich I'll be thinking about for awhile too

One of the OG's in the trendy Chinese fusion scene and must visit for those who love Hong Kong flavors and street culture. Came for brunch since all dinner resys were booked (validating my friends' opinions that dinner is the better menu), but still had a lovely time. The interior is a fun mix of old and new, with a cozy nostalgia of night market aesthetic and dim sum parlor during HK's heyday. The marquee over the bar sends positive vibes over the diners, while a trip to the bathrooms feels like you might be entering an escape pod that rockets you into a future in which everything is right again. No really, they're pretty cool and you should check it out. 

Weekday brunch is a pretty easy feat to carry out, and it was nice not to have to weave our way through too many people in the restaurant. We got to pick seats at the kitchen counter in the back, which is an entertaining spot to watch dishes getting prepped and sent out. The only downsides are low-backed stools and getting food envy whenever something comes out that you didn't order. 

You have to start with the HK milk tea or coffee milk tea, which in true Chinese fashion, can be customized to sweetness level. I wasn't really a fan of the Taro Shrimp Fritters, but the Pork Belly Cha Siu breakfast sandwich and HK French Toast were delightful. The sandwich works particularly well with the milk bread buns which really transport your taste buds to Chinese bakeries. The cha siu itself is actually fairly light, chewy as cha siu should be but still tender. It comes with a heaping side of fries which are crispy but oversalted. The Radish Cakes were the star of the eggs and hash, but the bacon was overcooked and the eggs were just alright. Would have preferred just a side of radish cakes dim sum style. 

Service was so pleasant, from our hostess to our primary server, to other staff who checked in to make sure we were enjoying our time and kept our water carafe full. Overall, lots of wins but also some misses which will probably keep me from coming back for brunch, but worth a try for anyone who finds themselves in the area - and I might see you back for dinner!

I liked this place a lot! It's a trendy modern Cantonese American restaurant. We liked the Hong Kong milk tea, karaoke fries which came with curry sauce and fish balls (an interesting Chinese take on fries!), cha siu bun with fries, and French toast! Service was great too!

From the cool ambience, fast service, and delicious menu items - Potluck club is definitely worth the hype. 

I have not tried everything off the menu but if I had to guess... all dishes are probably delicious.

We ordered the beef with rice cakes, along with the  fried chicken + scallion biscuit which were both stars. The short rib dish was solid but not as memorable as the others. 

I cannot wait to come back for brunch to try new dishes. So excited to visit this spot again.

Awesome interior! So beautiful, popping with color, but not too bright or overwhelming. The staff were super friendly and accommodating and sat us right away when we arrived.

4 people for 4 dishes--

Spicy eggplant-- great spicy vegetable dish. Lots of green onions to add a little crunch. Great dish cooked well and seasoned great.

Tiger prawns-- these were also spicy! Didn't realize they would be, but pleasantly surprised to have a nice kick which paired nicely with the sweet candied walnuts.

Salt and Pepper Chicken with Scallion Biscuits-- the star of this meal for me. The chicken was fried/cooked beautifully!! Super super juicy and the salt/pepper was not overpowering at all and it paired perfectly with the jam. The scallion biscuits were also wonderful and the jam on these was great too!!

We also got the rice noodles which were the close second best dish. Also seasoned and sauced BEAUTIFULLY and cooked perfectly. They were served in such perfect small sizes too.

Potluck club is GREAT! Another must visit spot once you snag a res. We will be back :)

Such a fun spot for elevated Chinese food! The ambience is excellent and so creatively decorated. Food is excellent and there's a fun twist on every dish. The service was attentive and so warm, and though my friend and I were there for awhile, we never felt rushed. 

It was a bit pricey but worth it for the service and elevated dishes. 

We shared the snow pea shoots, pork dumplings, and pepper chicken with scallion biscuits. 

Pork dumplings were very flavorful and featured lots of great textures -- maybe a smidge salty. 

The chicken and biscuits felt like a southern twist on a Taiwanese classic like peppercorn chicken. The fig jam was spicy and a nice surprise, and tasted amazing in the soft scallion biscuits. Definitely try this dish out! 

Pea shoots were a great vegetable to balance it all out, and was dressed in a yummy savory and citrusy sauce.
This evening ordered Oyster mushrooms,Rice noodle & Steak as a add on,also ordered the Pork stickersthe 11 points on a scale of deliciousness

Super famous potluck club in chinatown! 
This place is a new classic in Chinatown - I love how it both is a modern approach to chinese food but also pays homage to the history of chinatown. The place is pretty small, so be prepared to wait. 
The food was great, although some of the flavors were (intentionally) a little unique / nontraditional. 
- oyster mushroom rolls: definitely order, a favorite 
- chicken: also great, but would be open to trying something different next time 
- snow pea shoots: interesting sauce, but i liked it and would get it again. 
They also have amazing merch, peep the merch case!! Love the hat and shirt. 
I would say I like the sister restaurant Phoenix Palace a bit better, but still would come back here!

All around solid experience and meal.  My friend and I split the Salt and pepper chicken with biscuits, and mushroom potstickers.  Both excellent and makes me want to go back and try their other entrees. Sat at the bat area and service was excellent.  Will definitely come back

A lot of people have recommended this place to me, and it really didn't disappoint! Everything was truly great, from the food to the service to the overall vibe. We went for brunch and got the char siu egg sandwich and the chow mein. The chow mein was definitely better (especially the steak pieces it comes with), but the char siu was good if you're in the mood for a really hearty and fatty dish. We also got the milk tea which was served in a cute cup but other than that wasn't that unique. The servers were all super nice and attentive, and the restaurant itself was nicely decorated and very clean (the bathrooms too!). Would definitely go back to try dinner :)

Happened to find this place and boy did I make the right choice! The food was tasty! The shrimp fritters were amazing. I also tried a tea which was really strong (due to long brewing process), creamy and tasty but I can't remember the name. The bartender compared it to chai--but in my opinion, their tea was so much better. The waitress (Jenny, I think) and bartender (can't remember his name) were really nice and checked in on me frequently. The decor is really nice too! It definitely passed the vibe check! Oh, they also sell hats and shirts that look cool! Can't wait to wear my 212 Chinatown hat! Whenever you're in Chinatown check this place out!

We came here for brunch on a Saturday without a reservation. There wasn't table seating but we got to sit at the bar around the kitchen where you can look at the cooks making the food. Decor inside is beautiful. The staff were super friendly and welcoming. They checked up on us, provided recommendations, and made the dining experience pleasant. We tried both the pork belly and chicken sandwiches, the Hong Kong style French toast, and some shrimp fritters. Everything was super yummy!! The toast was a little bit too sweet for my taste. The sauce that the fritters came with was so good. We were dipping the fries in them as well. Speaking of fries, the sandwiches come with a ton of them haha and they're the crispy thin ones too. 10/10 experience and we'll be coming back to try the dinner menu. We've also tried the sister restaurant, Phoenix Palace, for dinner and it's also super delicious!

The food the people who work there and the ambience is amazing! We had a whole bunch of friends for dinner last night and they did such an amazing job with a price fix meal that included so much food and such a great variety! Our server Kim was so nice and you could really tell she loved to working there. Honestly, this food was so amazing. I am craving it the next day. Totally go check this place out. I highly recommend it.

Potluck club. If you grew up in an Asian household or have an appreciation for Cantonese movies. Walking in here felt quite nostalgic and hysterical at the same time seeing things that you remember around your house or the films played back in the early 80s, 90s, and 2000s.

The food is modern Chinese food style. The menu selection is not a lot but enough for you to browse and decide on what to have. Service was busy and attentive.

We called ahead to reserve a table for five people. I recommend calling ahead to making reservations. All payments are accepted, cash is recommended. Parking is available outside, you may have to search around and pay at a meter. 

The decorations at Potluck club were fun to look and stare at some that were displayed at a larger scale. When you see the menu, notice the names in it and you might connect it to the films you have watched.

Dare I say my favorite restaurant I've tried in New York? Every single thing on the menu is beyond tasty. The only thing I wasn't super impressed by was the fried rice, but it was still solid! Would probably try the noodles next time instead. The tiger shrimp and potstickers stole the show - followed closely by the curry tofu and the biscuits as part of the chicken and biscuits meals. The ambiance is super cute! A pretty narrow restaurant that extends way back, with a bar in the middle and in the back. Super friendly service, they accommodated an extra person at our table last minute. Will definitely come back!
Place is absolutely amazing. The food, drinks, staff, and atmosphere were all fantastic. Highly recommend the endive salad and salt & pepper chicken

Potluck Club opens for brunch on weekends, and it was on my friend's list to try. As a Cantonese person, I was very excited to try a Hong Kong cafe, especially since there aren't many in Manhattan. The three of us made reservations a couple weeks in advance right for 11 AM, right at opening time. Initially, the restaurant was pretty empty, but it quickly filled up shortly after.

We each got a drink and shared two dishes. The food came out pretty quickly and here were our thoughts:

MILK TEA - 4
The drinks came in these cute, cartoon-themed paper cups with the Potluck Club logo. My drink had two black tea bags and some milk, maybe sweetened with a bit of sugar. It was OK, and didn't add to my meal. I should have saved my money and got milk tea elsewhere.

HONG KONG FRENCH TOAST - 15
The order of french toast came with three thin, square-shaped pieces of bread, drizzled with condensed milk and topped with powdered sugar and a generous slab of butter. After cutting into it, the salted egg yolk lava flowed all over the plate. We were hoping for a thick slice of toast, so we were a bit disappointed that even with three pieces, it didn't create a thick layer. Overall, it was a good balance of sweet and salty, and the texture of the toast was nice. While we enjoyed the french toast, it wasn't anything exceptional.

POTLUCK CHOW MEIN - 24
The Potluck Chow Mein was overpriced and a complete letdown. The chow mein had an unpleasant, gritty texture, similar to butter that's melted but hasn't fully re-solidified. It left a strange aftertaste that we didn't like. On the positive note, I did like the flavor of the sauce used to stir-fry the chow mein. There was a decent amount of well-marinated hanger steak, chives, and fried garlic mixed in. Besides getting rid of the grainy aftertaste, we thought adding more toppings would enhance the dish.

Overall, Potluck Club has a very aesthetic interior with its vibrant color palette, eye-catching wall art, and open-kitchen design. It's definitely very Instagram-able, and gives a modern, high-end street food restaurant kind of vibe. Not at all a mom-and-pop. However, our food was not worth hyping up, and I probably wouldn't return.
Amazing food and service. Cute place too even the bathrooms were cool! Love the design

Everything was great
From getting a reservation at the very last minute to being accommodated with warm and sincere hospitality, to being served some of the best Cantonese/fusion food we have had in a very long time   
The decor is whimsical and fun

Went for a dinner after seeing it in a Michelin bib gourmand list.  Walk-in.  Able to be seated at a bar counter immediately. 

ambiance- trendy, newtro, feels both contemporary and retro.  

service- personable staff, relatively quick service

food-  fair to good
(1) endive salad - crunchy endives, pretty appearance, with generous/excess sauce, could have used more fruits (sprinkles) but overall good portion (shared between two and had leftover to take to-go). 
(2) Fried tiger shrimp - the plate looked small but the tiger shrimps are individually huge,  have great tangly chewiness.  Mayo sauce is a bit overpowering.  Appreciated the candied walnut. Overall enjoyed it as someone that likes shrimps.  
(3) salt and pepper fried chicken with biscuits- compared to the first two, this was underwhelming.  Thinly (albeit cruchy) battered, chicken itself was alright.  The gochujang like sauce on the side added little to the chicken personally but enhanced the biscuits.  

Ma wan cola- fair to try, tasted like a combination of ginger ale with a slight hint of herbal medicine.  


Would consider going again if I had a guest that liked retro asian art/aesthetics and was okay with/liked fusion food.

Picture Guangdong, China in the 1900s, but replace Hong Kong with Flavortown USA, and instead of the British in control, David Chang is in a consulting role saying, "Let's make everything a little more expensive than they expect." 

Don't get me wrong. I enjoyed the vibe. They do that ironic restaurant thing where retro décor makes the place seem more modern. Service was very attentive (right down to attentively asking us to leave when our 90 minutes were up).

I enjoyed the food too, although everything tended to be on the garish side. The dumplings were drowning in chili crisp. The drunken chicken did not need to be fried and then served with a ginger/scallion sauce. The snow pea leaves were strewn with a deeply unfortunate looking garlic jizz that killed most of the freshness of the dish. Out of everything, I enjoyed the rice noodles with steak and the walnut shrimp the most. But they also tasted the closest to what you can find elsewhere in Chinatown.

I also wish there were more menu options given the communal-style format. If you have a group of six, you probably have to order every single main (unless you don't mind repeats).

I think another reviewer put it best when they said, "Would consider going again if I had a guest that liked retro asian art/aesthetics and was okay with/liked fusion food." I agree but it is a circumstance so specific that I'm not sure if it's ever going to happen.
